Written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly, the new CALPHAD engine recomputes a complete phase diagram in the browser in a fraction of a second with zero installation on the user or server side. The high speed allows new ways of interacting with phase diagrams and underlying assessments. Validation against well-established CALPHAD software shows agreement to within 0.01 K for invariant temperatures and within 1e-6 for tie-line compositions for most databases. GibbScope offers interactive CALPHAD parameter adjustments, overlays of different assessments and point-by-point misfit to experimental data, which makes the diagram a live, working object. In addition, GibbScope provides convenient access to 2745 thermodynamic databases from the SGTE collection (Hallstedt, 2025) and their live adjustment. For over 1200 of these databases, all phases are modeled in full with the current implementation.

papers.title: Bias in Method-of-Moments Heritability Estimation Under Model Misspecification
papers.abstract: Method-of-Moments (MoM) based approaches for estimation of variance components --- heritability and beyond --- are central in computational genetics due to their flexibility in addressing diverse and complex models while minimizing assumptions, and ease of computation and approximation in biobank-scale data. MoM are closely related to other important methods in this area like LD-score regression. A fundamental, highly debated question relates to the bias inherent in MoM estimates of variance components when the fitted model is misspecified: since the true underlying model is unknown, the fitted model may be missing some of the components from the true model or contain superfluous ones. We offer a general mathematical formulation of this bias and investigate its properties. This leads to novel insights about the sign and the magnitude of the bias in settings of interest and allows extensions and re-interpretation of previous MoM results in the literature. One case study we pursue is in estimating gene-environment interaction variance components (GxE). We prove that when omitting environment-specific noise components (NxE), the resulting GxE estimates are strictly upward biased, even when no true interaction exists. In another case study, we consider heritability estimation, when the genetic variance components are incorrectly partitioned (such as using a single genome-wide component instead of chromosome-specific components). We derive explicit expressions for the bias in the estimate of genome-wide heritability and its dependence on LD scores within and between components. For example, if all components have the same average LD score, the misspecified heritability estimate is still unbiased.

papers.title: A Dual-Frequency-Constrained Structure-Function Kirchhoff Model for Near-Nadir Ocean Backscatter -- Part I: Theoretical Framework
papers.abstract: Most operational near-nadir geophysical model functions (GMFs) are empirical and fitted one radar band at a time, and do not explain the difference between Ku and Ka band. This paper derives a backscatter model in which one local description of the sea surface serves both bands. The near-nadir Kirchhoff integral is written in terms of the elevation difference between two surface points separated by a horizontal lag. The surface then enters through the structure functions of that difference, and the scattering kernel selects the lags each band samples, about 2.5-1.4 cm at Ku and 1.0-0.5 cm at Ka band. Geometric optics is recovered as the quadratic, isotropic limit, without a spectral cutoff. With a logarithmic second-order structure function, one wind-dependent log-slope sets both the incidence shape and the Ku-Ka shape difference, and band transfer reduces to evaluating one curve at a second lag. Same-footprint dual-frequency radar data show that one band alone does not determine this transfer. The log-slope is the level of the short-wave saturation range and grows about as the square of the wind speed; a physical short-wave spectrum reproduces this growth but overestimates the level. Dual-frequency radars thus measure the centimetre-scale roughness level, although they do not separate a scale-dependent structure function from non-Gaussian surface statistics. A companion paper delivers and evaluates the resulting GMF, KuKa-Mod.

papers.title: Budan--Fourier theorem for circuit polynomial systems
papers.abstract: We prove a Budan--Fourier theorem for linear combinations of analytic functions whose successive Wronskians are positive: the number of zeros of $g=\sum_{k=1}^s c_kh_k$ in an interval $(a,b]$, counted with multiplicities, is bounded by the drop of the number of sign changes of the sequence of Wronskians $W(h_1,\ldots,h_{k-1},g)$ between $a$ and $b$, and the difference is even. This refines the bound $s-1$ of Koiran, Portier and Tavenas, and we show that it applies, after a suitable renumbering, to any sequence of functions satisfying Descartes' rule of signs. We then study the functions arising from polynomial systems supported on circuits, that is, systems of $n$ equations in $n$ variables with $n+2$ monomials. For these functions, we show that the Budan--Fourier bound never exceeds Descartes' bound, and we compute it at the endpoints of the interval of definition. As an application, we obtain a refinement of the optimal Descartes' rule of signs for circuits of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård: we bound the number of positive solutions whose logarithm lies in explicit polytopes, these bounds add up to at most the bound of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, and they determine the parity of the number of positive solutions.

papers.title: Graph-Guided Bayesian Factor Analysis: A Fast Integrated EFA-CFA Approach for High-Dimensional Data
papers.abstract: Factor analysis has been central to the analysis of high-dimensional biomedical data. However, existing exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis methods face several limitations: less interpretable factor findings, difficulty in identifying which variables can and cannot be represented by low-dimensional factors, challenges in estimating the covariance among factors, and maximum-likelihood fits that break down when variables outnumber subjects. We propose graph-guided Bayesian factor analysis (gg-BFA) to address these gaps. We first use a Bayesian model to explore and learn the latent graph structure, identifying which variables can and cannot be represented by low-dimensional factors and how many factors are needed. A dense-subgraph search proposes partitions of the variables into communities, each defining one factor, and a forward stepwise search compares their fractional variational posteriors and stops when the evidence lower bound first decreases. We show that this search recovers the true communities even when the number of variables grows much faster than the sample size. We then develop a confirmatory Bayesian model whose variational posterior of the covariance contracts at the parametric rate up to a logarithmic factor, yielding posterior inference for the factors and their covariance, as well as predictions of missing values. Its four members range from a community mask to several cross-loadings per variable. In five biomedical panels, the complete analysis took under ten minutes each on one GPU, and cross-loadings improved held-out covariance and the prediction of masked measurements. In TCGA Kidney, six of the first eight factors were enriched for known pathways, and 190 of the 210 factor correlations had 95% credible intervals excluding zero. Overall, gg-BFA is computationally fast and provides interpretable factor analysis findings and reliable inference results.

papers.title: Learning Global Equilibria in Non-Concave Prospect Theoretic Games
papers.abstract: Human agents in non cooperative games often exhibit non rational behaviour. Prospect theory provides a behavioural framework to capture how agents perceive gains and losses under risk, but, its incorporation into games typically leads to non concave and non convex utility functions, making equilibrium computation challenging. In such cases, it is difficult to obtain algorithms that have global convergence behaviour. This paper proposes a learning algorithm which uses minorization-maximization (MM). Under a proximal Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition on the potential function, we establish global convergence of the algorithm to a potential-maximizing Nash equilibrium. We further show how the structure of the MM minorizer can be used to enable a distributed implementation of the algorithm. With additional noise injection, the individual updates of the agents can be obscured, while still ensuring global convergence.

papers.title: FEALPy.OPT: A Multi-Backend Tensor Computing Framework for Metaheuristic Optimization on CPU and GPU Platforms
papers.abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms (MAs) are widely used to solve complex optimization problems, but their computational costs can become substantial as population size and problem dimensionality increase. This paper presents FEALPy.OPT, an open-source Python framework for metaheuristic optimization built on the FEALPy computational infrastructure. It integrates a unified optimizer abstraction with multi-backend tensor computation, supporting NumPy and PyTorch backends on CPU and GPU platforms. To evaluate its computational performance, five metaheuristic algorithms are tested on ten benchmark functions under three problem scales, with population sizes ranging from 100 to 10,000 and dimensions from 30 to 100. The results show that NumPy/CPU achieves the shortest average runtime for small-scale problems, whereas PyTorch/GPU becomes increasingly advantageous as the problem scale grows. For large-scale problems, PyTorch/GPU is approximately 9.50 times faster than PyTorch/CPU and 32.96 times faster than NumPy/CPU. These findings demonstrate the value of multi-backend and multi-platform support for improving the computational flexibility and efficiency of metaheuristic optimization.

papers.title: Effective Time Advance of Quantum Clocks under Postselection
papers.abstract: In the familiar twin paradox, the traveling twin ages less than the one who stays behind as a consequence of relativistic time dilation. Here, we show that quantum postselection can effectively reverse this outcome. Using an analytically solvable quantum clock model, we demonstrate that postselection of the center-of-mass motion produces an effective time advance through anomalous weak values, even though every individual motional branch undergoes ordinary time dilation. We extend this analysis to a weak gravitational field and show that an effective time advance can arise even for simple coherent states of the quantum clock motion. We further illustrate this effect using a hydrogen-like atom, revealing how it manifests itself in the atomic wavefunction. Our results demonstrate that quantum interference and postselection can produce an effective time advance beyond conventional relativistic time dilation.

papers.title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
papers.abstract: We prove a local cohomological bound $RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-étale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(Π):= RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_Π\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type LB representations $Π$ of $G$, obtaining $\mathrm{JL}_{\mathscr{B}}(Π)\in D^{[0,2(n-1)]}$ for each choice of $\mathscr{B}$. We also prove that for arbitrary continuous principal series $I(η)=(\mathrm{Ind}_B^Gη)^{\mathrm{cont}}$, we have $\mathrm{JL}(\mathrm{Ind}_B^Gη)\in D^{[0, n]}$, while $\mathrm{JL}_{\widehat{\mathscr{O}}}(I(η)),\mathrm{JL}_{\mathbb{B}_J}(I(η))\in D^{[0, n-1]}$.

papers.title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
papers.abstract: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $μ$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ and $μ$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2τ\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_Hμ-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2τ$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions. The absolute continuity and fibre dimension theorems extend to non-coordinate projections of products under a joint Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ on the logarithmic contraction ratios. These imply for all self-similar sets $K,L\subset\mathbb R$ satisfying this condition and $\dim_HK+\dim_HL>1+2τ$, every sum $uK+L$, $u\ne 0$, has positive length, and $\dim_H(L\cap(y-uK))=\dim_HK+\dim_HL-1$ for Leb. a.e. $y\in uK+L$. The proof combines the $L^1$ Gaussian smoothing approach used in the higher dimensional case with averaging at random stopping scales with a Brownian martingale bound using Itô calculus.

papers.title: Permutation symmetries and characteristic polynomials
papers.abstract: We compute certain multilinear functionals of permutation-invariant random matrices, following the work of Marcus and Geneson. As an application, we derive formulae for the average characteristic polynomial of the sum and the product of permutation-invariant random matrices.

papers.title: Creative Intent as an Evolving Shared State: Supporting Cross-Stage Human-AI Video Co-Creation
papers.abstract: As generative AI becomes increasingly involved in video creation, creators face challenges in expanding, translating, and negotiating creative intent across stages. We therefore view creative intent as an evolving shared state throughout human-AI co-creation. A multi-stage design was employed: semi-structured interviews with 12 creators informed 3 design goals, followed by expert co-design and the development of VideoMaker. VideoMaker organizes creation into a six-stage workflow that progressively translates creative intent. At key stages, creators negotiate with AI through the Seed Panel, explicitly confirming, revising, and updating intent. A shared AI Agent, supported by the Multi-style Script Library and Cinematic Language Knowledge Base, enables differentiated expansion of initial intent and faithful translation. A within-subjects study with 30 participants showed that VideoMaker effectively supported the expansion and cross-stage translation of creative intent, with stronger intent preservation, while negotiated boundaries between creator-confirmed intent and AI initiative remained difficult to sustain.

papers.title: Double Blind Evals: Resolving the Dual Confidentiality Dilemma in AI Safety Auditing
papers.abstract: AI safety evaluations often involve sensitive prompts and proprietary models. Evaluators want to keep their evaluation prompts secret from model owners to prevent purposeful or incidental data leakage, ensuring longer usefulness of their benchmark. Model owners in turn wish to keep their proprietary model weights and inference code within their own secure infrastructure to protect their IP. We present a way forward for "double-blind evals", which provide cryptographic guarantees that an evaluator's prompts are not shared with the model owner, while simultaneously maintaining the confidentiality of the model weights and inference code. To accomplish this, we use secure enclaves that encrypt data in RAM at the hardware level. In a world-first pilot, we test this approach by evaluating a proprietary Google DeepMind model (Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite) against a selection of the private AILuminate benchmark corpus, using an NVIDIA H100 secure enclave on Google Cloud Platform, and using OpenMined's PySyft to maintain data and model privacy. We believe this effort marks the first use of this technology to provide mutual secrecy for one organization's frontier-class proprietary model weights and another organization's closed benchmark.

papers.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis. While recent work in the visual domain has explored direct conditioning on brain activity, this approach has not yet been extended to audio diffusion models. We introduce MAAS (Multi-Area Auditory Synthesis), an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer on ROI-wise fMRI responses without first supervising a decoder to predict an external stimulus representation. MAAS uses region-specific projections and learned brain tokens to condition Stable Audio through a dedicated cross-attention pathway. On a 7T fMRI dataset, we demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines, including two-stage fMRI-to-latent conditioning, across both acoustic and semantic evaluation metrics. In addition, we introduce a fidelity metric grounded in a computational model of auditory neural processing, which allows us to quantify the contribution of individual auditory cortical regions to reconstructed audio representations.

papers.title: The Paley--Wiener excess and a local law for the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is the proof that the Paley--Wiener excess of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process almost surely equals $\lfloor \sqrt{2/β}\rfloor$ for all $β>0$. We also derive the loop equations for the resolvent of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ point process and use them to obtain accurate bounds on the moments of the associated Stieltjes transform.

papers.title: Converse Lyapunov theorem for input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems
papers.abstract: We prove converse Lyapunov theorems for input-to-state stability (ISS) of a broad class of infinite-dimensional systems applicable to evolution equations in Banach spaces, boundary control systems, and delay systems. To this end, we employ a novel method that does not require constructing auxiliary closed-loop systems. We start by showing that ISS of a control system implies uniform global asymptotic stability of the same system with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. Then, under an additional regularity requirement, we prove that an ISS Lyapunov function can be constructed. Based on our general result, we prove that for linear systems with unbounded $\infty$-admissible operators, ISS is equivalent to the existence of a Lipschitz continuous coercive ISS Lyapunov function.

papers.title: Reducing Provers in Distributed Quantum Verification
papers.abstract: In the distributed quantum Merlin-Arthur ($\mathsf{dQMA}$) model introduced by Fraigniaud, Le Gall, Nishimura, and Paz (ITCS 2021), a network of quantum computers verifies a global property with the aid of a quantum proof supplied by an untrusted prover. While the nodes are computationally unbounded, the challenge is to limit proof size and the communication required for verification. In this paper, we consider the model of Hasegawa, Kundu, and Nishimura (PODC 2024), where the proof must be unentangled across nodes, and define its extension to $k$ unentangled provers, denoted by $\mathsf{dQMAS}(k)$. In this setting, we investigate the proof size per node and the communication costs of reducing the number of provers. Our first result reduces the number of provers from $k$ to two, doubling the proof size without additional communication. Moreover, with four additional rounds, we can reduce the number of provers from $k$ to one, using at most three times the original local proof size plus a logarithmic term in the number of nodes. Finally, we establish amplification for perfectly complete protocols. In this regime, a single prover suffices with a constant-factor overhead in our reductions, yielding $\mathsf{dQMAS} = \mathsf{dQMAS}(k)$.

papers.title: Consistent Mapping for Fluid Structure Interaction with Geometrically Nonlinear Isogeometric Beams
papers.abstract: Isogeometric beam formulations provide an efficient reduced-dimensional representation of slender structures, combining accurate geometry and high-order continuity with few structural degrees of freedom. Their application to fluid--structure interaction (FSI) requires transferring motion and loads between the one-dimensional beam centerline and the surrounding fluid interface. While mapping strategies exist for conventional finite element beams, geometrically nonlinear isogeometric formulations require operators consistent with their spline-based kinematics and distinct descriptions of cross-sectional rotation. This work develops consistent beam-to-surface mappings for geometrically nonlinear isogeometric Bernoulli and Timoshenko beams in partitioned FSI. Fluid-interface points are attached to the beam in the reference configuration and reconstructed using the nonlinear kinematics of each formulation. Consistent linearization yields a configuration-dependent mapping operator whose transpose ensures work-conjugate load transfer. The formulations are verified through analytical deformation tests, convergence studies, and virtual-work checks, and evaluated in beam-based adaptations of the Mok and Turek--Hron benchmarks and the Goland wing flutter benchmark. The results confirm accurate interface reconstruction and work-conjugate load transfer under large deformations, while demonstrating the applicability of both beam formulations to coupled FSI problems.

papers.title: Harmonic origin of local symmetry breaking in PbTe revealed using machine-learned potentials
papers.abstract: We use machine-learned interatomic potentials combined with higher-order interatomic force constant models to show that finite-range polar correlations in PbTe are driven by long-range harmonic interactions rather than lattice anharmonicity. Our molecular dynamics simulations reveal a spatial polar correlation range exceeding 50 Å at low temperatures and decreasing with increasing temperature. Selective interatomic force constant mapping demonstrates that crystal anharmonicity usually associated with the formation of polar nanoregions suppresses polar correlations. Instead, long-range harmonic interactions extending to 13 Å are necessary to reproduce the spatial coherence of local dipoles. In reciprocal space, these extended harmonic interactions correspond to high curvature of the transverse optical (TO) phonon branch at the $Γ$ point. Comparison with isostructural NaCl connects these extended interactions to local underscreening of predominantly Coulombic forces. Our results provide a key microscopic description of finite-range polar correlations and a framework for understanding local symmetry breaking in centrosymmetric materials.

papers.title: Unmasking Four Knapsack Problems in the Traveling Thief Benchmark
papers.abstract: The traveling thief problem (TTP) asks a thief to choose a tour and a packing together, and the benchmark of 9,720 instances of Polyakovskiy et al. (2014) is the standard test set for comparing TTP heuristics. We show that four of these instances are not TTP instances at all. Their files give a renting rate of 0.00, so the tour has no effect on the objective and each instance reduces to a 0-1 knapsack problem. One of them belongs to the 60 categorized instances on which new methods are usually compared, and on it five of nine published methods report exactly the same value. The cause is the format of the files, which keep the renting rate with two decimals, while the rule of the generator gives a rate close to 0.003 on these instances. The same rounding may shift the rate of 949 other instances by more than 1%. Since the tour and the packing used by the generator were not published, the original rates cannot be recovered. We therefore define new rates with the same rule, applied to a fully specified reference solution that we publish, and we show with a published heuristic that the corrected instances behave as TTP instances again. We also give reference results on the corrected instances and recommendations for future studies. Finally, we present ttplib, a new open-source Python library that loads any of the 9,720 instances, including the corrected ones, without downloading the whole benchmark.

papers.title: R-Function Representation and Composition for Flexibility Analysis and Robust Design Spaces
papers.abstract: Explicit multiparametric solutions provide analytical feasibility and design-space descriptions after elimination of adjustable variables. R-functions convert these descriptions into fields whose nonnegative regions represent feasible or robust designs. The principal contribution is the analytical composition of independently derived design spaces through union, intersection with engineering restrictions, and exclusion of prohibited regions, without repeating the underlying multiparametric elimination. A support-function construction supplies the robust design fields used in this composition. A two-parameter example demonstrates how alternative configurations, a manufacturing restriction and an exclusion combine into one admissible field. The resulting representations also support geometric interrogation of external boundaries, internal interfaces and limiting uncertainty contact, illustrated by a four-parameter heat-exchanger network. Explicit MPC offers a potential further application.

papers.title: The Edge of the Warm Corona in Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.abstract: A model of warm, dissipative corona on top of an accretion disk is investigated, to explain the soft X-ray excess (SXE) emission observed in active galactic nuclei (AGN). The final ray-traced spectrum, computed through photoionization code with Comptonization, accounts for both: emitted and reflected components. As a result, the strength of the SXE depends on the radial extend of the warm corona, i.e., its outer edge. We show that the radial transition from warm corona to disk atmosphere is governed by line cooling. By moving away from a central black hole Compton cooling is gradually replaced by line cooling, and the temperature drops sharply in vertical direction at a narrow iron ionization front, where iron ions Fe \textsc{xxv}--Fe \textsc{xxvi} recombine to Fe \textsc{xvii}. Notably, this transition takes place at a particular value of internal heating $\approx 1.6 \times 10^{-23}$ erg cm$^{3}$ s$^{-1}$, regardless of the Eddington ratio. We show, that at the given metal abundance, the SXE emitting area is larger for a higher accretion rate, in agreement with recent findings in changing look AGN. The overall emission spectrum from a warm corona is featureless, and the only iron K$_α$ line comes from a reflection. The line is stronger and more gravitationally distorted for a lower accretion rate, which is a direct result of the size of the warm corona. Furthermore, by increasing the iron abundance, the iron ionization front moves closer towards black hole, and a stronger iron line complex is emitted locally.

papers.title: Investigating the timescales traced by dynamical ages in young stellar systems
papers.abstract: Stars form in clustered environments, and then the stars may congregate into star clusters. The timescale on which individual stars form is not necessarily the same as the timescale on which star clusters assemble. Therefore, developing methods to probe these different timescales is a crucial part of understanding star cluster assembly and early evolution. Dynamical ages can be constructed from the kinematics of individual stars in clusters in the solar neighborhood using Gaia data. Using a star formation simulation, we test five different dynamical age methods. We divide dynamical ages into two approaches: methods which trace the size evolution of the cluster, and methods which trace the trajectories of individual stars. We confirm that size methods cannot accurately derive ages in bound clusters whereas methods tracing individual stars can be applied to both bound and unbound systems. We find that different dynamical age methods trace different epochs of star cluster formation and assembly: The method using stars with the oldest traceback ages provides an upper limit on stellar ages and the method using the median traceback ages is the best proxy for isochronal ages. Methods which trace the size evolution of the cluster best trace the onset of cluster expansion. Our work suggests that the median traceback time of stars moving away from the cluster provides the most reliable proxy for isochronal age, and that this method can be applied to any expanding system.

papers.title: On the entire solutions of Schröder iteration functions of first and second kind
papers.abstract: Let $S_{f,n}$ and $K_{f,n}$ denote Schröder's methods of the first and second kind with given order $ n $ ($\geq 2 $) applied to an entire function $ f $. This article investigates the existence of the entire solutions $f$ whenever $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ are rational. Utilizing the Nevanlinna theory, we obtain the general form of entire solutions for such equations. It is proved that either of $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ is a non-identity rational map if and only if $f = p e^{q}$, for some polynomials $p$ and $q$. Additionally, we provide one recurrence relation of $K_{f,n}$ depending only upon $K_{f,n-1}$.

papers.title: Fairness in Explainable AI Narratives: Decomposing Social Disparities in LLM-Generated Explanations
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate technical explainable AI (XAI) artefacts such as SHAP into explanatory narratives (XAINs) for lay users. In high-risk domains, these explanations are often the main resource through which individuals can understand and contest adverse decisions. Yet LLMs are known to reproduce social bias, even from proxy variables alone, and fairness in XAINs remains unstudied. Because XAINs are bound to a ground-truth artefact, fairness concerns not only what a narrative says and how, but also whether it is equally faithful across social groups. We introduce fairness in XAINs as a new field of research and propose a framework that generates narratives under three conditions (protected attribute disclosed, withheld, or counterfactually swapped), allowing five comparisons that pinpoint the cause of disparities. We apply it to adversely classified instances from four datasets in credit scoring, education and employment, generating narratives with five LLMs, and evaluate faithfulness, feature coverage and sentiment. We find significant disparities across all datasets, metric families and models, arising in two ways. Faithfulness disparities result from feature values: LLMs make plausible but false statements, triggered by values that are unequally distributed across social groups. Feature coverage and sentiment disparities stem from the protected attribute itself: once it is disclosed, LLMs give less explanation to, or frame more negatively the narratives of, groups that have historically been discriminated against or are stereotypically associated with worse outcomes. A more faithful model removes the faithfulness disparities, and withholding protected attributes mostly removes the others, but neither suffices on its own. Fairness in XAINs should therefore be audited separately from the predictive model and its XAI artefact.

papers.title: TRACE: Adaptive Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization for Open-Ended Molecular Design
papers.abstract: Optimizing molecules under small evaluation budgets requires deciding both where in chemical space to search and which candidate within that region to evaluate. We introduce Trust Region Adaptive Chemical Exploration (TRACE), a framework for open-ended molecular Bayesian optimization (BO), where candidates are generated on demand rather than selected from a fixed library. TRACE combines an objective-free graph-perturbation mechanism with a fixed, chemistry-aware Gaussian process (GP) surrogate using fragprints, a representation combining molecular fingerprints and fragment descriptors. Rather than learning the search geometry itself, TRACE makes the scale of chemical exploration explicit through a Tanimoto-similarity threshold controlling chemical extent and a cardinality budget controlling candidate-search breadth. A simple success/failure controller expands or contracts both quantities during optimization, while the GP and acquisition function select which admissible molecules to evaluate. Across six challenging molecular optimization benchmarks under matched 1,000-evaluation budgets, TRACE achieves the strongest overall sample efficiency as measured by the best molecule found as evaluations accumulate. Crossed ablations on two objectives further show that adaptive region control contributes beyond the proposal mechanism, while its benefit depends on the proposal distribution. We further apply TRACE to the stability of iron phthalocyanine (FePc), a non-precious molecular electrocatalyst whose degradation can involve loss of the Fe center. Using a first-principles density functional theory (DFT) workflow designed for accurate energy evaluation, TRACE increases the computed thermodynamic resistance to Fe dissolution from 0.42 to 2.59 eV over 80 designed evaluations.

papers.title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
papers.abstract: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial. We construct a polynomial that does not lie in the kernel of any nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on the polynomial ring, but there exist an affine domain, algebraically independent elements and a locally nilpotent derivation such that the result of substituting elements into the polynomial lies in the kernel of that locally nilpotent derivation, but at least one of the substituted elements does not lie in that kernel.

papers.title: Long-Range Ergotropy Transfer with Weakened Boundary-Coupling Spin Chains
papers.abstract: Ergotropy is a key quantity of a quantum battery that measures the maximum extractable energy. When the extraction process is not local, a faithful transfer of ergotropy across distance is necessary. In this work, we investigate such transfer by using spin chains with weakened coupling at the boundaries as mediator. Weakening the coupling at the two boundaries of the chain gives rise to localized edge states allowing high fidelity transfer within given time duration. We found that, for long spin chains, the transferred ergotropy alternates between even and odd number of spins. We explain this parity effect by investigating the chain spectral structure. Furthermore, we consider both the nearest-neighbor and long-range interactions between spin. In both model of interactions, weakening the boundary couplings improves the maximum transferred ergotropy for long spin chain, compared with in the case of conventional uniform chain. Although the long-range interaction reduces the transferred ergotropy, the transfer time is reduced, too, in particular for longer chain. In addition to the total transferred ergotropy, we also investigate the effect of initial states of the sender spin to the transport of the coherent and incoherent components of the total ergotropy, and the average transport efficiency.

papers.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
papers.abstract: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. The coupling is induced by the variations of the electronic structure when the relative orientation of the magnetization of adjacent monolayers changes from parallel to antiparallel, modifying both the dielectric constant and band alignment. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. We use density functional calculations to assess the magnitude of the effect in various materials, including CrI$_3$, CrBr$_3$, CrCl$_3$ and NiBr$_2$. We predict magnetoresistance ratios in the range of 1.14-1.20 for the charge-transfer device and up to $10^3$ in the single-electron transistor.

papers.title: AgentOPSD: Turn-Level Credit Assignment via Recursive Belief Revision
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards ordinarily spreads a single advantage over a whole trajectory, a granularity too coarse to isolate the few decisions on which success in a long, multi-turn interaction actually turns. Privileged self-distillation supplies denser supervision, but it leaves unanswered how a set of local teacher-student discrepancies should be converted into credit along a sequence. We introduce AgentOPSD, a critic-free scheme that assigns credit recursively, one interaction turn at a time. Inside a turn, the token-level log-probability gaps between a skill-conditioned self-teacher and the student are summed, and that sum acts as evidence in a recursive Bayesian update carried out in log-odds space; the resulting revisions reallocate the outcome-derived advantage across turns through a multiplier that is bounded and preserves its sign. With Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2.5-7B as policy backbones on ALFWorld, the method improves consistently on GRPO and on self-distillation baselines, and attains 89.1% success at the 7B scale. Ablations attribute the gain to aggregating evidence at turn boundaries and to making the belief revision depend on history, rather than to the local gap by itself.

papers.title: Effects of pulse durations in atom interferometry with double Raman diffraction
papers.abstract: Double Raman diffraction is a key enabling technique for future space missions relying on atom interferometry that offers enhanced sensitivity and intrinsic suppression of systematic effects. This diffraction mechanism naturally arises when employing a retro-reflection configuration in microgravity, but then accelerations can no longer be determined through a frequency-chirp scan. As a consequence, measurements become much more sensitive to systematic effects associated with pulse timing and duration. Indeed, the finite pulse duration can introduce additional phase shifts and small modifications of the arm trajectories, which are critical sources of error in high-precision measurements. In this work, we present the first complete analytical results of these effects for double Raman diffraction, building upon previous work for single diffraction and extending the standard literature. Our analysis determines the impact of finite pulse durations on the full interferometer sequence, quantifying the shifts of the atomic wave packets' trajectories and the acquired phases. The description relies on a comprehensive framework describing matter-wave propagation in terms of central trajectories and centered wave packets, and can be easily incorporated into relativistic treatments. Furthermore, we make use of group theoretic methods that are particularly useful when accounting for residual accelerations and frequency chirps, which are also relevant for ground-based applications. Our study includes time-dependent accelerations and frequency chirps, gravity gradients, retardation effects, AC Stark shifts induced by the Raman pulses, and external forces such those due to magnetic fields or temperature gradients in the black-body radiation.

papers.title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
papers.abstract: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.

papers.title: Vendor-Agnostic Pseudocontinuous Arterial Spin Labeling Using Pulseq: Cross-Vendor Quantitative Evaluation
papers.abstract: Purpose: Inter-scanner variability in cerebral blood flow (CBF) quantification limits reproducibility in multi-center arterial spin labeling (ASL) studies. We developed and validated a vendor-agnostic pseudo-continuous ASL (PCASL) sequence using the open-source Pulseq framework, and assessed its extensibility to advanced perfusion imaging. Methods: A vendor-independent PCASL sequence was implemented in Pulseq and deployed on 3T scanners from Siemens, GE, and United Imaging. Seven healthy volunteers underwent single-post-labeling-delay (PLD) PCASL on all platforms, including test-retest scans. An in-house adapted Siemens vendor-based PCASL sequence served as reference. Reproducibility was assessed using within-subject coefficient of variation (CVwithin), root mean square error (RMSE), regional CBF correlation, and voxel-wise variation ratio maps. Multi-PLD PCASL and planning-free VE-PCASL were implemented as proof-of-concept extensions. Results: Mean gray matter (GM) CBF was similar across implementations. Test-retest GM CVwithin was below 4% on all platforms; Siemens-Pulseq had the lowest value (2.65%), versus 3.64% for the native sequence. GM RMSE between Siemens-Vendor and Pulseq implementations was comparable to test-retest RMSE, and all inter-scanner CVwithin values were below 3%. Voxel-wise variation ratio distributions were centered near 100%, suggesting cross-vendor variability comparable to physiological baseline fluctuations. Multi-PLD and VE-PCASL ran successfully on all platforms, yielding consistent CBF/ATT maps and vascular territory delineations. Conclusion: Pulseq-based PCASL enables vendor-agnostic perfusion imaging with low inter-scanner variability. This open-source approach provides a reproducible, standardized solution for multi-center ASL studies and facilitates deployment of advanced ASL techniques in clinical research.

papers.title: Interface-Preserving ${H}_\infty$ Model Reduction of Network Systems
papers.abstract: We study projection-based reduced-order models that exactly retain specified input and output interfaces. Admissible projections are characterized geometrically: the retained subspace must contain every input and output direction, which fixes the minimum order. The reduction error factors into input-coupling, internal-dynamics, and output-coupling systems, giving a submultiplicative ${H}_\infty$ bound; for positively dominated factors the ${H}_\infty$ error equals a dc gain computable from linear solves. Strict dissipativity certifies the stability of every orthogonal reduction, and a Hankel singular value bounds the optimum a posteriori. These results motivate sequential graph-coarsening heuristics for networks. On a 65,566-state chip thermal network, interface-preserving coarsening yields sparse, positive lumped models that are more accurate than Kron reduction of the same interface at every order, with far fewer edges; balanced truncation is more accurate but destroys the network structure.

papers.title: Exact codegree Turán densities of even zycles
papers.abstract: We determine the exact codegree Turán density of the $3$-uniform zycle $Z_\ell$ for every even integer $\ell\ge 8$ with $3\nmid\ell$,showing that $γ(Z_\ell)=1/3$. More generally, we prove that $γ(Z_\ell)\le 1/3$ for all even $\ell\ge 8$. Our results partially answer a question of Piga and Schülke [Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 58 (2026), e70348] concerning the sharpness of their upper bound of $1/2$.

papers.title: The compositional link between rocky exoplanets and their host stars is consistent with Earth-like devolatilization
papers.abstract: Previous work found a higher bulk iron-to-silicon (Fe/Si) ratio in rocky exoplanets relative to their host star, traditionally explained by iron enrichment. An alternative explanation is devolatilization of the planetary abundance ratios with respect to the host star, where volatile elements such as O and S are progressively depleted compared to refractory elements such as Fe and Mg, as in Earth. We explore whether these elemental molar ratios are consistent with a devolatilization trend. We revisit the core mass fraction of 14 rocky exoplanets with masses between 0.5 and 10 Earth masses whose host stars have spectroscopic abundances of Fe, Si, Mg, O, and S in the literature. We use interior structure retrievals with two independent forward models, the Marseille Super-Earth Interior model and pyExoInt, to estimate compositional parameters, including elemental molar ratios, from mass and radius measurements. We find that 8 out of 14 exoplanets in our sample present an Earth-like devolatilization trend, while only one planet shows a 1:1 relationship between planetary and stellar abundances. This suggests that devolatilization offers a plausible explanation for the observed non-1:1 relation. The two interior models agree on the devolatilization trend, demonstrating that our derived trends are robust. The main limiting factor in constraining refractory compositions of rocky planets relative to their host star is the small sample with constrained stellar abundances and the lack of variety in orbital distances. The PLATO mission will help by extending the sample of characterized rocky planets to orbital periods of up to one year. The variety in refractory elemental ratio trends may indicate a wide diversity in bulk composition, outgassing and other mantle properties relevant for habitability.

papers.title: A Many-Shapes framework for Galactic Cosmic Rays
papers.abstract: Thanks to recent measurements by space and ground-level detectors, the energy spectra of cosmic ray protons and helium nuclei are now known with good precision over a broad energy range extending for more than six orders of magnitude, from a few GeV to approximately 10PeV. These measurements reveal that both spectra do not have a simple power--law form, and exhibit several features. The proton to helium ratio exhibits a very unexpected behavior: it decreases for rigidities $\lesssim 10^5$~GV, and increases for higher rigidities. Several authors have interpreted the observed spectral features as revealing the fact the CR spectra are formed by the contributions of a few components (in some cases as few as two) produced by sources that belong to distinct classes of astrophysical accelerators, with sources in the same class producing spectra with the same characteristic shape. Most of these authors also consider it necessary to include the contribution of one (or perhaps more than one) ``local'' sources, recently active in the vicinity of the solar system. However, this approach has several limitations, and in this work we discuss an alternative scenario in which the cosmic ray sources, even belonging to the same class, produce spectra with a broad range of shapes. The power--law form of the total source spectrum emerges as the average of these contributions. In this framework observable spectral features can be produced by statistical fluctuations, and different spectral slopes for protons and helium nuclei can be observed even if one assumes that acceleration is rigidity-dependent.

papers.title: Covert System Identification Under Timing Constraints: A Static Linear Model and Its Detectability Implications
papers.abstract: This paper studies covert system identification in cyber-physical systems, where an attacker infers plant dynamics while attempting to remain stealthy. We introduce a lightweight static linear model in which the time to execute a setpoint change is proportional to the commanded speed difference. On a Siemens PROFINET testbed this gain captures the drive's ramp response accurately but not its terminal overshoot. That omitted transient becomes the attacker's main exposure: on real traces, the residual left by the linear masking procedure is detected by two anomaly monitors, Process-Aware Stealthy-Attack Detection (PASAD) and the CUSUM change detector. Across the cascade identification and staircase attack strategies defined in the paper, the stealth boundary relates to the plant's own settling transients, a structural limit for this class of models under the adopted detector-calibration regime. Comparison against dynamic models obtained by N4SID, trained at multiple excitation amplitudes, shows that the evaluated N4SID models do not improve stealth over the structure-informed ramp model. Since per-cycle computation is negligible for both procedures, the binding trade-off is not inference cost but whether the attacker can acquire and refresh a model without injecting detectable perturbations.

papers.title: Nonlinear integral equations for stress-controlled rheology: Collocation methods for Volterra equations with functional kernels
papers.abstract: We present a class of numerical collocation methods to solve a typical inverse problem that arises in the stress-controlled rheology of complex fluids with pronounced history-dependent response, where the relation between stress and flow rate is given by an integral constitutive equation as the material law. We demonstrate the method by calculating the creep response of a nontrivial model of a shear-thinning viscoelastic fluid where a stress overshoot in rate-controlled startup flow leads to ``sudden yielding'' in stress-controlled creep. Our method is able to address the long-time behavior of the model, distinguishing the amorphous solid from the stress-induced yielded fluid, and from the in-between case of infinite deformation that never achieves a stationary shear rate (proper creep). To this end, we implement a method with flexible time-stepping, and prove uniqueness of the solution and convergence of the methods for a broad class of highly viscoelastic non-linear rheological laws in integral form.

papers.title: Monetisation and Cost Function Scalarisation Cannot Guarantee Valid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Monetary quantities are not preferences. Cost is an object-related system performance; value-for-money is an actor's subjective evaluation of it. Monetisation embeds trade-off information: its conversion coefficients express valuations and determine how heterogeneous performances compensate one another. Cost-benefit analysis, even net present value, yields quantities of money, not the preference value actors attribute to them. This creates a monetisation paradox. Cost enters a multi-criteria problem as one performance among several, but money is then elevated into the universal representation of all others, creating representational dominance. The problem collapses into a single-criterion one in which every performance acts only through its imposed monetary equivalent. Cost-function scalarisation does not resolve this by substituting points, normalised scores, losses, or penalties: these transformations and their weights fix preference directions, intensities, and trade-offs, so they are implicit preference models, yet are treated as technical constructs rather than measured and validated. A well-defined scalar optimum is therefore not necessarily a decision-valid multi-criteria outcome. Numerical commensurability does not establish preference commensurability. Decision validity requires heterogeneous performances to be transformed into actor preferences in a unified preference domain. Preference is relational and contextual, yet can be represented on an affine scale. Preference Function Modelling and the Linear Preference Space provide the commensurability required for valid aggregation. The decision criterion should thus maximise aggregated actor preference over the feasible and acceptable design-decision space, not monetised quantities or scalarised scores.

papers.title: All-to-all connectivity via adiabatic ZZ interactions in a superconducting flux qubit processor
papers.abstract: Scalable superconducting quantum processors would benefit from high qubit connectivity, yet existing architectures connect neighbouring qubits via tunable couplers, which introduce substantial wiring and control overhead. Here, we propose a baseband-driven adiabatic ZZ gate that entangles any selected pair in a register of flux qubits coupled via a common cavity. The qubits stay dc-biased at their flux sweet spot. Strong drives applied selectively through local flux lines, at frequencies far below the qubit transitions, adiabatically tilt the quantization axes and generate an effective longitudinal ZZ interaction. The strength of the coupling is tunable and controlled by the amplitudes and relative phase of the drives rather than by any resonance condition. Numerical simulations give coherent gate errors below $10^{-4}$ over broad ranges of drive frequency, with comparable fidelities for two simultaneous gates in a four-qubit register. The protocol is robust against frequency fluctuations and remains effective even when many qubits are coupled to the cavity.

papers.title: From Likelihood Convergence to Parameter Convergence in POMDPs
papers.abstract: Likelihood-based methods are widely used to learn the parameters of partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs). While finite-sample guarantees for policy suboptimality exist for certain POMDP subclasses, analogous guarantees for parameter recovery remain less well understood. For any candidate POMDP parameter, we bound its parameter recovery error in terms of its likelihood gap to the ground truth, the structural conditioning of the observation and transition kernels, and the behavior policy used to collect data. The bound applies in both the undercomplete and overcomplete regimes, with the latter following naturally from the undercomplete analysis. Because the result applies to any sufficiently good candidate, it yields finite-sample guarantees for the maximum-likelihood estimator and any procedure producing a parameter with controlled likelihood gap. This is particularly useful for near-optimal learning in infinite-horizon POMDPs, where existing approaches largely rely on model-based planning with accurate transition and observation kernel estimates. The bound separates the contributions of the behavior policy and model, showing how data-collection choices, including action coverage, and their effects on mixing can accelerate parameter learning.

papers.title: Evaluating Cross-Signal Coherence in Mammography Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: As vision-language models (VLMs) move toward interpreting medical images directly, their outputs increasingly include not just a label but a stated confidence and a written justification. Yet the field still predominantly evaluates VLMs using just accuracy. We evaluate the coherence between answer, confidence, and explanation across four VLMs on breast density and BI-RADS categorization, using two mammography datasets. We perform controlled perturbations of the question, multiple choice option orders, and the images and assess changes in the three outputs. Our results suggest confidence does not decrease even as the mammography image is changed. Shuffling the options also changes most VLMs' answers. Notably, there are cases where a model's own stated reasoning contradicts its final answer, a distinction accuracy alone cannot capture but one that governs whether an AI-generated answer can be trusted.

papers.title: Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics-Guided Machine-Learning Potentials for Mapping Nitric Oxide Interactions with Oxygen-Covered Graphite
papers.abstract: Exploratory ab initio molecular dynamics is used to construct machine-learning interatomic potentials for NO interactions with highly oriented pyrolytic graphite at 33\% bridge-site oxygen coverage. Representative configurations sampled across surface temperatures and incidence energies provide reference energies and forces for training and validation. The selected potential enables relaxation of 300 adsorption configurations and construction of spatial and angular interaction maps. These maps reveal increasingly restricted attractive regions during vertical approach and reduced short-range repulsion upon molecular reorientation. The resulting adsorption geometries and interaction landscapes guide further first-principles sampling toward refining potentials for NO oxidation dynamics.

papers.title: Text2NGAC: a multi-LLM pipeline for NGAC policy extraction with mutation-based verification
papers.abstract: Access-control policies are written in natural language but enforced as formal models, and translating them into NIST Next Generation Access Control (NGAC) graphs remains unsolved: prior systems cover only subsets of the NGAC model, and none verify the graphs they extract. We present Text2NGAC, a pipeline of cooperating large language models that disambiguates each sentence before extraction, escalates uncertain sentences to a multi-model ensemble, and checks the resulting graph with a five-strategy verifier whose own effectiveness is measured by controlled mutation testing. To our knowledge it is the first system to extract all four NGAC relationship types - associations, prohibitions, event-response obligations, and assignments - from real-world policy documents. Three results anchor the evaluation. The verifier detects 99.7% of 918 injected mutants and every structural fail-open fault, and the fault classes it misses are characterized and weighted by security consequence rather than left unexamined. The extracted graphs are enforceable: one corpus's graph loads unmodified into the NIST reference implementation, which reproduces all 55 access decisions the graph entails and fires an extracted obligation end-to-end. Extraction reaches 97.3-99.6% exact-tuple-match accuracy on the 714 scored sentences of four real corpora, far above three reproduced baselines on matched metrics, and paraphrase probes with semantic re-scoring bound the pipeline's sensitivity to rewording. Reported accuracy is wording- and benchmark-specific, adversarial input is outside the verifier's guarantees, and the intended deployment is extraction plus structural verification feeding expert review. A complete two-tier reproducibility artifact accompanies the paper.

papers.title: More Papers, Not More Output: Collaboration and Publication Trends among Early-Career Researchers
papers.abstract: Concerns about publication pressure often assume that early-career researchers now produce more papers than comparable researchers did in the past. However, publication counts may give a misleading impression of individual publication output because research has become increasingly collaborative. Researchers can list more papers on their CVs not only by producing more work themselves, but also by working with more coauthors and sharing credit for the same papers. Whether the collaboration-adjusted output of early-career researchers has increased over time has rarely been examined empirically. This study addresses this gap by analysing publication records from more than 200,000 early-career researchers at Western research institutions across five major science, engineering, and health fields between 1996 and 2024. Recent cohorts appear on more papers than earlier cohorts, but they also work in much larger research teams. Once publication credit is divided among coauthors, collaboration-adjusted output remains stable or declines across all fields. These findings show that research evaluation metrics that ignore collaboration are increasingly poorly aligned with how scientific work is produced. Rising publication counts alone should therefore not be taken as evidence that early-career researchers are producing more individual publication output.

papers.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Privacy-Enhanced Computing Through Register Renaming
papers.abstract: Privacy-Enhanced Computing (PEC) is a mechanism to hide program secrets from the outside world without paying the cost of fully-homomorphic encryption. Previous work has developed hardware mechanisms to achieve this goal but they require a dedicated processor enclave where all computations are done, requiring duplicate ALU resources and limiting the performance of PEC-utilizing applications due to not being able to access the full compute resources of the processor (e.g., multiple execution units and vector units), or not being able to execute PEC instructions in parallel and out-of-order. In this work, we introduce HPS-PEC (Hidden in Plain Sight PEC), a novel method of utilizing existing infrastructure in the CPU to achieve PEC with minor modifications to the architecture. We show that, across 25 VIP-Bench benchmarks and with a 7-cycle QARMA-64 cipher, HPS-PEC runs encrypted code at 3.41x the execution time of unprotected native code (geometric mean), of which 1.03x is the cost of data-oblivious code itself, and is 1.26x faster than a Sequestered Encryption (SE) unit while utilizing under a third of its dedicated area. Our method keeps plaintext out of reach of every instruction, as an enclave does given a correctly functioning renamer and register file, which every program already depends on.

papers.title: Contrasting one- and two-particle excitations in cuprate strange metals
papers.abstract: In unconventional superconductivity, the pairing mechanism remains one of the central unresolved problems in solid-state physics. Moreover, the normal state shows strong deviations from conventional Fermi-liquid behavior, most notably a scattering rate that is linear in energy and temperature. Here we study the momentum dependence of the energy and damping of collective excitations in optimally doped cuprates in the normal state. In particular, we analyze existing Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy (EELS) data of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8 [Phys. Rev. B 44, 7155 (1991)] and new analogous optical plasmon data of Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O10. Furthermore, we reanalyze similar Resonant Inelastic Xray Scattering (RIXS) acoustic plasmon data [Phys. Rev. R 6, 043184 (2024)] of La1.84Sr0.16CuO4 and La1.84Ce0.16CuO4. We contrast these two-particle excitation results with one-particle excitations measured by Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES). Most of the plasmon behavior can be described well by combined self-energies of a hole and an electron. The dispersion of optical plasmons at high energy is only weakly determined by correlation effects, indicating resilient quasiparticles. The damping of the optical plasmons at low energy, however, is strongly influenced by the reduced scattering rates described in the marginal Fermi liquid model for "strange-metal" behavior. In addition, the same model describes the linear-in-energy damping of acoustic plasmons. Contrary to some theoretical predictions, we see no overdamped optical plasmons below the classical Lindhard critical wave vector.

papers.title: Modeling and Estimation of a Towed Marine System
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the modeling and state estimation of a towed marine system consisting of two autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs), a pair of umbilical cables, towfish, and a trailing loop cable. Inspired by the existing literature, we employ a lumped-mass modeling approach for the cables and towfish, capturing the essential dynamics while maintaining computational tractability. A Lyapunov-based analysis is conducted to verify the stability and convergence properties of the proposed model. Building on this model, we propose two state estimation methods, namely a reduced-order observer and a perfect-measurement extended Kalman filter (PMEKF), using only the measurements from the ASVs' onboard sensors. Numerical simulations and experimental results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

papers.title: LawKAN: Group-Law Layers for Composition -- When Imposing a Known Law Pays Off
papers.abstract: Many tasks compose transformations by a known rule: chained rotations in robotics and navigation. Learned models relearn it, compounding error; classical estimators hardcode it and miss hardware deviations. We impose the known structure and learn only the remainder: an exact non-commutative group law sits in the node of a self-contained layer, its edges learn local increments, and a zero-initialized correction psi learns unknown deviations of the law. A pre-training criterion predicts exact representability. On fixed-angle SU(2) composition, a 54-parameter dense edge is the most accurate dense model, at 27x fewer parameters than the strongest fixed-matrix baseline, and lies 0.05 deg above the Bayes floor. On real robot arms, an isolated 306-parameter psi reaches 1.12-1.14 mm versus 1.29-1.33 mm for Gauss-Newton at N >= 60, and the recipe transfers across three vendors and two protocols. The recipe matches classical fits where the data obey the law and loses where the imposed law is not the task's.

papers.title: Quantum benchmarks for magnetic energies and transition temperatures
papers.abstract: Predicting magnetic ordering temperatures requires accurate exchange interactions and an appropriate treatment of spin thermodynamics. Here we assess these requirements through complementary quantum Monte Carlo benchmarks. For five insulating antiferromagnets, we compare ferromagnetic-antiferromagnetic energy differences from diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) and density functional theory with references reconstructed from inelastic neutron scattering (INS) exchanges. DMC underestimates these references but achieves a mean absolute error comparable to the best-performing functionals tested. Separately, we directly test the previously proposed (S+1)/S rescaling of classical Monte Carlo temperatures against quantum stochastic series expansion simulations for 17 compounds using corresponding INS-derived Heisenberg Hamiltonians. Rescaling reduces the mean absolute classical-quantum temperature difference from 81.7 to 8.2 K, with a mean absolute percentage difference of 5.9 %. These results establish a direct quantum benchmark for the rescaling within the tested models and emphasize that improvements in electronic magnetic energy scales should be accompanied by attention to quantum spin thermodynamics.

papers.title: That Time of the Year Again: Government Pay Revisions in the Aggregate Economy
papers.abstract: Public pay is set by law in nominal terms, so inflation erodes its real value between legal acts until the government revises it. I model each revision as the choice of a forward-looking government, shaped by two costs that push in opposite directions. A fixed cost of acting makes revisions large and rare, whereas a convex cost of financing the increase at once makes them small and frequent. Through the budget, each revision also moves debt and the risk of fiscal stress under which the next one is made. In the documented pay decisions of eleven countries, pay set at discretion erodes against prices and private earnings and is restored in discrete steps, every cut was decided during market stress or an adjustment program, and court rulings drove a wedge between the cuts legislated, the cuts paid and the cuts that lasted. Estimated on the legal acts, the model reproduces the documented paths of pay in most countries when data and simulations are measured the same way. In Portugal's estimated model, the savings that the Treasury requires once spreads rise produce the cuts, the debt overhang holds pay down after the crisis, and a court that strikes cuts after they take effect invites cuts it will strike. Review of cuts before they took effect would have lowered the social cost of Portugal's crisis relative to review after the fact, and partial indexation would have paid in Bangladesh unless its automatic increases were costly to finance.

papers.title: GHiML: VLM-Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label Learning with Applications to Benthic Imagery
papers.abstract: Vision language models (VLMs) encode substantial expert knowledge within their weights, yet their direct application to specialised classification domains such as benthic imagery remains limited. Meanwhile, vision transformers trained on these tasks rely predominantly on low-level visual latents (colours, textures, and shapes) that lack the higher-level reasoning humans employ for identification. We propose Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label (GHiML) learning, a pipeline that extracts conceptual latent variables from a VLM conditioned on training data, generates sample-relevant captions grounded in those variables, and fuses the resulting textual embeddings with image embeddings via cross-attention and a per-node gated router. We also introduce the inverted HML score ($d_{\mathrm{inv}}$), a similarity score that evaluates hierarchical multi-label predictions through graph traversal distance and a cardinality penalty, providing an interpretable alternative to existing measures, which are insensitive to realistic degradations in sparse, deep hierarchies. Experiments on BenthicNet, FathomNet and iNaturalist show that the router improves macro $F_1$ over the vision-only baseline by up to 6.7 pp and $d_{\mathrm{inv}}$ by up to 21.1 pp on in-domain benthic data, with gains persisting under distribution shift. Ablations locate the contribution of the text itself: on the multi-label biotic hierarchies, removing the per-sample text signal degrades $d_{\mathrm{inv}}$ while leaving macro $F_1$ unchanged, consistent with text acting through prediction cardinality rather than node discrimination, whereas iNaturalist, whose annotations are single-label, loses 18.7% of macro $F_1$. Our results support the hypothesis that VLMs contain exploitable specialised knowledge that, when appropriately elicited, can augment classification in domains where direct visual learning is insufficient.

papers.title: Distinguishing thyroid nodule malignancy using digital palpation
papers.abstract: Accurate pre-operative diagnosis of thyroid nodules remains a major clinical challenge. Current diagnostic techniques rely on fine-needle aspiration and demonstrate high rates of inconclusive results, often leading to avoidable thyroidectomies with lifelong implications. Here, we introduce a mechanics-based diagnostic method that leverages Digital Palpation to determine malignancy and identify tissue subtypes in human thyroid nodules. From a cohort of patients undergoing thyroidectomies, we evaluated ex vivo thyroid specimens and processed the resulting mechanical data from 36 tests in 10 thyroid nodules. Principal Component Analysis reveals that these experimental results are distributed within a three-dimensional space of interpretable scalar features reflecting tissue grittiness, strength, and toughness, which map closely to descriptions of malignant and benign nodules given by clinicians. Our results further demonstrate that malignant nodules exhibit distinct mechanical signatures compared to their benign counterparts. This revealed a statistically significant difference (p = 9 x 10^-4) and separability (95% lower-bound Hedges' g = 1.08) between benign and malignant nodules along a direction in principal component space representing effective stiffness. Preliminary clustering patterns were also observed among malignant subtypes, including follicular, oncocytic, and papillary thyroid carcinomas. Together, these results highlight the potential of Digital Palpation as a novel mechanics-based method for tissue characterization and motivate its further development toward diagnostic applications.

papers.title: Differential Flatness of Nonlinear Consensus Networks: A Graph-Theoretic Perspective
papers.abstract: We study the property of differential flatness for networks of identical flat agents coupled through a consensus protocol, where a single exogenous input acts on one agent and the output of another agent is measured. We distinguish whether the network admits a flat output at all from whether the measured task output is a flat output. For the former, we show that flatness at a synchronized equilibrium requires controllability of the Laplacian leader--follower pair, which is also sufficient for linear agents but not for nonlinear ones. For the latter, we show that the relative degree of the task output is determined by its graph distance to the input node, so that it is a flat output if and only if the graph is a path with the input and output nodes at its ends. Numerical examples illustrate how flatness enables finite-time transitions between consensus configurations through a single input.

papers.title: Quotient Index for Symmetry-Protected Zeros and the Tenfold Way in Mackey's Construction of Super Corepresentations
papers.abstract: Symmetries that anticommute with a Hamiltonian can protect zero modes by obstructing their removal through symmetry-compatible perturbations. We formulate this obstruction as a quotient of the additive group of symmetry representations by the image of the map that forgets a compatible representation grading. To compute the quotient, we use Mackey's method to construct all irreducible super corepresentations of finite graded symmetry groups, allowing antiunitary operations and projective factor systems. Starting from the unitary Hamiltonian-preserving normal subgroup, this construction yields two complex and ten real structural types, characterized by residual Altland--Zirnbauer symmetry algebras. The residual and induced graded modules have isomorphic graded commutants, and their represented symmetry algebras share a graded Morita class that is super opposite to that of the commutant. We derive character criteria that identify these types. Exhaustive enumeration of the restriction relations gives independent sector contributions $0$, $Z$, or $Z_2$, with only integer factors in the purely unitary case. In the finite semisimple setting, the complete index vanishes if and only if all zero modes can be lifted by a symmetry-compatible perturbation. Applications to one-dimensional end states and interpolation cylinders of disordered boundary Dirac theories recover protected multiplet counts and connect the quotient to bulk topology and sigma-model topological terms using bulk--boundary correspondence, texture-index theorems, and fermion-phase calculations.

papers.title: The Neptunian ridge depends on the choice of linear or logarithmic period
papers.abstract: The Neptunian ridge has been reported as an overdensity of planets with radii of $\simeq$5-8 R$_\oplus$ and orbital periods of $\simeq$3-6 d, located between the Neptunian desert and the savanna. It was first identified in Kepler data and has recently been reanalysed using our TESS occurrence rates, where it appears as an approximately twofold excess relative to neighbouring regions. We show that the reported excess arises from expressing the occurrence density per unit period, $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}P$, rather than per unit logarithmic period, $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}\ln P$, where the logarithmic form is standard in planet demographics. Because the savanna interval used for comparison is twice as wide in period as the ridge, a population uniform in $\ln P$ naturally produces a factor-of-two contrast in $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}P$. When expressed per unit $\ln P$, the published TESS and Kepler ridge-to-savanna contrasts decrease from 1.6-2.2 to 0.8-1.2, all consistent with unity. A simulated population with a desert but no intrinsic excess reproduces the appearance of a ridge in $\mathrm{d}N/\mathrm{d}P$ precisely. Reanalysing the TESS-SPOC occurrence rates of 5.5-8.5 R$_\oplus$ planets around FGK stars, we find a ridge-to-savanna ratio of $0.91^{+0.21}_{-0.16}$ per unit $\ln P$, which does not support the claimed overdensity at the ridge. Taken together, these tests imply that the published ridge is a result of the scale choice used, rather than a definitive property of the observed planet population.

papers.title: Completely monotone memory systems
papers.abstract: Linear time-invariant (LTI) relaxation systems are characterized by a completely monotone impulse response. This paper proposes an extension of this property to nonlinear systems: a system is said to have completely monotone memory if a positive increment in the past input leads to a completely monotone increment in the future output. We show that this property constitutes a strong form of monotonicity, while also imposing stability constraints that closely resemble fading memory, contraction, and incremental stability. We also show that completely monotone memory is equivalent to classical relaxation for LTI systems and to a combination of monotonicity and stability for a class of scalar state-affine systems. Finally, we illustrate the relevance of our framework to the gating dynamics of conductance-based models.

papers.title: Gelfand and sampling numbers of weighted Wiener spaces
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish sharp asymptotic bounds on the Gelfand numbers of weighted Wiener spaces $\mathcal{A}^r_θ$ measured in $L_q$. This is done by using results for Gelfand numbers of sequence spaces and applying them to each layer of a hyperbolic cross to obtain results for Gelfand numbers between different (weighted) Wiener spaces. These can then be used to establish bounds in $L_q$ by combining them with known results and techniques for Besov spaces. This significantly narrows a gap in the current research, since the Gelfand numbers provide a lower bound on the (non-linear) sampling numbers, whereas upper bounds on this quantity have been studied in multiple papers via an upper bound given by the best m-term approximation.

papers.title: WanderBench: Can World Models Explore Dynamic Worlds from Video?
papers.abstract: Video world models conditioned on an input video make it possible to explore real, recorded dynamic scenes, enabling re-shooting of footage, free-viewpoint replay, and real-to-sim environments for embodied agents.
