Here, we demonstrate how pump engineering enables the generation of high-dimensional MESs for arbitrary $d$ defined in $d \times d$ subspaces. By identifying the interplay between the spatial pump structure and the choice of OAM subspace, the required pump profile for a target MES is directly determined. Our results reveal that maximal entanglement with OAM requires a careful and nontrivial design of the effective high-dimensional Hilbert subspace.

papers.title: Self-Healing by design: Immune-system inspired autonomous cyber resilience
papers.abstract: Digital innovations have strongly improved ship capabilities, including command, control & communication, navigation and combat management. In the wake of digitisation and geopolitical stress, resilience against cyber-attacks has become a key challenge. Autonomous Cyber Resilience (ACR) methods, inspired by features of the human immune system, provide a promising perspective. Proofs of concept of autonomous self-healing and self-protecting software have been realised in cloud environments using containerisation, monitoring and deployment technology. However, developing a suitable "cyber immune system" for more complex digital systems is still an intricate challenge. In this paper, we share insights on how ACR methods can be combined with resilience mechanisms present in critical naval and aeronautical manoeuvring systems. Using TNO's "OpPic" application, we show how TNO's Self-Healing for Cyber Security software can provide autonomous mission- and threat-adaptive resilience. On this basis, six guidelines for the design of autonomous cyber resilient systems are derived. The ultimate goal is to enable operators to oversee and control their system's "cyber immune response", to be able to continuously adapt to evolving threats and mission priorities.

papers.title: Information--control limits for record-indistinguishable reset of a monitored qubit
papers.abstract: A qubit that is continuously monitored from the moment it is prepared in its excited state writes evidence of that preparation into its measurement record. We ask how much control is needed to reset such a qubit to its ground state while keeping its complete record statistically close to the record of an undriven ground-state qubit. The qubit is measured in $σ_z$ at rate $Γ_m$ with efficiency $η$ and has no relaxation. For feedback that acts causally on the record, distinguishability is the Kullback--Leibler divergence $D$ of the controlled record law from the reference law, and the control cost is the quadratic effort $J$, the integrated squared Rabi frequency. We prove that every open-loop drive leaves $D$ infinite and that every admissible control obeys $DJ\geΓ_mU(η,D/κ_0)$, where $U$ is given by a one-parameter family of integrals and $κ_0=1-\ln2$. Our main result is the exact high-effort constant $\lim_{ε\downarrow0}\inf\{DJ/Γ_m: D\leε\}=K(η)$, where $K(η)=[\int_0^π\sqrt{2η(1+\cosθ)^2+(1-η)\sin^2θ}\,dθ]^2$; an explicit sequence of two-phase feedback policies attains it. The first term of the integrand is the population evidence that the record receives while the qubit is rotated toward the ground state. The second is the price of the impurity created when the unrecorded part of the measurement dephases the coherence that the rotation needs; the record receives this evidence later, when the measurement repurifies the qubit. The global constant $c(η)=\inf DJ/Γ_m$ satisfies $K/2\le F_2\le c\le K$, where $F_2$ is again given by an integral; $c$ is known exactly at $η=1$ and in the limit $η\to0$. With any nonzero relaxation rate the unconstrained infimum of $DJ$ vanishes, so $c(η)$ is specific to the relaxation-free model.

papers.title: A Distributed Observer with Random Agent Activations over Random Communication Networks
papers.abstract: This paper develops a distributed observer for the forward-Euler discretization of a continuous-time linear time-invariant system under random local operations and random communications. Under uniform stochastic strong connectivity, we establish almost sure exponential convergence of all local state estimates for sufficiently small discretization step sizes. We further examine how the underlying parameters and components affect the admissible range of the discretization step size and the guaranteed convergence rate bound. Unlike related approaches, the proposed method does not require each local unobservable subspace to admit an $A$-invariant complement.

papers.title: Let the Gallery Learn Itself: Training-Free Iterative Side-View Face Recognition
papers.abstract: What if a face recognition system could learn from every encounter without a single gradient update? We present Gallery Self-Evolution (GSE), a training-free framework where the gallery itself adapts at test time. The core mechanism---dedup-FIFO curation---archives novel appearance samples after successful recognition while permanently locking the enrollment template, bounded at 30 embeddings per identity. On CFP-FP and IJB-C benchmarks, GSE closes the side-view gap by +23 points at 45° yaw and boosts TAR@FAR=0.001 by +9.4 points, all at CPU-level cost. No retraining. No GPU. Just a gallery that grows smarter every time it meets you.

papers.title: Quantitative Homogenization and Global Lipschitz Estimates for Elasticity with Periodic Rigid Inclusions
papers.abstract: We consider the pure traction problem for linear elasticity in a bounded domain containing an $\varepsilon$-periodic array of perfectly rigid inclusions. For compatible $L^2$ boundary tractions on a Lipschitz domain, we prove an $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ error estimate in $H^1$ for a smoothed first-order two-scale expansion. If the exterior and inclusion boundaries are $C^{2,β}$, we also obtain a global Lipschitz estimate, uniform in $\varepsilon$, for compatible $C^{0,σ}$ tractions, where $0<σ<β$. The displacement is normalized modulo rigid motions, and the estimate controls the full gradient in the matrix and the inclusions. The boundary argument uses a local Neumann comparison estimate whose constant is independent of the choice of inclusions retained in cells cut by an artificial localization boundary. We prove this estimate by combining cellwise rigidification, divergence-free stress extensions, and duality, and then apply a boundary Campanato iteration and local estimates at the microscopic scale.

papers.title: Smooth approximations to character sums and zeta sums
papers.abstract: We study smooth approximations to Dirichlet character sums and zeta sums. The uniform upper-bound consequence of the Granville--Soundararajan conjecture, when imposed on all nonprincipal characters including imprimitive ones, implies the Riemann hypothesis for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet \(L\)-function. The proof uses characters induced to moduli divisible by all small primes. In the other direction, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,χ)\), we establish the conjectured approximation uniformly for \(q^a\le x\le q\), where \(0<a\le1\) is fixed, with \(y=(\log q+(\log x)^2)(\log\log q)^C\) for every fixed \(C>6\). In this range both the character sum and its smooth restriction, and hence their difference, are exponentially small relative to the number of \(y\)-smooth integers coprime to \(q\). We establish the corresponding approximation for \(\sum_{n\le x}n^{-it}\) under the Riemann hypothesis for the zeta function, uniformly for \(T^a\le x\le T\) and \(2T\le t\le5T\). We also show that the full zeta-sum smooth-approximation conjecture implies the Lindelöf hypothesis.

papers.title: Uniform inference for $U$-statistics of exchangeable arrays under degeneracy
papers.abstract: Many $U$-statistics of row-column exchangeable arrays become degenerate at natural null hypotheses: their convergence rates change and their limiting laws may or may not remain Gaussian. We establish conditions under which inference based on the classical unbiased variance estimator is uniformly valid across these changes, without knowledge of the degeneracy order. It is known that $U$-statistics can be decomposed into orthogonal projections indexed by bipartite graphs. Under uniform fourth-moment assumptions, we establish that the standardized statistic is asymptotically Gaussian and the classical unbiased variance estimator is ratio-consistent, as long as a certain measure of concentration for projections indexed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. Under compactness of the normalized projections, both properties hold if and only if the proportion of variance contributed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. The necessity of this condition follows from a general limit theorem for these $U$-statistics, in which each graph contributes to a Wiener chaos of order equal to its number of connected components. We note that the row-column jackknife variance estimator, although nonnegative, does not generally give a studentized statistic with a standard normal limit in degenerate regimes. We illustrate our theory with an application to estimation and testing based on a distance from product form, exhibiting Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits at various rates depending on the model. We also propose a conservative inference procedure that does not require a Gaussian limit, valid under additional moment and projection conditions.

papers.title: Orthogonal Updates for the Win: Towards Accelerated Adaptive Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: Single-loop minimax methods are appealing for modern machine learning, but standard stochastic gradient updates can be unstable and oscillatory under tightly coupled primal-dual dynamics, making performance notoriously sensitive to stepsizes. To fundamentally improve stability, we develop an orthogonal update framework tailored to minimax optimization, which applies updates along orthogonalized directions to reduce update anisotropy. However, orthogonalization reshapes the optimization geometry and makes coordinating primal-dual stepsizes even more delicate. To overcome this challenge, we develop AdaSGDA, which equips orthogonal updates with an adaptive stepsize rule driven by accumulated gradient norms. This mechanism automatically balances coupled primal-dual progress under orthogonalization, yielding an effectively parameter-free method for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization. We prove that AdaSGDA avoids problem-dependent tuning while attaining the state-of-the-art $\mathcal{O}\left(T^{-1/4}\right)$ convergence rate. We further propose AdaSGDA-VR, which incorporates a carefully designed variance reduction scheme and achieves the faster $\mathcal{O}\left(T^{-1/3}\right)$ rate. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our methods deliver competitive performance compared to existing minimax optimization methods.

papers.title: What Travels Across Languages? Reading, Transfer and Erasure of Cross-Lingual Concept Subspaces in Bangla Idioms
papers.abstract: Cross-lingual concept analysis requires distinguishing the information that a subspace retains from the classifiers and erasers that transfer through it. We study these operations in six frozen encoders using 10,359 Bangla (Bengali) idiom senses, eight input conditions, and figurative-class and sentiment labels. Class-mean directions provide the most consistent evidence of shared coarse meaning: in post hoc analyses, they outperform random-subspace, permuted-label and covariance-matched nulls in all 12 model-label tests under balanced accuracy. A prospective internal re-split supports idiom-alone sharing in 10 of 12 tests, spanning five encoders. The original confirmatory logistic-regression family rejects both planned nulls in 4 of 12 tests, where English directions gain only a few accuracy points above the majority-class floor (3.0-7.3). Classifier transfer depends on the input map and regularization: English-trained class-mean readouts beat both zero-shot nulls in 8 of 12 discovery tests, and stronger source-selected penalties improve transfer through logistic and LEACE directions. These readouts use Bangla-validation-selected layers and unlabeled target preprocessing. Input controls show greater coarse-class sharing for explicit glosses than for idiom counterparts. Reading, however, does not imply effective erasure: English-fitted LEACE removes less than one percentage point of Bangla figurative-class accuracy, compared with 4-11 points for Bangla-fitted LEACE; INLP shows a similar asymmetry. Pattern-filter analysis, covariance-weighted input maps and a binary Gaussian overlap bound explain how these operations can diverge. The analogous multiclass ordering is an empirical diagnostic, observed in 11 of 12 cells. The results support an estimator-sensitive account of cross-lingual concept sharing and motivate evaluating reading, classifier transfer, erasure and overlap separately.

papers.title: Hausdorff Dimension of Escaping Sets of Transcendental Entire Functions in the Speiser Class
papers.abstract: For every $d\in[1,2]$, we construct a transcendental entire function $f$ whose finite singular value is contained in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and whose escaping set has Hausdorff dimension $d$. For $d<2$, the construction combines spiral corridors with quasiconformal folding. A narrowing Archimedean spiral gives dimension one, while a logarithmic spiral with adjustable width gives intermediate dimensions. The endpoint $d=2$ is realized by the exponential map. This gives an affirmative answer to a question of Bishop posed in 2018.

papers.title: Collective Chiral Response of Achiral Plasmonic Arrays Induced by Truncated Bloch-Floquet Effect
papers.abstract: Chirality in plasmonic systems is commonly associated with structures differentiated by their handedness. Here, we demonstrate the emergence of collective chirality in structurally achiral periodic hole arrays induced by non-local surface-plasmon interactions. We attribute this effect to the transfer of the optical angular momentum in the system. While an individual sub-wavelength circular aperture is not expected to alter the total angular momentum, the periodic structure results in a coherent coupling of plasmons wavefronts, giving rise to a collective Bloch-Floquet-like response. The edge of the structure accumulates the helical phase that eventually results in a visible spin-dependent shifting of the plasmonic beam. We systematically study the effects of hole-array size, periodicity and the geometry. The observed phenomenon shows an unprecedented robustness and consistency. These results establish periodic plasmonic arrays as a platform for converting localized helicity-dependent responses into collective chirality, providing a route toward controlling chiral plasmonic wavefronts in structurally achiral systems.

papers.title: Nonlinear Stability of Planar Shock Waves for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations in R^3
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the global nonlinear stability and large-time decay rates of small-amplitude planar viscous shock waves for the three-dimensional (3-D) full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier equations in the whole space $\R^3$. {We prove that if the initial perturbation is sufficiently small in $H^3(\R^3)\cap\Hm(\R^3)$, then the Cauchy problem admits a unique global strong solution that converges to the planar shock profile without any phase shift. In the moving shock frame, both the conservative and primitive perturbations decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/4}$ in $H^3(\R^3)$. Their time and transverse spatial derivatives decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/2}$, measured in $\Hm(\R^3)$ for the conservative perturbation and in $H^1(\R^3)$ for the primitive perturbation.} No zero-mass condition or spectral stability assumption is imposed. On the whole space $\R^3$, the main analytical difficulties stem from the continuous transverse low frequencies, the opposite signs of shock compression in $L^2(\R^3)$ and unweighted $\Hm(\R^3)$, and the absence of density dissipation in the continuity equation coupled with temperature variations. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce a density-weighted $\Hm(\R^3)$ multiplier built from the inverse entropy Hessian and a modified curl operator. Through entropy symmetrization and the curl projection, all second-order acoustic derivatives of the potential cancel out and the transverse acoustic modes are controlled, so that the normal Euler drift is governed by the compressive derivative of the characteristic speed. Combined with an effective momentum variable and a momentum--density cross estimate, this negative-order energy absorbs the unfavorable compression term in the $L^2$ energy and closes the $H^3(\R^3)$ a priori estimates without loss of derivatives.

papers.title: The comparison of density estimation for transfer learning in Banach, Hilbert, Euclidean spaces
papers.abstract: Domain adaptation or DA methods are indispensable when target labels or computational resources are scarce, yet the domain kernel density and subspace alignment approaches completely assume a Hilbertian geometry. They measure distributional discrepancy with symmetric L2 divergences over Euclidean feature spaces or reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS). This preprint summarizes the manuscript Non-Hilbertian Domain Adaptation. Total Variation Alignment via L1 Density Regularization on Feature Manifolds, which proposes Banach Manifold Transfer Learning or BMTL. BMTL makes two coupled design decisions. The first one is that features are embedded on a geodesic manifold rather than treated as points of a flat Euclidean space, and the second one is that the density matching regularizer is formulated in an L1 Banach norm, whose minimization is equivalent, by Scheffe's theorem, to contracting the Total Variation or TV distance between domain densities, a bounded metric that weights all regions of the sample space uniformly. The L2 formulation, by contrast, squares deviations and therefore amplifies errors in the tails, over emphasizing density outliers that do not reflect meaningful distributional shift. Experiments on MNIST-USPS, COIL20, and Office+Caltech10 show consistent gains; the L1 variant beats an otherwise identical L2 ablation on every task, for example 92.44% vs. 89.80% on USPS->MNIST and surpasses the strongest baseline DMDA by +3.68% on average over twelve Office+Caltech transfers. This document situates the contribution with an explicit comparison of Euclidean, Hilbert, and Banach geometries.

papers.title: Does Predictive Performance Translate to Causal Performance? Evaluating tabular foundation models as nuisance learners for causal effect estimation
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models based on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) achieve strong predictive performance, but their value for causal inference is unclear. We evaluated whether PFNs, which predict through in-context learning, could match or outperform conventional nuisance learners in supporting accurate causal estimation and reliable uncertainty quantification (inference). Learners modeled propensity scores and outcome regressions within doubly robust estimators of average causal effects, with and without cross-fitting, across synthetic and semi-synthetic settings with varying confounding complexity and effect heterogeneity. Under simple parametric data-generating processes, the PFNs were competitive with correctly specified parametric regressions and ensembles containing them. In more complex settings, they outperformed all conventional learners evaluated, including richly specified Super Learner ensembles, for both accuracy and uncertainty quantification. As sample size increased, only the two PFN models (TabPFN and Mitra) consistently approached nominal confidence interval coverage, whereas under-coverage persisted for conventional learners. In some settings, PFNs achieved near-nominal coverage and well-calibrated standard errors even without cross-fitting. At the smallest sample size (n=200) and in the higher-dimensional semi-synthetic settings, PFNs and other flexible learners exhibited poor coverage without cross-fitting. For PFNs, this appeared to be driven by propensity score overfitting consistent with in-sample memorization of treatment labels. These findings highlight the promise of prior-data fitted networks as in-context nuisance learners for causal estimation, while underscoring the need for further evaluation in challenging settings.

papers.title: Negative Dynamical Friction in Dark Matter Spikes around Rotating Black Holes
papers.abstract: Dark matter may affect extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) through orbital-energy exchange and a conservative metric response. Here we show that dark matter spikes around rotating massive black holes can drive negative dynamical friction, supplying orbital energy to secondary black holes on stable prograde circular orbits. The energy-gain region extends beyond the innermost stable circular orbit once the black-hole spin exceeds a model-dependent threshold. For an illustrative four-year inspiral with Milky Way--like halo parameters and mass ratio $q=10^{-5}$, the total dynamical-friction contribution produces a phase difference of order $10^2$ radians relative to vacuum. For the same system, the fixed-frequency environmental redshift correction is comparable in magnitude and opposite in sign to the first-order conservative self-force correction. Both environmental energy exchange and the conservative metric response are therefore essential to precision EMRI modeling.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Collapse Prevention with Score-Based Entropy Maximization
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have demonstrated the effectiveness of score-based objectives for generative modeling, yet their potential for self-supervised representation learning remains underexplored. We introduce Entropy-Based Regularization (EBReg), a framework that uses latent score estimation to regularize the latent distribution during self-supervised training. EBReg jointly learns an encoder and a latent score model, and utilizes the learned score to provide a diversity-preserving signal that prevents representational collapse. Motivated by a mutual-information lower bound, we formulate the objective as view alignment with smoothed marginal entropy maximization and optimize the marginal entropy without explicit density evaluation. The same score model can additionally be used at test time to refine corrupted representations toward the training latent distribution. Empirically, EBReg learns competitive representations on ImageNet-1K, achieving 75.57% linear-probe accuracy with ViT-L. Across diverse architectures, score-guided test-time adaptation further improves robustness on ImageNet-C, yielding an average relative accuracy gain of approximately 5%.

papers.title: SegDis: Foreground Segmentation Followed by Type Discrimination for Salient and Camouflaged Object Detection
papers.abstract: Salient and camouflaged object detection (SOD and COD) both recover foreground support, yet most joint methods output only a binary mask and therefore cannot distinguish the type. USC12K distinguishes the two types, but its baseline USCNet still binds foreground existence to the type within a single normalization, so the failure source cannot be attributed. Our cross-task study shows that foreground localization transfers between SOD and COD, whereas type discrimination does not: a COD-only model recovers foreground on SOD images but its type judgement follows the training distribution rather than the foreground-background relation, so the two decisions require separate mechanisms. SegDis factorizes the output into an explicit foreground probability and a conditional type probability given foreground: FLR provides high-quality task-agnostic support, and RTA refines the SOD/COD assignment from the foreground-background relation without a task identifier. Because support is explicit, each ground-truth foreground pixel is classified as correct-type, type-swapped, or missed, so foreground-recovery and type-assignment errors are diagnosed separately. With PVT-v2-B2, SegDis attains 68.98% FG-mIoU and 78.35% mIoU on USC12K at about one-eighth of USCNet's parameters; CSCS is 5.75.

papers.title: Scenario-Based Assessment of Transport Electrification for Low-Carbon Urban Planning: A Case Study of Phu Quoc, Vietnam
papers.abstract: Urban net-zero strategies require a defensible emissions boundary and quantitative estimates of the contribution achievable through individual mitigation measures. This study assesses road-transport electrification within a planned residential development in Phu Quoc, Vietnam, using the assumptions and scenario data of an urban-planning study originally prepared in 2022. A vehicle-class inventory combines population-dependent fleet projections, assumed travel activity, gasoline and diesel consumption, fuel-specific carbon dioxide (CO_2) factors, and electricity-related emissions from battery-electric vehicles. The reference case projects annual road-transport emissions of 59.41, 73.86, and 87.23 tCO_2 for 2022, 2025, and 2030, respectively. Three year-specific substitution scenarios, corresponding to nominal electric-vehicle shares of 25%, 50%, and 100%, yield source-reported avoided emissions of 9.43, 13.64, and 55.41 tCO_2/year, or 15.9%, 18.5%, and 63.5% of their respective baselines. However, a cross-scenario audit identifies an inconsistency in the 2025 mixed-fleet results under time-invariant vehicle-class emission-intensity ratios: under that additional assumption, 2025 avoided emissions would be 23.45 rather than 13.64 tCO_2/year. The original detailed vehicle-energy input tables are not included in the available source document, preventing definitive reconciliation. The study therefore provides a transparent, preliminary planning assessment rather than evidence of citywide net-zero attainment. Its principal value is a reproducible accounting structure and an explicit identification of the data, electricity-system, and infrastructure constraints that must be resolved before policy or investment decisions.

papers.title: Fractional distance-edge-monitoring in lexicographic products
papers.abstract: We give an exact formula for the fractional distance-edge-monitoring number of $G\circ H$, where $G$ is connected of order $m\ge2$ and $H$ has order $n\ge2$. By the previously established endpoint-monitoring property, the fractional monitoring program reduces to fractional vertex cover, whose linear-programming dual is fractional matching. Writing $d_c(H)$ for the critical difference of $H$, we obtain $\operatorname{dem}_{f}(G\circ H)=(mn-D(G,H))/2$, where $D(G,H)=\max_{A\in\mathcal{I}(G)}\bigl(d_c(H)|A|-n|N_G(A)|\bigr)$ and $\mathcal{I}(G)$ denotes the family of all independent sets of $G$, including the empty set, while $N_G(A)$ is the open neighborhood of $A$. This formula characterizes the products attaining $mn/2$ and gives an equality criterion for the fractional matching lower bound of Ma, Cheng, Mao and Wang. Under the stated hypotheses, the lower bound of Ma et al. is attained if and only if either factor has a fractional perfect matching or $H$ is edgeless. Two outer trees show that the factor orders and fractional matching numbers do not determine the product value.

papers.title: Linear Objective Problems: A Complexity Framework for Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Many bilevel and robust optimization problems are complete for the second level of the polynomial hierarchy, but such results are usually proven one problem at a time with problem-specific reductions. A recurring obstacle is that the lower level must select an optimal solution rather than merely a feasible one, whereas standard reductions preserve only whether a solution exists, not which solutions are optimal. We introduce linear objective problems (LOP), a framework for optimization problems whose solutions are explicit subsets of a ground set and whose objective is linear in these elements. We define tight solution-embedding reductions, which map the optimal solutions of one problem element by element onto the optimal solutions of another, without having to recognize optimal solutions, which is coNP-hard in general. This gives a notion of LOP-completeness, with Satisfiability as the canonical complete problem, even with unit weights. We show that many classical problems are LOP-complete, including Vertex Cover, Dominating Set, TSP, Knapsack, and Steiner Tree, and we introduce a duality that transfers LOP-completeness between minimization and maximization problems. As our main application, we prove a meta-theorem for min-max regret optimization under interval uncertainty: for every LOP-complete problem, the min-max regret version is $Σ_2^p$-complete. Instead of a separate proof for each nominal problem, it suffices to show that the nominal problem is LOP-complete. This recovers known results for the interval min-max regret versions of Knapsack and Maximum Benefit Set Cover and yields completeness for over 50 further problems.

papers.title: Small Data Generative AI for Culturally Specific Artistic Creation: A Case Study on the Sonic Space of sarir
papers.abstract: Large-scale generative AI (GenAI) models have become increasingly integrated into contemporary creative practice, yet they often reproduce cultural biases and fail to meaningfully engage with non-Western artistic traditions. In response, this paper explores a small-data approach that foregrounds artist-curated and culturally informed dataset creation and model training. Through a case study on sarir (the distinctive sound produced by the reed pen in Persian calligraphy), we demonstrate how small-data GenAI can operate within a highly situated cultural context that lies beyond the representational reach of large-scale GenAI models. We construct a bespoke sarir audio dataset and train two models, RAVE and StyleGAN2, adapting each to the sonic domain through audio synthesis and spectrogram generation. The resulting models learn the fine-grained timbral and gestural nuances of sarir, enabling both real-time interaction and extended generative output. By comparing these results with state-of-the-art text-to-audio models, we clearly demonstrate the disparity in their performance and highlight the expressive possibilities unlocked through the small data approach. This focused case study demonstrates the feasibility of small-data GenAI for culturally specific artistic creation and underscores the value of further investigations that extend this approach to other cultural materials and artistic domains.

papers.title: Optimal execution in a fractional setting with reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of optimal liquidation with linear market impact, as in the seminal work of Almgren and Chriss, but with an asset driven by a fractional Brownian motion. For $H \neq 1/2$, we observe that the deterministic solution given by Almgren and Chriss is no longer optimal. We develop a strategy to exploit the information induced by the correlation between price increments. The strategy is derived from a policy gradient algorithm, parameterized by a neural network, trained to maximise the CARA utility, for which our method allows for significant improvements.

papers.title: LLM-based Multi-Criteria Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Efficient 5G UPF Selection
papers.abstract: User plane function (UPF) selection in 5G networks is an active area of research, with various limited approaches proposed to enhance network efficiency and manage resources effectively. In this paper, we address this gap in the related literature by proposing a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) UPF selection method that utilizes a dynamic, multi-objective reward function and validating it on a real-world 5G emulation platform. The proposed method is based on the large language models' (LLMs) translation of network operator intents and the network data analytics function (NWDAF) abnormality alerts. The experimental results validated in the real-world experimental setup demonstrate that our dynamic DRL solution achieves an effective balance between latency, power consumption, and traffic distribution, outperforming the heuristic baselines and fixed DRL by 16.89%. These findings highlight the real-world applicability of our approach for dynamic, intent-driven UPF selection.

papers.title: D3Tree: Learning to Prune Block-Diffusion Draft Trees for Efficient Verification
papers.abstract: Block-diffusion drafters propose a whole block of tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees built from their position-wise marginals increase the expected accepted length of speculative decoding. Every tree node occupies a query row in target verification, so under concurrent serving low-yield branches compete with other requests for verification capacity. Existing tree methods select verified nodes by draft probability under a fixed or cost-selected per-request budget, and thus always retain a prefix of the drafter's ranking. We present D3Tree, which learns which nodes of a block-diffusion draft tree are worth verifying. A tree-size head with 2H+2 parameters predicts each candidate's conditional survival from the draft state, the candidate embedding, and its draft log-probability. Thresholding the product of these scores along parent chains yields an ancestor-closed subtree whose size adapts to each request and decoding round. The head is trained on a frozen drafter with conditional labels on the full candidate tree; an optional joint mode also steers the drafter toward the retained reference path. At serving time, D3Tree verifies whole trees under light load and, under heavy load, allocates one batch-wide node budget by predicted survival, sized to the target's matrix-multiplication tiles. Retained trees share one ancestor-masked target pass, while construction, pruning, and scheduling run on the GPU and overlap with the host. Across six vision-language verifiers and 17 text and multimodal benchmarks, D3Tree is fastest in 70 of 72 load settings, with 3.2-4.0x speedup over autoregressive decoding for one request and 1.3-1.8x at 64 concurrent requests, where fixed-budget trees fall below autoregressive speed. Under a time-varying arrival trace, it has the lowest mean end-to-end latency in every arrival phase.

papers.title: A Simple Phase-King Protocol with Predictions
papers.abstract: Inspired by recent work (Ben-David, Dzulfikar, Ellen, and Gilbert, $\textit{Byzantine Agreement with Predictions}$, PODC 2025) we study synchronous binary Byzantine Agreement in the learning-augmented setting, where each process receives predictions about which processes are honest or Byzantine. We present a deterministic Phase King protocol for the anauthenticated setting, combining early stopping with a specifically designed prediction-aware king selection procedure. For at most $t<n/3$ Byzantine processes, the protocol handles arbitrarily many prediction errors, improving upon the $O(n^{3/2})$ bound of Ben-David et al., and terminates within $O(P)$ communication rounds, where $P=1+\min\{\mathbf{B}/n,f\}$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the total number of incorrect prediction bits held by honest processes, and $f$ is the actual number of Byzantine processes. Our protocol uses $O(n^2P)$ messages and $O(n^2P\log n)$ bits, avoiding the initial cubic bit cost of exchanging complete prediction vectors. In comparison to very recent independent work (Dufay, Dzulfikar, and Gilbert, $\textit{Predictions Can Only Help! Communication Efficient Byzantine Agreement with Predictions}$, DISC 2026), which achieves the same error tolerance and round complexity but better communication bounds, our construction provides a much simpler Phase King approach that completely avoids involved preprocessing constructions, rendering it more practical, especially for achieving agreement in time-evolving networks. We believe that the novel prediction-aware king selection technique of our scheme is of independent interest and can find further applications in learning-augmented distributed consensus.

papers.title: Tiling of Hyperbolic Surface by Maximal Number of Tiles
papers.abstract: Tilings of a closed hyperbolic surface by congruent $n$-gons with $n\ge 7$ is a finite problem. One extreme of the finite problem is that the number of tiles is maximal. The problem is related to edge-to-edge tilings of the Poincaré disk ${\bb H}^2$ by congruent $n$-gons, such that all vertices have degree 3 and the vertex sets satisfy certain balance condition. For the special case $n=7$, we show that the heptagon in any such tiling belongs to one of the four families, and tilings of ${\bb H}^2$ by generic heptagons in each family is unique. As a consequence, for any closed hyperbolic surface of Euler characteristic $χ$, we may classify all tilings of the surface by maximal number $-6χ$ of congruent generic heptagons in the four families.

papers.title: BiVerify: Closing the Loop Between Backward and Forward Verification for Mathematical Self-Correction
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have made substantial progress in mathematical reasoning but still produce incorrect solutions to complex problems, indicating the need for more reliable self-correction mechanisms. Mathematical self-correction typically identifies errors through verification, which can proceed backward or forward. The two directions provide complementary verification capabilities. Backward verification checks a candidate answer against the original constraints, bypassing complex intermediate reasoning, but cannot ensure correct reasoning or objective completeness. Forward verification follows the problem conditions and current solution, enabling it to locate reasoning errors and assess objective completeness, but may overlook key constraints in complex solution chains. We propose BiVerify, a dynamically scheduled framework for bidirectional mathematical verification. BiVerify begins with backward verification to screen the answer against the original constraints, followed by forward verification of the reasoning process; subsequent direction switching, state resetting, and re-verification are governed by verification outcomes. Upon failure, the system revises the candidate or verification flow until the same candidate passes both directions. We also introduce shared mathematical tools that separate logical reasoning from precise computation. We systematically evaluate BiVerify on five challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks using multiple mainstream DeepSeek, GPT, and Gemini models. BiVerify exceeds the strongest representative public baseline evaluated in this work by 13.5 percentage points in average accuracy, with the margin reaching 31.2 percentage points on GPT. Further analysis shows that BiVerify's overall performance exceeds that of either verification direction alone.

papers.title: Probing Exotic Electron-Electron Interactions via Adiabatic Spin Inversion in MRFM
papers.abstract: Light bosons beyond the Standard Model can mediate exotic spin-dependent interactions between electrons, motivating sensitive searches at short distances. We propose a magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM) scheme that exploits oscillating-cantilever-driven adiabatic reversals (OSCAR) of electron spins to convert these interactions into measurable mechanical signals. The ferromagnetic tip serves as both a dense polarized-spin source and a source of magnetic-field gradients, enabling force detection without magnetic shielding between the source and sensor. Within a linearized treatment of the coupled spin-mechanical dynamics, we derive resonance-frequency shifts associated with the $V_2$ and $V_3$ interactions and a second-harmonic force signal arising from the velocity-dependent $V_8$ interaction. We further investigate interrupted-OSCAR differential detection and distance-dependent measurements to discriminate exotic signals from conventional magnetic backgrounds. Using representative parameters from ensemble and single-spin MRFM experiments, we estimate the projected sensitivity under specified noise and statistical assumptions. The results suggest that the proposed scheme could provide complementary sensitivity to short-range spin-dependent interactions, with the potential to improve existing constraints on $V_2$ over selected submicrometer interaction ranges. Our study establishes adiabatic spin-inversion MRFM as a promising approach to probing exotic electron-electron forces.

papers.title: Exceptional Points in Scalar Quasinormal Modes of Rastall String-Fluid Black Holes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study exceptional points (EPs) in scalar quasinormal modes(QNMs) of Rastall string-fluid black holes by adding a localized Pöschl--Teller perturbation to the scalar potential, with the bump position $a$ and amplitude $\eb$ serving as independent controls. We solve the hyperboloidal problem with two-domain Chebyshev collocation and arbitrary-precision linear algebra, and use the complex discriminant, eigenvector coalescence, Jordan-chain residuals, square-root splitting and closed-loop mode exchange as complementary tests of defectiveness. For the regular $A=1$, $\eR=-1$ branch, the two-parameter search locates a resolution-stable second-order EP from $N=24$ to $N=60$, while constrained semidiscrete evolution gives the Jordan response $(C+Dt)e^{\iiω_{\rm EP}t}$. For the logarithmic $A=2$ branch, defective points occur in each finite truncation but their coordinates do not converge, so we make no continuum claim for this branch.

papers.title: MG-Cache: Multi-Granularity Caching for Accelerating Diffusion Transformer Inference
papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformer (DiT) models, while having become a powerful backbone for generative synthesis, suffer from high inference cost on generating high-resolution images. Diffusion caching has emerged as a promising acceleration technique to reduce inference cost. However, existing caching strategies fail to accurately identify the varying importance of different computational modules and rarely coordinate cache reusing across the timestep and layer granularities, making it difficult to control error accumulation. To address these limitations, we propose multi-granularity caching (MG-Cache) for DiTs, a novel and fully training-free approach to exploit computational redundancy both on timesteps and Transformer layers. Our core innovation contains a two-stage caching strategy: an offline timestep profiling analysis that identifies redundant timesteps for cache reuse, followed by an adaptive layer-wise caching strategy that combines input stability with importance of each Transformer layer to selectively cache stable Attention and MLP submodules. Extensive experiments on mainstream open-source DiT models validate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving significant acceleration while maintaining high fidelity to the uncached output, with up to a 4.18x acceleration on HunyuanVideo.

papers.title: OOM: Offload-Optimized Full-Parameter MoE Training via Memory-Execution Co-Design
papers.abstract: Offloading model state to host memory and streaming layer weights let a single multi-GPU node train large mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. GPU memory then becomes a performance budget, shared by resident expert state, retained activations, and execution worksets. The best allocation depends on the expert execution path, batch size, and sequence length. We present OOM (Offload-Optimized MoE), a full-parameter MoE training system that co-designs expert execution and memory allocation. For expert-parallel execution, OOM updates resident experts on their owning GPUs and jointly plans state residency and MoE activation retention according to pipeline dependencies. For local execution, OOM bounds GPU worksets through dependency-aware partitioning; in hybrid models, it also retains attention results on the host to avoid costly recomputation and selectively regenerates layer boundaries through cheaper layers to make room. Calibrated cost models guide joint configuration within GPU and host budgets to minimize step time; OOM selects among the configured paths through short executions. On four H100s, OOM trains with 1M-token contexts, whereas FSDP2, ZeRO-Offload, and MegaTrain exhaust GPU memory at 512K. It also trains a 122B-parameter MoE model, on which all three exhaust host memory. On four 24 GB RTX 4090s, it trains 512K-token contexts and 1,024 1K-token sequences per step without gradient accumulation. Across matched-global-batch comparisons, OOM delivers 1.58x and 4.08x geometric-mean (up to 2.14x and 7.77x) throughput over CPU-offloaded FSDP2 on the two platforms while using the least host memory among the evaluated systems -- as little as 1/3.0 of FSDP2's.

papers.title: Sections of the Kottwitz homomorphism and affine pinnings
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group split over $\mathbb{Z}$. The Kottwitz homomorphism identifies the group of connected components of the loop group of $G$ with the group $Ω$ of length zero elements of the extended affine Weyl group. We show that this homomorphism always has a homomorphic section, and that the section can be chosen inside the normalizer of $T$ in $G(\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}])$. We then ask whether the section can be chosen to preserve an affine pinning. This is possible if no simple factor of $G$ is of type $B_{2m}$ or $C_{2m}$. It is impossible for $(SL_2\times Sp_{2n})/μ_2$ and $(SL_2\times Spin_{2n+1})/μ_2$ when $n$ is even. We show that the obstructions for $G$ and for its Langlands dual group are dual to each other, and we compute them by a lattice computation with a Coxeter element. As an application, we show that the component group of the centralizer of any semisimple element lifts to the centralizer. Under the same condition on the simple factors, the lift can be chosen to preserve a pinning of the neutral component.

papers.title: Fundamental Groups of Permutation Complexes
papers.abstract: We present an elementary argument showing that fundamental groups of permutation complexes are free. Hence, $\mathbb{R} P^2$ cannot be realized by a permutation complex, answering a question of Chachólski, Levi and Meshulam.

papers.title: Uncertainty principle on $\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: This paper establishes an uncertainty principle on the mixed space $\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ for $n \ge 2$. Leveraging the paraboloid restriction theorem on $\mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ derived from Barron's global-in-time Strichartz estimates for the semi-periodic Schrodinger equation, we construct measurable sets $S \subset \mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ and $A(R,δ) \subset \mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ that form a strong $L^2$ annihilating pair, satisfying the uniform inequality $\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)} \le 3(\|f\|_{L^2((\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)\setminus S)} + \|\widehat{f}\|_{L^2((\mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)\setminus A(R,δ))})$ for all $f \in L^2(\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)$, where the measures of $S$ and $A(R,δ)$ can be made arbitrarily large while the constant 3 remains unchanged. As an application, we derive a two-time observability inequality for the semi-periodic Schrodinger equation under a support condition on the phase-modified solution at the first observation time.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Axisymmetric Vortices in the Magnetic Ginzburg-Landau Equations
papers.abstract: We study vortex solutions of the magnetic Ginzburg-Landau model (or the Abelian-Higgs model). We establish uniqueness of axisymmetric vortex solutions for every winding number $n\geq1$ and coupling constant $λ>0$. Our proof uses a lattice inequality and constrained minimization to construct a positive radial solution lying above any two given radial solutions. A comparison argument based on the virial identity then establishes uniqueness. We further prove that the unique radial solution depends real analytically on $λ$ and that both radial profiles are strictly increasing with respect to $λ$.

papers.title: NuJEV: Structured Visual Judgments for Consistent Nuclei Quantification
papers.abstract: Nuclear quantification requires locating and typing nuclei, beyond generating a count. Inspired by Jev's structured decisions in place of free-form generation, we introduce NuJEV for nuclear perception in Qwen3-VL-2B. We jointly train visual LoRA and a parallel head to predict nuclear presence, centers, and types. One image encoding feeds both the nuclear head and original language decoder. The decoder interprets region and type requests, with counts computed from the predicted nuclei. On 2,732 PanNuke test images, NuJEV achieves a five-query mean absolute error ($\mathrm{MAE}_5$) of 1.844 overall and 5.268 on dense images, with localization/typed F1 of 0.816/0.682. A matched encoder ablation shows 41.0\% lower dense error with visual adaptation. For language requests, NuJEV reduces request MAE by 76.2\% relative to direct generation. Our code will be released as open source.

papers.title: Persistence landscape velocity: Closed formulas and a topological probe of quantum criticality
papers.abstract: We introduce the landscape velocity $ξ$, a scalar measure of variation of a parameter-dependent persistence landscape. For families of finite barcodes whose bars are all born at the fixed filtration value $0$, we show that $ξ$ is the $L^2$ speed of the landscape curve where the sorted death times are differentiable and derive an exact closed formula that requires no persistence landscape at all: the death times of the barcodes, as functions of the parameter, suffice. For the velocity of the empirical mean of several landscapes we also prove a closed formula which, again, strikingly requires neither the empirical mean landscape nor any of the individual landscapes, only the individual barcodes. As an application, we revisit Olsthoorn's persistent homology analysis of the transverse-field Ising chain. Whereas his approach uses different homology degrees and summaries depending on the boundary conditions, ours uses $H_0$ only and a single rule: the position of the maximum of $ξ$. This rule locates the quantum critical point for both periodic and open boundary conditions, and for both mutual-information and correlator-based dissimilarities. The position of the maximum converges to the critical point faster than all the estimators we can extract from Olsthoorn's work. In the 4 scenarios considered (different boundary conditions and different dissimilarity matrices), the peak of the normalized velocity becomes increasingly pronounced with system size, with observed logarithmic growth. This logarithmic growth is proved for periodic boundaries with correlator dissimilarity under stated hypotheses, identifying landscape velocity as a singular topological response to quantum criticality.

papers.title: A divisorial domain with non-Prüfer normalization
papers.abstract: We answer a 1968 question of Heinzer by constructing a two-dimensional local divisorial domain whose normalization is not Prüfer.

papers.title: What an Observer Reads off a Holographic Screen
papers.abstract: What does an observer read off a holographic screen that is an array of qubits rather than a surface? In the generalized holographic principle the interaction between two separable systems acts on such a screen as a weighted sum, up to an overall prefactor, of commuting observables with values plus and minus one. When the weights are nonnegative and the prefactor is one and the joint eigenspaces are lines, everything a probe reads off the spectrum depends only on the list of weights, which we call the profile. On the screen with equal weights summing to one the running dimension read by a diffusion probe falls short of two at unit time by at most twice the reciprocal of the number of qubits; a geometric profile gives instead, through its level count, a plateau of any positive height. An observer correlates sets of qubits; its readout carries a profile at a given weighting when the levels it reads, counted with multiplicity, are those of a screen with one weight per set. We prove that a readout carries a profile at every weighting exactly when the distinct nonzero traces of its qubits are linearly independent over the field with two elements, the trace of a qubit being the list of sets that contain it; such a readout is a partition of the qubits it covers up to an invertible recoding, and a dependent one carries a profile only on finitely many proper linear subspaces of weightings. Refining a grouping without end builds a tower whose boundary is a profinite set and hence a condensed set, on which a strictly positive compatible profile separates the locally constant functions by a distance. Applications certify probabilistic and strong contextuality and give the leading shortfall of the distance between the poles of the fuzzy sphere; in a model of monogamous entanglement the pairs that weight-one threads representing operational ER=EPR can occupy at once are exactly the partial matchings.

papers.title: Attacking Slide Puzzle CAPTCHAs Based on Time and Space Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.abstract: CAPTCHAs can protect websites from malicious attacks. As a typical representative of behavior CAPTCHAs, slide puzzle CAPTCHAs have become increasingly popular in recent years due to their user-friendliness and high security. Previous attack methods on slide puzzle CAPTCHA mainly face challenges in the following four aspects. (1) The defense mechanisms of previous slide puzzle CAPTCHAs were relatively simple. The current slide puzzle CAPTCHAs have added complex interferences, detected slide trajectory features in the two-dimensional space, and added other defense mechanisms. (2) The previous notch detection methods were difficult to accurately locate the notch positions. (3) Previous attack trajectories were limited to the horizontal dimension, making them impossible to pass the existing detection. (4) The previous attack trajectories were generated by fitting functions, which were relatively simple and could not well simulate the slide characteristics of human users. In response to the above challenges, firstly, we systematically analyze the defense strategies of six most popular slide puzzle CAPTCHAs: Capy, Dingxiang, Geetest, Kyger, Shumei and Tencent. Secondly, for each type of CAPTCHA, we construct a notch detection dataset and a slide trajectory dataset separately. Thirdly, we use advanced YOLOv11 to detect the notch positions and train generative adversarial networks (GAN) to generate attack trajectories. As far as we know, we are the first to generate attack trajectories by directly learning human slide trajectory characteristic. According to the experimental results, this method cracked six most popular slide puzzle CAPTCHAs with success rates of over 90\%, and the attack time is only about 5 seconds, indicating that the security of existing slide puzzle CAPTCHAs is facing challenge. At the same time, we propose various methods to enhance the security of slide puzzle CAPTCHAs.

papers.title: An Adaptive Short-Step Variant of BroxGD with Linear Convergence under Quadratic Growth
papers.abstract: Broximal Gradient Descent (BroxGD), recently analyzed by Richtárik et al. (arXiv:2605.08850v1), is a projection-free sister method to Projected Gradient Descent (ProjGD) for solving $\min_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)$, where $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ and $\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ is nonempty, closed and convex. The method performs local linear minimization over the feasible set intersected with a Euclidean ball and carefully prescribed radius. Like ProjGD, BroxGD enjoys linear convergence in the smooth strongly convex setting, with the same condition-number dependence. However, the known radius rule leading to linear convergence requires unavailable information and is therefore impractical. We develop an adaptive short-step variant of BroxGD which converges linearly for smooth convex functions under quadratic growth (generalizing strong convexity), without requiring unavailable information. We use $$z_k\in\arg\min_{z\in\mathcal X\cap\mathbb B(x_k,t_k)}\langle\nabla f(x_k),z\rangle,\quad x_{k+1}=\mathrm{Proj}_{S_k}(x_k-\nabla f(x_k)/L),$$ where $L$ is the smoothness constant of $f$, $\mathbb B(x,t)$ is the Euclidean ball centered at $x$ of radius $t$, and $S_k$ is the line segment connecting $x_k$ and $z_k$. The radius is updated by $t_{k+1}=\max\{\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|,t_k/2\}$. Projection onto $S_k$ requires only scalar clipping. Assuming an exact local linear minimization oracle, each update uses one oracle call. For any positive initial radius, we bound all oracle calls to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ and obtain $O((L/α)\log(1/\varepsilon))$ for fixed initialization, where $α=\min\{α_0,L\}$ and $α_0>0$ is the quadratic-growth constant.

papers.title: Crystal and magnetic structures of MnSi in zero magnetic field: Neutron diffraction and symmetry analysis
papers.abstract: Combining high-resolution wide-angle neutron powder diffraction with magnetic-superspace symmetry analysis, we refine the crystal structure and present, to our knowledge, the first systematic refinement of cubic $P2_13$ MnSi's zero-field magnetic structure across multiple magnetic satellite families. We compare single-arm rhombohedral 3+1D and cubic four-arm 3+4D magnetic superspace-group (MSSG) descriptions with propagation vectors along $\langle111\rangle$. Simultaneous extinction of the two satellite groups around $\{100\}$ dictates a transverse circular-helix model. This suppression and refinements of 18 separately varied satellite-group intensities support this ideal limit with only one adjustable magnetic amplitude. In the ideal single-arm model with MSSG $R3.1'(0,0,g)ts$, the moment has constant magnitude 0.535(3) $μ_B$ per Mn. An explicit four-arm 3+4D cubic superspace construction presented here combines four interpenetrating helices and, for the illustrated phase choice, has moments ranging from zero to 0.874(5) $μ_B$ per Mn, with the same root-mean-square moment as the 3+1D structure. Their identical powder profiles prevent the present measurements from distinguishing them. The average crystal structure remains cubic within experimental resolution, providing structural motivation for the cubic magnetic model. The mean lattice parameter, determined with formal relative precision $σ_a/a \lesssim 10^{-5}$, exhibits nonmonotonic temperature dependence below the Néel temperature.

papers.title: Zero forcing is not unimodal
papers.abstract: The zero forcing polynomial of a graph counts the number of distinct zero forcing sets of every possible size. In 2018, Boyer et al. asked whether the zero forcing polynomial is always unimodal, and provided some evidence that it is. We answer this question by constructing an infinite family of graphs whose zero forcing polynomials are not unimodal. Our construction also shows that the graph polynomials associated with connected forcing and total forcing are also not unimodal in general.

papers.title: The Fate of Collisional Neutrino Flavor Conversion: Fixed Points, Period Doubling, and Chaos
papers.abstract: Core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers are among the most energetic astrophysical events and promising sources of multimessenger signals. Their dynamics and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino transport, yet the impact of neutrino flavor evolution in these dense environments remains poorly understood. Predicting the outcome of collisional flavor instability (CFI) remains a challenge, despite progress in local-relaxation methods for fast flavor conversion. Here we construct homogeneous collective-precession states with stationary flavor populations in two-flavor quantum kinetics with collisional relaxation. The method applies to arbitrary energy spectra and energy-dependent collision rates. Our numerical examples exhibit persistent oscillations and a period-doubling route to chaos. Even in these regimes, the stationary populations estimate the time-averaged flavor populations to within $10\%$ in our tests. These fixed points provide a physically motivated input for incorporating CFI into astrophysical simulations, with implications for neutrino heating and ejecta nucleosynthesis.

papers.title: Financial Connectedness: Heavy Tails andResponse Attribution
papers.abstract: A financial market can appear mainly dependent on its own shocks under a variance account and mainly dependent on external shocks under a cumulative-response account. We establish how these opposite diagnoses arise from the same propagation system. For a given cumulative magnitude, squaring gives greater weight to responses concentrated across sources and time. Source priorities can therefore reverse even in stable Gaussian systems with known parameters. Heavy tails raise a separate question: whether the reported shares have a fixed population basis. One innovation with an infinite second moment removes the full network's finite covariance input. We characterize when normalized shares nevertheless stabilize and construct rank-amplitude connectedness, a cumulative-deviation target without finite first or second moments. It can be consistently estimated under local dependence and identification conditions. With fitted dynamics and rank scatter fixed, changing attribution replaces 3.14 names in the daily Top 10 of forty stocks, selecting recipients with greater external persistence relative to their own adjustment. In five futures contracts, mean external share rises from 28.0% to 55.9%, and 70.9% of recipient-dates switch from own to external dominance.

papers.title: AOP-Smart-Finder: A High-Throughput Human-AI Hybrid Framework for AOP Discovery and Evidence Mapping from Large-Scale Literature
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of scientific literature and the high heterogeneity of biological terminology and mechanistic descriptions make it difficult for researchers to integrate scattered research evidence, identify connections among biological events, and construct mechanistic networks. Here, we developed a high-throughput human-AI hybrid framework, AOP-Smart-Finder, for biological event discovery, relationship mining, and Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) construction and evidence mapping from large-scale literature. This framework integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), AOP-Smart retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology, and Python-based automation, supporting two analysis modes: one based on a single compound and the other based on a predefined set of biological events. In the di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) case, the system processed 12,983 articles within 30 min and included 1,093 of them, from which it extracted 1,589 biological events (including 458 official key events [KEs] and 1,131 candidate KEs) and 2,519 key event relationships (KERs). In the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) case, the system identified 55 stressors from 437 articles and extracted 278 biological events and 548 event relationships. Following manual curation and Weight of Evidence (WoE) evaluation, a mechanistic network comprising 16 KEs and 23 KERs was ultimately constructed. This framework can either use existing AOPs as knowledge guidance for mechanistic expansion and evidence supplementation, or discover novel event connections and construct mechanistic networks around user-specified research topics. It provides a high-throughput, traceable, human-AI hybrid methodology for complex biological mechanism elucidation and AOP discovery driven by large-scale literature.

papers.title: Separation of Skilling Context for Standard Operating Procedure-based Agents
papers.abstract: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are kept concise for human readability, so LLM agents that generate executable skills from them lack the tacit knowledge and implementation details needed for automation. Human intervention fills these gaps, but must be repeated as SOPs evolve---a problem we call \textit{SOP-skill drift}. We propose managing SOPs and Contextual Knowledge (CK) separately, together with a \textit{contract-aware} evaluation that distinguishes genuine violations from CK-resolved differences. On eight Indeed-derived workflows (single LLM), it raises the functional-equivalence rate from 12\% to 58\%. Under three SOP-revision perturbations, previously extracted CK already covers 79.5\% of newly introduced automation gaps.

papers.title: Elliptic flow of $ϕ$ and $Ω$ via quark recombination mechanism in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract: Multi-strange hadrons, such as the $ϕ$ meson and $Ω$ baryon, serve as unique probes for the properties of the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Using a quark recombination model with the quark phase-space information parameterized in a viscous blastwave, we show that the elliptic flow $v_2$ of $ϕ$ and $Ω$ can be describled by quark recombination in a wide energy range from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV. We check the scaling properties of $v_2$ of $ϕ$ and $Ω$ and find the number-of-constituent-quark (NCQ) scaled $v_2$ of $ϕ$ and $Ω$ are approximately equal. We further present the $v_2$ of strange quarks at hadronization extracted from $ϕ$ and $Ω$ data. We find the $v_2$ of strange quarks is close to the NCQ-scaled $v_2$ of $ϕ$ and $Ω$ at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7-200 GeV, but significant larger than the latter at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.76-5.02 TeV, suggesting that the $v_2$ of strange quarks cannot be simply equated to the NCQ-scaled $v_2$ of $ϕ$ and $Ω$. Our results demonstrate that the quark recombination mechanism is valid for $ϕ$ and $Ω$ production in heavy-ion collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV, indicating the existence of constituent quark degree of freedom at these energies.

papers.title: IntentLens: Grounding Underspecified Multimodal Queries for Recommendation via Tool-Augmented Reasoning
papers.abstract: As intelligent personal assistants are increasingly deployed in real-world scenarios, recommendation paradigms are shifting from passive preference matching to inferring user intent from underspecified multimodal inputs. In practical interactions, users typically issue a reference image paired with a vague natural language query, keeping key visual attributes, personalized preferences, and item-side constraints implicit. Existing recommendation methods either leverage historical user interactions augmented with multimodal item features or assume fully articulated textual queries; both paradigms struggle to resolve underspecified multimodal queries for accurate item matching. To address this limitation, we propose IntentLens, a tool-augmented recommendation framework that grounds ambiguous multimodal queries into query-relevant evidence prior to user-item matching. IntentLens follows a ground-then-rank pipeline: a shared multimodal LLM leverages visual tools, user memory modules, and item attribute retrieval tools to (i) infer latent user intent from image-text inputs and (ii) augment each candidate item with fine-grained, query-conditioned evidence. Subsequently, a lightweight ranker scores candidates based on the grounded representations. To facilitate research in this novel setting, we construct two benchmarks with underspecified multimodal queries, namely \textsc{GoogleReview-MMTool} and \textsc{Yelp-MMTool}. Extensive experiments on these benchmarks demonstrate that IntentLens outperforms competitive MLLM and retrieval baselines, and exhibits strong generalization to unseen categories and datasets.

papers.title: Extremal graphs for Alon's graph coupon-collector conjecture
papers.abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite simple graph without isolated vertices. Starting with every vertex uncovered, at each step sample a vertex uniformly and independently and cover one of its uncovered neighbors, chosen uniformly, if any. Let \(\cc(G)\) denote the expected number of steps required to cover all vertices. Alon conjectured that disjoint unions of \(K_{d+1}\) maximize \(\cc(G)\) among \(d\)-regular graphs of a prescribed order whenever such unions exist. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture for every fixed \(d\ge2\) and give a complete characterization of the extremal graphs for \(d=2\) at every order \(n\ge3\). In particular, all but at most six vertices of any such extremal graph lie in four-cycle components.

papers.title: Spatial Harness: Grounding Spatial Reasoning in Executable World States with Physics Engines
papers.abstract: Spatial reasoning requires understanding how objects and observers are arranged in a scene and how their relations change with viewpoint or movement. Vision-language models (VLMs) typically perform both steps through model-internal reasoning, forming an implicit scene interpretation from partial views and imagining the consequences of spatial transformations. A misread scene can lead to a wrong answer, while even a correct interpretation does not ensure that imagined transformations satisfy spatial constraints. We introduce Spatial Harness, which represents scenes as explicit and executable world states to ground spatial reasoning in physics-engine feedback. A Perceiver integrates scene constraints extracted from the question with specialized visual estimates to place objects and cameras in a shared coordinate frame. The resulting state is instantiated in a physics engine, where a Reasoner executes viewpoint changes and uses computed measurements and rendered views to guide reasoning. We evaluate on MindCube, SAT, MMSI-Bench, and SpatialRGPT-Bench with open- and closed-weight VLMs. On MindCube, Spatial Harness improves Qwen3.5-27B from 52.70% to 71.14%, surpassing pySpatial by 7.52 percentage points. Given identical annotated object and camera poses, it reaches 98.25% versus 71.81% for model-internal reasoning. Code is publicly available at: https://github.com/tmlr-group/Spatial-Harness

papers.title: Ergotropy as distance from equilibrium
papers.abstract: We show that the ergotropy (a.k.a available energy) of a thermally isolated system is the $1$-Wasserstein distance between two energy probability density functions. Specifically, between the energy profile of the system state, and the energy profile of its associated passive state. We prove this for both classical and quantum systems, and illustrate it with examples. Our result formalises the intuition that ergotropy is a quantifier of distance from equilibrium

papers.title: Agent Self-Improvement with Frozen Weights: The Added Value and Limits of Failure Traces
papers.abstract: We evaluate whether an AI agent's harness, the notes around its model, can learn from the agent's failure traces beyond a matched search that never sees them. It can, but less than it looks. We tested an open 9-billion-parameter model with fixed weights; a larger teacher model wrote its notes. On generated customer-service decisions, where both note writers were told the target rules, notes based on the agent's mistakes improved accuracy by 4.0 percentage points over notes from the same process with the mistakes withheld. That process alone, trying and keeping better-scoring notes, reached about 60% of the total improvement. In full customer-service conversations the same notes showed no demonstrated improvement. Separately, a strict screen of single lessons admitted two customer-service lessons, still awaiting tests on new data, and one tool-use lesson, written without seeing the agent's mistakes, which showed no demonstrated gain on new tool-use tasks. A neutral note with no procedure scored higher than the learned lessons (exploratory). A blind audit judged 146 of 240 tool-use test items defective.

papers.title: On quantitative aspects of ideal membership certificate and GCD inequality for polynomials evaluated at almost units
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain an effective bounds for the ideal membership certificate in polynomial rings over almost all rings of S-integers, thereby generalizing results of Aschenbrenner and Evertse and Gyory. We also establish an effective refinement of a result of Xiao, building on earlier work of Levin and Corvaja and Zannier. In particular, we provide explicit bounds for both the number and the total degrees of the exceptional hypersurfaces arising in an inequality that bounds the greatest common divisor of multivariable polynomials evaluated at almost S-units under consideration. As an application of our results, we obtain an effective refinement of a theorem of Corvaja and Zannier: Let $(F_n)_n$ and $(G_n)_n$ be two linear recurrence sequences and $\mathcal{N}$ be the set of positive integers $n$ such that $F_n/G_n$ is an integer. Hadamard quotient theorem, conjectured by Pisot and proven by Van der Poorten states that if the set $\mathcal{N}$ coincides with $\mathbb{N}$ then $\left(F_n/G_n\right)_n$ is itself linear recurrence sequence. Corvaja-Zannier proved that if $\mathcal{N}$ is infinite set, then there exists a nonzero polynomial $P(X)$ such that $\left( P(n)F_n/G_n\right)_n$ agrees with a linear recurrence sequence for all $n$ in a suitable arithmetic progression. We give an explicit bound $C$, depending explicitly on the parameters of the recurrence sequences such that, the conclusion holds if $\mathcal{N}$ contains at least $C$ elements.

papers.title: Agentic Attribution of Cloud Resource Ownership
papers.abstract: Security tools raise findings across cloud environments, and AI agents now investigate and prioritize them. A finding is still resolved by people: it has to reach the people responsible for fixing it and accountable for the resource it concerns. Ownership is the organizational context that decides who that is. Where recorded, it is declared by hand in configuration management databases or owner tags and goes stale unless kept current; accounts are shared, and automation creates much of the infrastructure. The knowledge sits in work records, code history, audit logs and identity directories, encoded in each organization's own conventions. Recovering it poses four challenges: the signal is scattered across sources, none of them authoritative; the conventions that carry it differ between organizations; reaching an owner takes multi-hop links; and those related to a resource differ in the strength of their relation. We define ownership as a set of entities, people or teams, each related to the resource by one of five patterns ordered by strength. We present a reference architecture for agentic ownership attribution that derives ownership from these records instead of declaring it: it profiles an organization offline into tested signal procedures and an ownership playbook, then attributes each resource with a coordinator agent and parallel investigators, with confidence computed by rules. On 100 resources of 50 Amazon Web Services (AWS) resource types in one organization, we pool the architecture's candidates with those of an unprimed general-purpose agent and verify every evidence piece against the records. The architecture reaches 92.1% weighted recall and 86.6% weighted precision, against 54.8% and 77.4%, at 0.55 times the agent's cost per unit of coverage. The difference lies in people who build and change resources without an explicit owner, found through work records and code history.

papers.title: Visualizing d-wave pairing symmetry at the atomic scale in a cuprate high-Tc superconductor by Josephson tunneling
papers.abstract: Superconducting pairing symmetry provides crucial insight into the microscopic mechanisms of Cooper pairing. However, probing the local manifestations of sign-changing superconducting order parameters remains experimentally challenging. Here, we investigate the superconducting condensate in optimally doped (OPT) Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O10+δ (Bi-2223) using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), equipped with an s-wave superconducting tip. Measurements at ultra-low temperatures reveal a pronounced modulation of the Josephson tunneling signal at different locations inside the crystallographic unit cell. A distinct Josephson tunneling signal is detected above O sites in the underlying CuO2 plane, whereas the signal nearly vanishes above the Cu-plaquette diagonals, including Cu sites and plaquette centers. This unique intra-unit-cell spatial pattern agrees with the theoretical prediction for the symmetry-dependent cancellation of Josephson tunneling between an s-wave superconducting tip and a d-wave superconducting sample. Our findings provide atomic-scale, real-space evidence for d-wave pairing symmetry in OPT high-Tc Bi-2223 and establish SJTM as a powerful approach for investigating the pairing symmetry of unconventional superconductors.

papers.title: Gamma classes, central connection matrices, and tt* geometry
papers.abstract: We review the gamma class of complex projective space, but from the point of view of topological-antitopological fusion. We deconstruct the central connection matrix which appears in the work of Dubrovin, Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani, and Cotti-Dubrovin-Guzzetti.

papers.title: OPSRL-SSP: Optimistic Posterior Sampling for Stochastic Shortest Path with Minimax-Optimal Regret
papers.abstract: We study online reinforcement learning for the stochastic shortest path (SSP) problem with unknown transition dynamics. Although existing posterior-sampling methods perform well empirically on SSPs, their regret guarantees do not achieve the minimax-optimal order. We address this limitation by proposing OPSRL-SSP, an optimistic posterior-sampling algorithm for the SSP setting. The algorithm operates in epochs and uses a logarithmic, time-dependent schedule for the number of posterior samples. To induce optimism, we augment the transition model with a pseudo-state assigned an optimistic boundary value. We establish a high-probability regret bound of $\tilde{O}(B_\star \sqrt{SAK} + B_\star S^2 A)$, where $B_\star$ is an upper bound on the expected cost of the optimal policy, $S$ and $A$ are the numbers of states and actions, respectively, and $K$ is the number of episodes. In addition, we extend the analysis to general zero-cost SSPs using a universal cost-perturbation argument. The leading term matches the minimax lower bound $Ω(B_\star \sqrt{SAK})$, thereby addressing the open problem raised by Jafarnia-Jahromi et al. [19] for posterior sampling in the SSP setting.

papers.title: Where Should a Gate Look? Input vs. State Gating in Diagonal State Space Models
papers.abstract: Modern state-space models owe much of their computational efficiency to their linear, often diagonal, dynamics. Classical recurrent neural networks instead allow nonlinear state-to-state interactions, which can be beneficial when memory updates need to depend on the past context. In this paper, we ask whether state feedback through a simple gate regulating memory updates can enhance the expressivity of diagonal state-space models. To investigate this question, we compare gates that depend on the current input, the recurrent state, or both. We establish a strict expressivity separation: for scalar models, state gating solves induction-head tasks for arbitrary vocabulary size and sequence length, whereas input gating fails on a finite instance under standard stability assumptions on the state transition matrix. Experiments show that state gating retains its advantage on induction-head tasks in higher-dimensional models, whereas input gating performs better on selective copying tasks. Together, our results show that even a simple, diagonal form of state-feedback gating can unlock capabilities unavailable to input-controlled models, while input and state gating offer complementary strengths and achieve the strongest overall performance when combined.
