The proposed framework is supported by asymptotic theory showing that the type I error rate converges to the nominal level under regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method maintains reliable type I error control across a range of settings, including contaminated data and small pilot sample sizes. Compared with existing blinded and unblinded methods, the proposed framework is more flexible and less sensitive to outliers. A clinical trial application illustrates its practical utility.

papers.title: Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning for an Options Market Maker: An Empirical Study with Real S&P 500 Options
papers.abstract: Options market makers absorb client order flow and must hedge the resulting inventory risk under trading frictions. We study whether an option hedging reinforcement learning (RL) agent trained on historical market data outperforms three alternatives in tail-risk protection: (i) traditional delta hedging, (ii) simple hedge-ratio rules, and (iii) the same agent trained in simulated markets. Most RL hedging agents are trained in model-generated markets that do not capture the crashes and volatility regimes present in real data. We introduce an empirical replay environment using S&P 500 option data from 1996 to 2017 and compare against a matched geometric Brownian motion (GBM) environment, a stochastic-volatility (SABR) simulator, and a hybrid that values historical paths with Black-Scholes, all sharing the same portfolio mechanics, stochastic arrivals, costs, and test period. We train a distributional Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) agent and evaluate it out of sample over 2018-2023. The agent trained on empirical data reduces Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) tail loss by 3.1% compared to delta hedging and outperforms every hedge-ratio rule chosen during the training period and every alternative training environment. The reduction reaches 8.9% in volatile and falling markets, but reverses to a cost of 7-10% in rising markets. Empirical training induces a state-dependent short net delta: the policy under-hedges negative-delta books, most strongly after prices have fallen. This tilt disappears with GBM training and is weaker with SABR or hybrid training. These findings suggest that exposure to historical market dynamics can materially change a tail-risk hedging policy, although the evidence rests on a single test path and the edge is regime-conditional.

papers.title: Causal Outcome Learning with Noisy Proxies
papers.abstract: Modern observational biomedical datasets contain increasingly extensive baseline and outcome measurements, yet detecting a clinically meaningful treatment effect remains difficult because investigators must identify an outcome that captures treatment response while adjusting for confounding distributed across numerous noisy baseline variables. We introduce SCOUT (Score-based Causal Outcome Learning Using Treatment signals), a framework that learns a clinically interpretable, treatment-responsive outcome while adjusting for confounding throughout the learning process. SCOUT constructs low-dimensional adjustment representations of high-dimensional baseline measurements to estimate the average treatment effect (ATE) and conditional average treatment effect (CATE) for the learned outcome. Importantly, the final adjustment space is at most two-dimensional, allowing treatment-effect heterogeneity to be estimated in this space rather than in the full high-dimensional covariate space. SCOUT also introduces a fourth-order statistic for testing treatment-effect heterogeneity that emphasizes unusually large deviations from the ATE. In synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments, the algorithm achieved competitive ATE estimation accuracy and substantially lower CATE estimation error. In an observational study of patients with bipolar disorder, SCOUT identified a clinically recognizable lithium-associated adverse-effect profile, detecting both a significant ATE (Holm-adjusted $p$ = 0.0026) and significant treatment-effect heterogeneity (Holm-adjusted $p$ = 0.033).These results demonstrate how jointly learning outcomes and controlling for confounding can facilitate the discovery of treatment effects in high-dimensional observational data.

papers.title: MPSi: Neural Extraction of Site-Specific Multipath Propagation Properties for Massive MIMO
papers.abstract: Accurate extraction of site-specific multipath propagation properties enables a wide range of wireless applications, including initial access, wideband channel reconstruction, and the generation of channel datasets for learning-based and continual-learning systems. Classical parametric channel-sounding algorithms such as RIMAX provide physically interpretable estimates, but their data-dependent model-order selection and iterative nonlinear refinement introduce substantial delay and computational cost. This paper proposes MPSi, a physics-guided neural framework that replaces these costly stages with a compact path-count network and a fixed-depth, deep-unfolded Levenberg-Marquardt refinement. MPSi estimates the complex gain, angle of arrival, and propagation delay of each multipath component while preserving the underlying physical channel model. We evaluate MPSi in two site-specific ray-traced environments, a small cell and a dense urban area, and show that it achieves initial-access and full-channel-estimation performance comparable to an enhanced RIMAX baseline while requiring significantly fewer optimization iterations. The reconstructed channels also yield bit-error-rate performance close to the perfect-channel knowledge reference. These results position MPSi as a promising low-overhead framework for extracting multipath propagation properties in massive-MIMO systems and for generating cell-specific channel pseudo-labels for training when direct ground-truth measurements are unavailable.

papers.title: Dominant permutations, positive mixed-variable formulas, and product-splitting equivalence for (double) Schubert polynomials
papers.abstract: We present new positive combinatorial formulas for triple Schubert coefficients in mixed-variable products of double Schubert polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_u(x;y)\mathfrak{S}_v(x;z)$, expressed in the $\mathfrak{S}_w(x;y)$ basis, in the case where $u$ is dominant. This result complements earlier results where $v$ was assumed dominant. To generalize further, we introduce a relation on permutations that we call ``domination,'' under which dominant permutations dominate all others. When $u$ dominates $w$, we obtain an explicit positive formula for $c^w_{u,v}(y;z)$, which in particular yields positivity when $u$ and $v$ have separated descents. In addition to these new positivity results, we establish a product--splitting equivalence for double Schubert polynomials, relating triple Schubert coefficients to splitting coefficients. This equivalence highlights structural symmetries and provides reduction methods for computing coefficients that are otherwise difficult to access. Taken together, these results extend the range of double Schubert polynomial products for which positivity can be established combinatorially and yield explicit formulas that can be implemented computationally.

papers.title: Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks
papers.abstract: We study the optimal sampling and transmission policies for a transmitter communicating with n gossiping receivers with the objective of tracking a source's status over time using a semantic freshness metric: Version Age of Information (VAoI). The transmitter observes the version changes in the source, and can acquire a new information version by paying a sampling cost. The receivers gossip, allowing information exchange among each other without direct transmission. Gossiping can save on transmission cost, but it may propagate stale version information, necessitating transmitter intervention. With imperfect communication links, we formulate an infinite horizon average cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) in order to jointly optimize receivers' VAoIs, sampling and transmission costs in a time slotted fully connected (FC) gossip network. We first solve the MDP using Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm. Then, we prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter VAoI. Further, under reliable gossiping links, we show that transmission and idling has an VAoI-difference threshold structure with minimum VAoI activation. Numerical results obtained using RVI show that the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines. These results characterize how source sampling, direct transmission, and receiver gossip should be jointly coordinated for cost-aware semantic freshness in gossip networks.

papers.title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
papers.abstract: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.

papers.title: Interpretable Cyber-Physical Attack Detection in Smart Grids: A Leakage-Controlled Multi-Testbed Evaluation of Fusion, Robustness, and Observability Limits
papers.abstract: Cyber-physical smart-grid detectors are typically treated as black boxes and validated exclusively on clean, temporally shuffled datasets, which risk overly optimistic performance claims. This work presents a multi-testbed evaluation study built around an interpretable, time-windowed fusion Random Forest, adopting the pessimistic result whenever evaluation protocols disagree. (i) On a public paired cyber-physical dataset, shuffled cross-validation is optimistic: macro-F1 falls from 0.96 to 0.88 +/- 0.06 under rolling-origin temporal evaluation. A topology-free graph convolutional network (GCN) serving as a control confirms that this lightweight model is competitive on these splits. (ii) The adaptive and adaptive-joint feature-space attacks, which are infeasible as realistic grid manipulations, degrade macro-F1 to 0.67 and 0.34, respectively. Adversarial training and randomized smoothing partially restore performance, and a physics-constrained evolution-strategy evasion on the IEEE 14-Bus testbed shows the same vulnerability pattern. (iii) On real IEC-104 traffic, the cyber view reliably catches structural attacks (recall of 0.87 to 0.98) but largely fails on semantic value manipulation (recall of 0.11 to 0.35). An observability taxonomy on the IEEE 14-Bus system reveals that stealthy false data injection defeats all three observation views. (iv) On a full AC weighted least-squares state-estimation testbed, a forecasting-aided temporal test is evaded by slow ramps precisely where a rate-invariant physics-manifold test sustains detection at a common 5% false-alarm target. A full end-to-end evaluation on IEEE 118-Bus confirms the ordering but bounds its strength: the manifold test detects every trial down to 0.05 degree/step and 0.48 at 0.02 degree/step, against 0.14 for the temporal test. All code and benchmarks are released.

papers.title: Explicitly capturing demonstrator multi-modality for distillation into diffusion policies
papers.abstract: The diversity of a distilled diffusion policy's outputs matters beyond how it impacts the policy's success rate. In particular, downstream applications like test-time search and policy improvement require exploration. Thus, we want to distill multi-modal demonstrators into diffusion policies which reproduce their conditional action distributions. Standard data collection for behavior cloning applies a sliding window to demonstration episodes, which pairs unique observation histories with actions. These datasets can be fit by a policy that is either multi-modal, or unimodal with high Lipschitz constant to capture a diversity of actions seen at nearby observation samples. Prior work finds that diffusion policies trained on sparse data learn the latter, memorizing one action per observation. We adapt vine sampling to behavior cloning data collection to resolve this ambiguity: at some states the demonstrator visits, query it $k$ times from exactly the same observation. On a synthetic task, we study how the number of actions per observation, $k$, affects the learned policy, and find that larger $k$ yields a policy that better matches the demonstrator's conditional distribution, including its multi-modality and diversity. On a 2D truck unloading task, vine sampling likewise leads to a policy closer to the demonstrator and substantially improves both best-of-$N$ and expert iteration performance.

papers.title: An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes
papers.abstract: These open lecture notes provide a broad introduction to measure-theoretic probability and stochastic processes, with a focus on applications. Topics include probability spaces, conditional expectation, generating and characteristic functions, Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, convergence of random variables, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, stochastic differential equations and their connection to partial differential equations, jump diffusions, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and Monte Carlo methods. Most chapters include exercises, and solutions are provided. The notes were written for a two-quarter course for first-year PhD students in applied mathematics, and should also be useful to graduate students in statistics, engineering, economics and finance. The LaTeX source is freely available on GitHub under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license, and readers are encouraged to fork the notes and contribute corrections, improvements, and new material.

papers.title: Validating AI-Discovered Cloud Threats on Live Infrastructure: A Multi-Model, Multi-Cloud Study
papers.abstract: Cloud infrastructure threat modeling lacks empirical validation of AI-discovered threats. We present a three-phase methodology of multi-agent threat discovery, automated exploit synthesis, and non-destructive live validation, and apply it to three commercial foundation models on two cloud architectures, validating each threat natively on the cloud (AWS, GCP, or Azure) it was discovered against. Of 233 AI-discovered threats, 103 were confirmed and 34 refuted (75.2\% precision, 95\% CI [67.3, 81.7]); 44 were conditional (the named mechanism refuted but an equivalent impact shown through another path) and 52 indeterminate. Multi-model discovery helped through breadth, not agreement: the three models together found 2.2$\times$ the confirmed threats of the best single model at comparable precision, while threats reported by several models were confirmed no more often than single-model ones. False positives were not architecture-specific: they asserted access or system state the deployment did not have. Threats coded in advance as observable configuration resolved cleanly more often than multi-step behavioral threats (72.5\% vs.\ 51.6\%), which were more often conditional, suggesting that models more often misidentify the exploitation mechanism than the underlying weakness. AI-assisted discovery is a practical input to security workflows when paired with empirical validation.

papers.title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
papers.abstract: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.

papers.title: CoupledFlow: One-Step Neural Operators for Coupled Multi-Physics PDEs
papers.abstract: This paper introduces COUPLED FLOW, a new neural operator learning framework for multi-physics PDE systems that captures the co-evolution of multiple physical processes by modeling their cross-process interactions. Unlike existing neural operator methods that primarily target single-physics settings, COUPLED FLOW employs a novel structure-constrained flow matching algorithm to learn process- specific mean velocity fields conditioned on the full multi-physics state. This enables fast and accurate one-step prediction of coupled PDE systems that would otherwise require expensive numerical simulations. A key challenge in training COUPLED FLOW however lies in sampling structure-constrained conditional flow interpolants that capture cross-process correlations and serve as training examples for flow matching. To address this challenge, we derive a multi-physics mean-flow consistency identity that characterizes cross-process interactions and defines the structure-constrained mean-flow matching loss. To provide informative training samples for flow matching with this loss, we develop a principled method for sampling correlated conditional interpolants based on posterior multi-output Gaus- sian processes, which capture richer cross-process correlations than the commonly used endpoint-conditioned linear interpolants. We also establish a theoretical re- sult showing that the Wasserstein-2 distance between the predicted and oracle PDE solution distributions is upper-bounded in terms of the structure-constrained flow matching loss and the smoothness of the learned flow. Experiments across diverse coupled PDE benchmarks demonstrate that COUPLED FLOW consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art neural operators and generative PDE solvers.

papers.title: Molecular Photoionization Spectra from Signed Dyson Orbitals and Anharmonic Nuclear Motion
papers.abstract: Molecular photoelectron bands couple changes in nuclear structure to the energy-dependent scattering of the departing electron. Band intensities require both nuclear transition moments and electronic continuum amplitudes. We present SPARKS (Scattering and Photoionization: Amplitudes, Response Kernels and Spectra), a molecular photoionization approach that connects signed Dyson orbitals to complex molecular dipole amplitudes and harmonic or anharmonic nuclear transition moments. Compact B-spline and finite-element discrete-variable representations support spectral and sparse outgoing-boundary solvers. Independent molecular checks reproduce a reference H$_2^+$ spectrum and CO continuum amplitudes, while analytic hydrogen photoionization tests establish the continuum normalization. For H$_2$O/H$_2$O$^+$, electronic derivatives activate a Franck--Condon-dark fundamental and enter the same nuclear operator used in harmonic, perturbative and internal-coordinate variational calculations. Furan extends the nuclear treatment to all 21 vibrational coordinates in a selected configuration-interaction window, including low-lying out-of-plane states. Four epichlorohydrin ionization channels show how orbital mixing reshapes cross sections and angular distributions at similar Dyson norms. Energy conservation is imposed separately for every vibronic transition at fixed photon energy. The resulting spectra retain vibrational assignments and electronic interference, connecting weak-band activation, anharmonic spacings and photoelectron angular distributions within one physical description.

papers.title: Forecasting Replication Study Results from Meta-Analyses
papers.abstract: Multisite replication projects often rely on published meta-analyses to plan their sample sizes, but meta-analyses tend to overestimate population effects because of publication bias and differences in study characteristics. We developed methods to forecast site-level estimates of a not-yet-conducted replication from a meta-analysis. Extending calibrated estimates from meta-regression, we constructed nonparametric prediction intervals that condition on each site's moderator levels and correct for publication bias through inverse-probability-of-publication weighting under an assumed severity. These intervals achieve nominal coverage asymptotically when population effects are normally distributed, with a bounded coverage error otherwise. We compared four forecasting models (intercept-only meta-analysis or meta-regression, each with and without publication bias correction) in simulation study (81 scenarios and blinded retrospective forecasts of two multisite replications in infant cognition: ManyBabies 1 (104 sites) and ManyBabies 4 (33 sites). Correcting for publication bias improved interval calibration, with gains that increased with bias severity. Meta-regression improved forecasts only when measured moderators explained effect variation and replication sites differed meaningfully on them. In practice, publication bias correction should be the default when forecasting replications from meta-analyses, and replication projects that deliberately vary measured moderators across sites would enable more informative forecasts.

papers.title: Thermodynamic, Optical, and Wave Signatures of Charged Letelier AdS Black Holes with PFDM and Quintessence
papers.abstract: We study a four-dimensional charged Letelier--anti-de Sitter (AdS) black-hole metric containing a cloud of strings, a phenomenological perfect-fluid-dark-matter (PFDM) source, and a Kiselev-type quintessence term. We derive the curvature invariants, horizon temperature, entropy, electric potential, and horizon-based mass function, and analyze local thermal response and the associated extended-phase-space identities. A rectangular benchmark cycle gives $W=0.095000$ and $η\simeq15.39\%$ for the explicitly stated geometric-unit parameters; these values are model- and cycle-specific and are not presented as a universal efficiency enhancement. For geometric optics, we derive the photon-sphere condition, critical impact parameter, and finite-radius shadow angle. For a massless, minimally coupled scalar field, we obtain a radial-coordinate Helmholtz equation and identify frequency-dependent barriers, evanescent intervals, and candidate trapping regions; the eikonal barrier-top scale approaches the photon-sphere capture scale. Two qualifications delimit the interpretation. First, with the stated PFDM stress-tensor convention, $ρ_{\rm PFDM}=-β/(8πr^3)$, so positive $β$ describes a negative-density effective source. Second, the mass function follows from the horizon equation, but identifying it with a conserved asymptotic AdS mass requires a separate charge and boundary-normalization analysis. The potential-well analysis likewise does not determine complex quasinormal frequencies. We therefore present the results as a consistent, parameter-specific analysis of the adopted phenomenological geometry, while distinguishing algebraic thermodynamic identities from conclusions requiring asymptotic-charge or spectral calculations.

papers.title: Deintercalation Equilibria Control the Composition, Structure, and Electronic Quality in the Synthesis of 2$M$-WS$_2$
papers.abstract: Alkali-metal intercalation-deintercalation (AMID) enables access to metastable layered materials such as 2$M$-WS$_2$. Mechanistic studies of AMID have focused on intercalation; how deintercalation proceeds and influences crystal properties is comparatively poorly understood. Here, we assess 34 deintercalation treatments of 2$M$-K$_x$WS$_2$ and find that K$^+$ removal proceeds through coupled redox and ion-exchange equilibria, whose positions set the composition, structure, and electronic quality of the products. Across a series of neat solvents, K$^+$ deintercalation amount increased with solvent polarity and was driven to near-completion upon addition of nonoxidizing crown ether chelators, regardless of solvent polarity. Spontaneous reintercalation occurred when 2$M$-WS$_2$ was placed in dilute aqueous solutions of the strong base KOH but not the neutral salt KCl. These results suggest that the extent of deintercalation is governed by the stability of K$^+$ in solution, rather than oxidant strength alone, consistent with a reaction under thermodynamic control. Treatments that bias the deintercalation equilibrium most strongly toward the products while avoiding deleterious side reactions produce the highest quality 2$M$-WS$_2$. A six-hour treatment with acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ gave the highest average residual resistivity ratio ($\overline{RRR}$). Residual K$^+$, quantified by ICP-MS, was found in all treated samples and appeared to impose an upper bound on $\overline{RRR}$. Treatments yielding crystals with $\overline{RRR}$ below this bound did not always afford 2$M$-WS$_2$; we observed two new structures in bleach-treated samples and signatures of alternative phases under other conditions. This work demonstrates that deintercalation is not merely a processing step in AMID but a mechanistically rich reaction that might be rationally tuned to improve and control metastable materials.

papers.title: Semantic Synthesis over Brute-Force Search: LLM-Guided Transformation Design for Efficient Learning
papers.abstract: Data transformation pipelines shape the training distribution in computer vision, but designing them is a computationally expensive problem. We investigate whether large language models can enable efficient discovery by synthesizing executable transformation programs outside predefined augmentation spaces. We compare nine strategies under a unified training protocol, including standard augmentation policies, brute-force search, direct code generation with two LLMs, and performance-guided generation using LLMs fine-tuned on accuracy-ordered transformation pairs. When the best candidates are retrained for 20 epochs, LLM-generated transformation programs lead on every dataset, reaching 0.8877 accuracy on CIFAR-10, 0.5825 on CIFAR-100, and 0.9588 on SVHN, surpassing brute-force search over 6,000 candidates. The best transform on CIFAR-10 and SVHN comes from a fine-tuned generator using 270 candidates, while the best on CIFAR-100 comes from an off-the-shelf generator using only 10. This needs 22x fewer candidate evaluations in the generation step and 600x fewer for off-the-shelf generations, relative to brute-force search. Beyond transformation discovery, we analyze the reliability of the reduced-budget evaluation commonly used for augmentation search. Correlating one-epoch selection scores with 20-epoch outcomes reveals strong, weak, and absent predictive relationships depending on the dataset and architecture, with correlations ranging from 0.756 to near zero. A positive control indicates that range restriction alone is unlikely to explain the low correlations. Our results indicate that semantic synthesis with code LLMs provides an efficient alternative to search-based transformation discovery and highlight the importance of validating evaluation fidelity when optimizing data transformations.

papers.title: In-Band Boundary Resonances from Coalescing Zero-Group-Velocity Points
papers.abstract: Boundary states generally reside in band gaps, whereas in-band confinement typically requires exact decoupling from propagating modes. We demonstrate an alternative mechanism in reciprocal, topologically trivial Hermitian lattices arising from the coalescence of two zero-group-velocity (ZGV) points. At coalescence, the group velocity and inverse effective mass vanish simultaneously, and the corresponding Bloch root acquires higher multiplicity. The coalesced root remains propagating, whereas nearby root splitting yields weakly evanescent channels that, together with a bulk-matched termination, generate a boundary-weighted resonance within the propagating spectrum. The mechanism is realized analytically in a two-leg ladder model through the coalescence of time-reversal-related ZGVs and extends to distinct ZGVs produced by longer-range interactions. Finite-size scaling distinguishes the resulting resonance from extended and defect-bound states. Scanning laser Doppler vibrometry on a 3D-printed elastic ladder reveals boundary enhancement in a nearly flat band region, consistent with operation slightly below criticality. ZGV coalescence thus provides a bulk framework for in-band boundary resonances in reciprocal Hermitian lattices.

papers.title: BRACE: Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control for Safe Navigation under Unknown Disturbances
papers.abstract: Disturbances encountered during autonomous navigation generally vary across space, often discontinuously, as obstacles redirect wind and changing terrain alters traction. Tracking controllers typically assume sufficient control authority to mitigate disturbances and maintain safety; the regime where this assumption fails remains underexplored. We present Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control (BRACE), a hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) framework for reach-avoid navigation under unknown, bounded, spatially varying disturbances. BRACE infers a disturbance belief from model prediction errors and uses that to condition a high-level policy that adapts the reference trajectory. The policy combines a nominal and a belief-guided residual term, trained jointly with a likelihood-ratio advantage reweighting heuristic. We evaluate BRACE in three simulated quadcopter environments with abruptly switching wind fields, and validate it on Crazyflie hardware with fan-generated disturbances. Across these settings, BRACE improves reach-avoid performance over model predictive control and RL baselines.

papers.title: Lifting mechanical zero modes without dispersion
papers.abstract: Floppy frameworks carry flat bands of zero-frequency mechanisms with no finite-frequency resonance, and couplings that lift them usually spread them. We show that an on-site tensor lifts a mechanism band without first-order dispersion exactly when, projected onto the mechanisms, it acts as wavevector-independent scalars on orthogonal pieces. Three structures achieve this: local normal modes, invariant symmetry sectors, and a balance law. A mechanism moves both ends of every bond between two vertex classes equally along it, and where the inter-class bond tensors are class scalars this balance law fixes its norm shares and hence the flat value from geometry alone. For the fluorite net the band lies outside the tensor spectrum, at 14/9 of the contact stiffness to first order, and stays flat to all orders in a fixed cage. A placement inside a tiling dual that keeps the common symmetry supplies such tensors, because each contact star inherits its site symmetry. Ten catalogued dual pairs lift flat; half are eigenvalue cases a resolved count matches, and the balance law explains flat bands in random cages too. Duality makes the rigid cage common. In a printable beam-frame lattice, contacts that lock joint rotation remove first-order bending dispersion whenever bonded mechanisms are orthogonal local normals.

papers.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
papers.abstract: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.

papers.title: Compact metric spaces as exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces
papers.abstract: The class of compact metric spaces (metric spaces which induce a compact topology), despite being an important class of metric spaces, is not closed under many natural constructions. For instance, infinite metric products of compact metric spaces will often fail to induce a compact topology, while on the other hand, the topological product of any family of compact metric spaces is always a compact topological space, evidencing a discrepancy between topological and metric products. The notion of metric compact Hausdorff space -- compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a lower semi-continuous metric -- provides a class of spaces which keep track of metric data and topological data separately, thereby forming a complete and cocomplete category, while including all compact metric spaces. Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.

papers.title: Stellar Disruption and Black Hole Retention in Massive Collisions: The Role of Thermonuclear Feedback
papers.abstract: A stellar-mass black hole (BH) that collides with a massive star can be captured by drag and settle at its center as a black hole star. Hydrodynamic simulations that neglect nuclear reactions have found that the star survives and becomes a black hole star (BH*) for BH-to-star mass ratios $q\lesssim0.2$. We perform hydrodynamic simulations of head-on collisions with the \athenak\ code, including CNO burning coupled to the gas, for $q=0.1$ and $0.2$ BHs, stellar masses of $100$ and $500\,M_{\odot}$, solar, metal-deficient, and Helium-rich compositions. In all models (with $q\le0.2$), the energy dissipated by drag is comparable to or less than the binding energy that the captured BH adds to the gas so that it alone does not disrupt the star. But, under compression around the captured BH, gas is heated to $\gtrsim2\times10^8$\,K and undergoes thermonuclear burning at the $β$-limited hot-CNO rate. Within about one dynamical time after the BH settles at the center, the nuclear energy released during the encounter becomes a significant fraction of the star's binding energy $\tfrac32\barβ\int P\,dV$. The star loses most of its mass once the cumulative release reaches this binding energy. Below this threshold, the release rate declines. Merger between a solar-composition star and a BH with a mass ratio $q=0.2$ leads to the disruption of the star after releasing most of its total mass. But a metal-poor star, with nearly the same binding energy and total yield, survives with minor release after merger with an identical BH. After coalescence with a less massive ($q=0.1$) BH, stars with both solar and metal-poor composition survive as black hole stars, burning at a rate $\gtrsim 10^{44}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$, far from thermal equilibrium. Very massive and helium-rich stars, which are weakly bound, are the most easily disrupted.

papers.title: Qubit representation of the mass observable in quantized Schwarzschild interior
papers.abstract: We develop a quantum-computational framework for the mass observable of the Wheeler--DeWitt quantized Schwarzschild black-hole interior. Working in the physical sector spanned by correlated two-mode oscillator states, we construct finite-dimensional representations of the mass operator and map them onto qubit operators through Pauli decomposition. We analyze the resulting representations for increasing truncation sizes and establish analytically the scaling of the number of nonvanishing Pauli terms and independent measurement settings. These results provide a quantitative characterization of the quantum resources required to encode and measure the black-hole mass observable. As a representative benchmark, we implement a two-qubit variational quantum eigensolver for the smallest nontrivial truncation and find excellent agreement with the exact finite-dimensional spectrum. We further describe a quantum-circuit procedure for verifying the Wheeler--DeWitt constraint independently of the mass estimation. Our results provide a direct connection between Wheeler--DeWitt quantum gravity and quantum computation and establish a structured route toward the quantum simulation of gravitational observables.

papers.title: Beating the Pool, Not the Game: A White-Box Equilibrium Agent for Language-Based Economic Games
papers.abstract: We describe sudsho, a rule-based agent for the GLEE Competition that plays bargaining, negotiation, and persuasion with zero inference-time LLM calls. Games are scored as payoff percentiles against an empirical pool of prior play on the same configuration, so pool percentiles set our demand targets while clamped equilibrium shares bound demands and acceptance. Every move is a deterministic function of the visible state (persuasion mixing aside), so alignment is verified by replaying the post-freeze move log through the policy. Across 117,280 games the agent reached an overall rating of 2056 at $0 inference cost, and the account, ranked by its best agent (a same-policy replica), placed 26th of 71 ranked accounts. A replay against three frozen snapshots of the opponent pool credits the pool-aware clamp with 274 to 330 points of mean per-game bargaining rating, an effect that holds where logged opponent decisions fix the replay.

papers.title: Gendered Misclassification from Surname-Based Race Imputation
papers.abstract: Researchers increasingly estimate political behavior based on race and gender from voter files, where race is imputed from surnames and geography. This only works where surnames suggest group membership, an assumption violated where surnames follow norms around marriage. Imputation is therefore biased against women who adopt their husband's surname, especially those who racially inter-marry, an outcome itself endogenous to partisanship. Using six US states recording self-reported race, I show that imputation is less accurate for Asian and Hispanic women, particularly those sharing the surname of a partner of another race, who differ politically from other women of their race. This violates assumptions behind downstream inference approaches, which nearly double the gender gap in partisanship among Asian voters. I derive an expression showing the bias is largest where a group is small. Using maiden rather than marriage-adopted surnames in North Carolina raises accuracy up to fourfold for women married across racial lines. Recovering maiden surnames, or omitting the married surname, removes much of the bias. In a national replication of a study of gender gaps in turnout, the correction more than triples the gap among Asian voters. In Lebanon, where wives register in their husband's locality, the error enters through geography.

papers.title: Beyond Host-Side Control: HBM Controller Partitioning Across Host and HBM Base Dies
papers.abstract: Recent generations of high bandwidth memory (HBM), such as HBM4, allow the base die of the memory stack to be manufactured using a logic process that can accommodate more complex controller functions next to the DRAM. We present the first systematic quantitative study of function-level controller placement between the host and the HBM4 base die on a silicon interposer. We divide the controller into its main functions and evaluate four placements, from a complete host controller to a complete base die controller, with intermediate placements that move maintenance or scheduling to the base die. We extend Ramulator 2 with HBM4 timing and maintenance, model a die-to-die (D2D) link with timing checks at the DRAM interface, and compose area, energy, and temperature from synthesized controller blocks, modeled storage, and interface data. A provisioned D2D link preserves per-stack bandwidth and adds about twice its one-way delay to unloaded latency. Maintenance moves to the base die with no bandwidth cost and frees host command slots, and the freed share grows with stack height. Replacing the wide interface with a D2D link saves 61% of host shoreline and 16.85 mm2 of host area per stack. The D2D link dominates the added base die area and power, and the base die runs cooler under streaming with link energy below 0.4 pJ/bit. Shared control delivers up to 1.72x the throughput of static partitioning between two requestors.

papers.title: Augur: An Online Learning-based Hardware Data Prefetcher using Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Machine-learning-based hardware prefetchers can learn complex access patterns, but practical deployment demands online adaptation, low-latency inference, and modest hardware cost. We present Augur, a hardware delta prefetcher based on next-generation reservoir computing (NGRC) that meets all three requirements. Augur formulates delta prediction as a history-based regression problem. It constructs a fixed-size reservoir from hashed delta features over a short context window and predicts the next delta using a single dot product. The model is updated online via one-step SGD and requires no offline pre-training, no workload-specific tuning, and no floating-point arithmetic. A key technical insight makes this practical: replacing the integer multiplications traditionally used to generate nonlinear reservoir features with bitwise AND operations removes all feature-generation multipliers while preserving the joint context encoded in hash-derived features. Because Augur regresses a continuous delta rather than classifying into a fixed action set, it can predict any delta in [-64, 63]. Augur pairs the reservoir with a simple Markov-based delta predictor for simple delta patterns and employs multi-layered filtering and adaptive lookahead to suppress wasteful prefetches. Evaluated on 169 traces spanning GAP, Ligra, PARSEC, SPEC CPU 2006, SPEC CPU 2017, and AI workloads, Augur outperforms the state-of-the-art ML-based delta prefetcher by 2.9%, 4.5%, and 5.3% in geomean speedup on 1-, 4-, and 8-core systems, respectively, while achieving ~2x higher prefetch accuracy and 37.8% fewer overpredictions. Augur is practical to implement at 35 KB storage, 0.32 sq. mm area, and 32.7 mW in 12 nm.

papers.title: Polynomial-Preserving Processes and Volatility Modelling in Discrete Time
papers.abstract: This paper develops a discrete-time framework for volatility modelling and derivative pricing based on polynomial preservation. The framework provides exact moments of arbitrary order and serial cross-moments of variance and return processes over any finite horizon through finite-dimensional matrix representations. This analytical tractability is maintained while accommodating flexible leverage and variance-of-variance dynamics and non-Gaussian innovations. We introduce two novel classes of stochastic volatility models that nest widely used discrete-time specifications and study their statistical properties. Under two distinct scaling regimes, we establish weak convergence to polynomial diffusions and jump-diffusions and convergence of polynomial moments, linking discrete-time moment recursions to continuous-time matrix-exponential formulas. An empirical analysis of S\&P~500 returns and a large panel of options spanning 1996--2023 shows that the proposed specifications improve return fit and reduce mean weekly implied volatility root mean squared errors by approximately 8--41\% relative to their nested benchmarks, depending on the variance dynamics and innovation distribution.

papers.title: Absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology
papers.abstract: We construct absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology, for real 3-manifolds such that the image of the fixed point set in the quotient is nullhomologous. This allows us to fix the sign of Miyazawa's degree invariant. Our construction uses a mod-two index-theoretic correction term, the Arf invariant.

papers.title: DeepFinance: Can AI Diligence a $100MM Deal?
papers.abstract: Existing evaluations of AI models on high-finance work focus on retrieving answers from financial documents and producing numerically correct outputs. Real private equity (PE) and investment banking (IB) work also depends on choosing between conflicting sources, making sound assumptions, and keeping every step auditable. We introduce DeepFinance, an ultra long-horizon benchmark of 21 end-to-end PE and IB tasks that take a human professional an average of 27.1 hours. Each task pairs a request with a data room averaging 19 files and is graded against an average of 84 expert-written rubric criteria covering output, workflow, and judgment. We evaluate 22 model configurations, each in its native agent harness. The best configuration, GPT-6 Astra with max reasoning, satisfies 57.6% of rubric criteria, and the top four configurations are not statistically distinguishable. Frontier models often calculate correctly from the wrong inputs and find decision-relevant evidence without acting on it.

papers.title: Z-Estimation under Unignorably Large Clusters
papers.abstract: Cluster-size heterogeneity can invalidate conventional cluster-robust inference when a small number of clusters dominate observation-weighted estimating equations. This paper develops asymptotic theory for cluster-balanced \(Z\)-estimators under independent clusters, arbitrary realised cluster sizes, and unrestricted within-cluster dependence. Building on the size-adjusted reweighting of Chiang, Sasaki & Wang (2025), the analysis distinguishes target definition, identification, and inference. A common cluster-level zero, imposed as an identifying condition or derived from individual-level exogeneity or design-based mechanisms, makes the structural target invariant to deterministic cluster reweighting; separation of the reweighted population moments then ensures identification. The pointwise results establish asymptotic normality while allowing the covariance sequence to vary along the cluster array. The results for functional parameters establish weak convergence and validity of a cluster multiplier bootstrap for uniform inference. The framework covers smooth and non-smooth scores with distribution, quantile, and expectile regressions as concrete applications. Monte Carlo experiments illustrate pointwise and uniform inference under heterogeneous cluster sizes, and a supplementary empirical application illustrates the consequences of cluster weighting in municipal-school data.

papers.title: Diophantine definitions of nonsplitting for central simple algebras over global fields
papers.abstract: For every global field and every fixed degree, we prove that the structure constants defining nonsplit central simple algebras form a diophantine set. We formulate a local witness principle separating reliable localization, exact localization, and local detection. Adapted Kummer and Artin--Schreier presentations provide a common construction of witnesses through a uniform radical formula and ramification matching. This gives an independent proof of the non-characteristic case, which also follows from Morrison's nonnorm theorem, and treats the characteristic-degree case by the same method. We recover prime-degree nonnorm definability and give applications to rootless polynomials, anisotropic quadratic forms in all characteristics, and generalized Severi--Brauer varieties.

papers.title: Prescriptive Learning of Linear Policies with Feasibility Guarantees for Binary Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Binary decision-making under uncertainty arises across a wide range of applications, including energy systems scheduling, transportation, and workforce planning. While machine learning has been increasingly applied to accelerate or replace mixed-integer solvers in such settings, existing approaches rely on predictive learning, training models to reproduce optimal decisions from labeled data, which lacks knowledge of counterfactual outcomes and provides no guarantees that the resulting decisions will be feasible. This limitation is further compounded under distributional shift, where policies trained on historical data may produce systematically infeasible decisions. We propose a prescriptive learning framework for binary decision-making that addresses both limitations. Rather than predicting optimal labels, the framework jointly optimizes over linear decision policies and feasible assignments across all training scenarios, allowing feasible alternatives and their operational performance to be considered directly during training. We further extend the framework to a distributionally robust chance-constrained formulation using a Wasserstein ambiguity set, which enforces feasibility with a prescribed probability under the worst-case distribution in the ambiguity set and enables a tunable trade-off between robustness and solution quality. We demonstrate the framework on two case studies, namely a unit commitment problem and a staff allocation problem. Out-of-sample experiments under test distributions that either match or differ from the training distribution show that the robust model is more conservative when the two distributions coincide, while under distributional shift it substantially reduces unmet demand and lowers total cost by up to 76.5% relative to classical predictive learning.

papers.title: A Tool for Anonymized Clinical Knowledge Retrieval and Speaker Interaction Analysis of Healthcare Tele-mentoring Sessions
papers.abstract: We present a tool for anonymized retrieval of clinical knowledge and analysis of multi-speaker interactions in tele-mentoring sessions of Project ECHO (Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes). Our tool's novel design includes: (a) a compound metadata filter that enforces strict speaker- and session-level isolation during retrieval, preventing cross-session context contamination; (b) MedGemma-4B as a locally-hosted language model for clinically grounded answer generation across three query modes; (c) interaction graphs to compute betweenness centrality, PageRank influence, and turn-taking patterns to quantify participation equity; and (d) a consistent alias-based anonymization scheme that prevents real participant names from appearing in any rendered output. During the demo, a healthcare provider (user) will interactively query multi-year ECHO sessions, explore participation dynamics through interaction graphs, compare sessions side-by-side, and assess answer quality via six reference-free RAG metrics, all without any cloud API dependency.

papers.title: Sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints for composite hypotheses
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints, where multiple independent data sources are observed over time, but only a limited subset can be sampled at each instant. The objective is to identify the anomalous sources while controlling the probabilities of at least one false alarm and at least one missed detection below prescribed levels. An identification policy must jointly determine when to stop sampling, which sources to declare anomalous, and how to allocate observations across sources under the sampling constraints. We seek policies that minimize the expected time to decision to a first-order asymptotic approximation as the error probabilities vanish. The observations from each source follow an unknown density belonging to one of two disjoint sets, corresponding to regular and anomalous behavior. Focusing on a nonparametric framework, which allows greater flexibility in modeling regular and anomalous statistical behavior, we establish general conditions for asymptotic optimality and provide a unified characterization of asymptotically optimal policies for composite hypothesis testing under sampling constraints. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed policies, and the robustness of the nonparametric framework.

papers.title: Positivity Proofs for Third-Order Holonomic Sequences via Differences Scaled by Rational Functions
papers.abstract: We study the positivity of sequences $f$ that satisfy a third-order holonomic recurrence $f(n+3)= P_2(n) f(n+2) + P_1(n) f(n+1) + P_0(n) f(n)$ whose coefficients $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ are rational functions in $\R(x)$. We provide a sufficient condition on $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ for the recurrence to admit a solution all but finitely many terms of which are positive, and whose positivity is robust under small perturbations of the initial values. This sufficient condition is also a necessary condition for a subclass of the recurrences. By developing the proof of this sufficient condition, for another subclass of the recurrences, we show that it is decidable whether all the terms of a given sequence are positive for any initial values outside an exceptional plane. It is common to construct a positivity certificate, which guarantees the positivity of a solution, to show this kind of decidability. In this paper, we construct a new type of positivity certificate via the $S$-scaled difference $f(n+1) - S(n) f(n)$ for a suitable $S \in \R(x)$. This result partially improves the work by Ibrahim and Salvy.

papers.title: Vertex splitting, global rigidity and nondegenerate equilibrium stresses
papers.abstract: We prove Whiteley's conjecture that every nontrivial vertex split of a generically globally rigid graph preserves generic global rigidity in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), for all \(d\geq1\). We give two proofs of the stronger assertion that the split graph is infinitesimally rigid at every generic coincident realisation of the two split vertices. Both proofs use maximum-rank equilibrium stress matrices and then apply the coincident-rigidity criterion of Cruickshank, Jackson and Tanigawa. The second construction also shows that every generically globally rigid graph admits a nondegenerate equilibrium stress of maximum rank at every generic realisation, establishing a conjecture of Jordán and Tanigawa.

papers.title: On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
papers.abstract: We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using Čech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.

papers.title: Remembering to Reason: Structured Memory for Scene and Workflow Understanding in Robot-Assisted Surgery
papers.abstract: Surgical video understanding is an important foundation for intelligent assistance in robot-assisted surgery. Similar surgical views can reflect different actions or procedural stages. Interpreting these views requires access to earlier observations, yet frame-centric prompting leaves this history unavailable. We introduce MemSurg, a framework that remembers surgical observations before reasoning over them. Its structured memory graph stores timestamped entity categories, locations, motion cues, and interaction summaries. Chronological links preserve recent context, while entity-associated links connect recurring observations across the procedure. Task-adaptive retrieval then supplies evidence-grounded prompts for scene and workflow reasoning, supporting both frozen inference and memory-conditioned supervised fine-tuning. Evaluation on robot-assisted prostatectomy and two complementary surgical benchmarks shows a 10.43-percentage-point gain over SurgRAW with GPT-4o. Memory conditioning adds 6.52 points under matched Qwen3-VL-8B fine-tuning, and an inference-time plug-in adds 7.04 points to EndoChat. These results support structured memory as a reusable source of procedural evidence for surgical video understanding. Our code will be publicly released.

papers.title: An Optimal First-Order Active-Hull Method for Convex Composite Hölder Smooth Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider the problem (P): ${\min}_{x\in \mathbb{R}^n}\, f(x)+g(x)$ under the Euclidean geometry, where $f$ is convex and $(M,ν)$-Hölder smooth on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and $g$ is proper, closed and convex on $\mathbb{R}^n$, admits a generalized linear minimization oracle (GLMO), and has bounded domain with diameter $D$. An first-order active-hull (AH) method has access to both the first-order oracle (FO) of $f$ and the GLMO of $g$, and outputs a point that lies in the convex hull of all the past GLMO returns. We propose a new first-order AH method for solving (P), which is based on our newly developed ``recentered homotopy smoothing framework''. We show that in the high-dimensional regime, this method achieves the optimal FO and GLMO complexties simultaneously for all $ν\in[0,1]$.

papers.title: Bias-free superconducting microwave nonreciprocity from a passive nonlinear resonator
papers.abstract: Routing microwave tones in a nonreciprocal fashion in a superconducting chip usually requires an external bias, commonly in the form of static magnetic fields, pump tones or temporal modulation. Here we demonstrate microwave nonreciprocity in a bias-free, passive platform, a single nonlinear superconducting resonator patterned in one film without Josephson junctions. Unequal coupling with the two feeding ports makes its nonlinear resonance shift direction-dependent, and its sharp Fano lineshape converts this asymmetric response into a large transmission contrast when excited from opposite directions. Our niobium nitride (NbN) device reaches a directional contrast of 53.0 dB at an insertion loss of 4.6 dB, and it exceeds 20 dB over 9.7 MHz. Time-resolved measurements show that the device routes pulses from 2 us to 1 ms with more than 30 dB of contrast and switches within a few microseconds. Made with the same technology as superconducting amplifiers, such bias-free nonreciprocal components could simplify the on-chip routing of strong pump and control tones in quantum processors

papers.title: Untangling flow-harmonic correlations in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC using event-shape engineering
papers.abstract: Symmetric cumulants $\mathrm{SC}(m,n)$ measure the correlation between the event-by-event fluctuations of the flow harmonics $v_m$ and $v_n$, which, for higher harmonics, is influenced by the nonlinear response to the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) flow. Event-shape engineering, which selects events by the reduced flow vector $q_n$, is expected to control this contribution. However, its power is limited by the small forward multiplicity in light-ion collisions. In this work, we study the effect of the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections on the symmetric cumulants in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV using EPOS4 with an ATLAS-like acceptance. Using the law of total covariance, the symmetric cumulant is separated into a selected part, which follows the differences between the $q_n$ classes, and a residual part within them. It is observed that in OO collisions the correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$ remain almost entirely within the $q_2$ classes, unlike in Pb--Pb collisions. Nevertheless, events with the smallest $q_2$ in central OO collisions show weaker correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$, which is attributed to $v_4$ approaching its linear response. In Pb--Pb collisions, the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections act separately on the two factors of the nonlinear coupling of $v_5$, which establishes a way to isolate them experimentally.

papers.title: Bit-level Perceptron Prediction for Indirect Branches
papers.abstract: Modern software uses indirect branches for various purposes including, but not limited to, virtual method dispatch and implementation of switch statements. Because an indirect branch's target address cannot be determined prior to execution, high-performance processors depend on highly-accurate indirect branch prediction techniques to mitigate control hazards. This paper proposes a new indirect branch prediction scheme that predicts target addresses at the bit level. Using a series of perceptron-based predictors, our predictor predicts individual branch target address bits based on correlations within branch history. Our evaluations show this new branch target predictor is competitive with state-of-the-art branch target predictors at an equivalent hardware budget. For instance, over a set of workloads including SPEC and mobile applications, our predictor achieves a misprediction rate of 0.183 mispredictions per 1000 instructions, compared with 0.193 for the state-of-the-art ITTAGE predictor and 0.29 for a VPC-based indirect predictor.

papers.title: One Measurement, Many Fronts in Kitaev and Cluster Chains
papers.abstract: A projective measurement of one site in the ground state of a quantum chain disturbs the chain in two ways: learning the outcome shifts distant expectation values at once, through ground-state correlations, and the measurement erases the correlations between the measured site and the rest. Both changes travel outward. We solve this problem exactly for the Kitaev chain, the cluster chain in a transverse field, and the Kitaev chain with power-law couplings, and we find that far from the measured site every quadratic observable responds through a front. Where the front is and how fast it broadens depend only on the quasiparticle dispersion. How strong it is depends on two operators: how strongly the measured one creates the fastest quasiparticles and how strongly the observed one detects them; if either factor vanishes, the front is weaker and decays faster. One measurement therefore launches many fronts, one per observable, with a common position and width but different decay laws. In the Kitaev chain the density and the bond energy, the two terms of its nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian, respond to one density measurement with decay laws that trade places between the topological and the trivial phase; in the cluster chain, measuring a symmetry-odd spin instead of a symmetry-even one changes the critical decay law at a fixed Hamiltonian; and with power-law couplings the width law itself changes. All decay laws and profiles are obtained in closed form.

papers.title: Towards A Parametrized Complexity of Determinization
papers.abstract: Given a nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA), we want to estimate the difficulty of finding an equivalent deterministic finite automaton (DFA). We demonstrate that computing the state complexity of an NFA within polynomial precision is \textsf{PSPACE}-hard, and furthermore the same holds for the complexity of the subset construction, Brzozowski's algorithm, or, indeed, \emph{any} determinization algorithm which runs at least as fast. This result implies that making any \textit{a priori} estimate of the running time of the major determinization algorithms is inherently hard. To circumvent this---in the spirit of parametrized complexity---we try to identify complexity measures which can guarantee efficient determinization. Our main idea rests on linking the complexity of the subset construction to transition monoids using the semigroup complexity. We show that the semigroup complexity by itself can be reasonably approximated for certain classes of NFAs, and then introduce \emph{subset complexity}---a refinement of the semigroup complexity which has a tighter connection with the subset construction. In certain scenarios, the subset complexity can be approximated in polynomial time, making it potentially viable for more practical applications.

papers.title: Impact of the large scale environment on the baryonic scaling relations of disc galaxies: Insights from the GASP survey
papers.abstract: The Tully--Fisher relation (TFR) and the specific angular momentum--mass relation (SAMR) link the baryonic content of a disc to its kinematics and dynamics. Hence, these scaling relations should bear the imprints of any process removing baryons or altering their kinematics, such as those acting in clusters of galaxies. We test this using the MUSE survey "GAs Stripping Phenomena in galaxies" (GASP), which targets field, group, and cluster members at $z \approx 0.05$ and various stages of ram pressure stripping. For the 81 discs with favourable inclinations, we measure the distribution and kinematics of stars and ionised gas, and their specific angular momenta. Within their scatter, the stellar and baryonic relations show no significant dependence on the large scale environment: the TFRs have slopes $α\approx 3.6$ and $\approx 3.5$ for any kinematic tracer, and the SAMRs have $α\approx 0.65$--$0.75$, as predicted by tidal torque theory. The same holds for the ten S0-S0/as in our sample, consistent with the "faded spiral" formation scenario. Only the gas SAMR shows an environmental signature, with ram pressure stripped galaxies lying $\approx 0.16$~dex below unperturbed ones. This offset is mostly due to their enhanced star formation rate, and thus higher gas mass when inferred through the Schmidt-Kennicutt law, rather than to kinematic perturbations or disc truncation. Our results suggest that, within the area probed by MUSE ($\lesssim6$ disc scale lengths), these discs have preserved the angular momentum acquired at formation not only from cluster processes and pre-processing in filaments, but also from mergers and ejective feedback acting in any environment.

papers.title: Pole or Vector? Encoders Capture Bangla Compound Verbs, but LLMs Read Them Literally
papers.abstract: In Bangla, a main verb is often followed by one of a small set of vector verbs. These verbs lose their own meaning and add a shade of meaning instead, such as completion. For example, likhe phello means that someone finished writing, not that they wrote and threw something. The same two verbs can also describe two separate events, so only the context shows which meaning is meant. This makes compound verbs a hard test of how language models handle multiword expressions. We present BanglaCV-Probe, a benchmark of 17 vector verbs with 1,044 minimal pairs, 204 entailment items and 197 pairs of correct and incorrect combinations, all checked by native speakers. We test 26 models (encoders, LLMs and translation systems) on four skills: telling the two meanings apart internally, understanding what a vector adds, preferring correct combinations and keeping the vector's meaning in translation. Probes on five encoders tell the two meanings apart and still reach up to 93% accuracy when trained on pairs without surface cues. Prompted models rarely use this knowledge. Entailment accuracy stays between 59% and 81%. Several LLMs answer Yes or No to almost every item, and nine of ten models miss that someone who ate up the rice left none. Most instruction-tuned LLMs translate vectors literally in 15-20% of vector sentences and in up to 55% for mora (die). On correct combinations, a small Bangla-only model (88%) matches BLOOM-7B1 (87%) and both beat Qwen2.5-7B (74%). Data and code: https://github.com/ashuvo25/Pole_OR_Vector

papers.title: Beyond Real or Fake: A Dual-Channel Authenticity and Reasoning Protocol for Photographic Assessment
papers.abstract: Forensic verification has converged on a binary "real vs. fake" label that confates fully synthetic, tampered, and AI-retouched images despite their very different consequences. We argue that GenAI manipulations decompose along two complementary channels: a camera channel of sensor fingerprints (destroyed by neural processing), and a semantic channel of scene-level coherence (disrupted by content edits). Each manipulation type leaves a distinctive two-channel signature. We instantiate this taxonomy in 2CAP (2-Channel Authenticity Protocol), pairing a contrastively-trained camera encoder with a frozen semantic encoder to serve two applications on a shared backbone: (i) four-class authenticity classification via cross-attention fusion with learnable reliability weights; and (ii) evidence generation, where an authentic image serves as a reference for a query and the two encoders produce per-channel alignment scores together with a patch-level saliency map. These signals are supplied as privileged context to a frozen Vision-Language Model (VLM) through an Observe-Generate-Refine loop, yielding explanations with localization without forensic fine-tuning. On a multi-source benchmark, 2CAP attains the best classification performance, including strong retouching detection where existing methods fail, and improves explanation quality.

papers.title: eAdS- embedded AdS, tensionless strings and contracted Carroll-Weyl symmetry
papers.abstract: We adapt the Dirac conformal $d+2$ dimensional embedding construction to define a null string in $AdS_{d+1}$. Introducing an extra Stückelberg field $φ$, which is a scalar under $AdS$ and shifts under local scaling of embedding space, the model acquires a local scaling invariance. We refer to this string as the embedded anti-De Sitter, $eAdS$, null string. A very useful property of this new gauged formulation is that, unlike previous gauged actions in $AdS$ background, the local scaling symmetry commutes with the $so(d,2)$ symmetry of $AdS$. Interestingly, the $eAdS$ null string is the tensionless limit of a tensile string in embedding space and the same holds for its reduction to an intrinsic description of AdS. We display the symmetries and constraint algebras both in embedding space and directly in AdS.

papers.title: SCorPion: A Strategic, Controllable and Personified Conversational Companion
papers.abstract: Fixed prompt-based language models face challenges in open-domain conversations, where versatile topics require different expert advice or demonstrations to maximize their universal performance. Motivated by the dynamic prompt studies in language generation, we extract different chatting strategies from varied forms of text corpus, which steer the language model to different styles based on human principles. We design and deploy a conversational companion called SCorPion, which uses GraphRAG to extract and summarize the knowledge graph globally, yield community-summarized strategies, and produce query-focused optimal strategies. SCorPion has strategic thinking, yields personified and stylized responses, and can be controlled by explicit factors. Code and further results can be found in https://bachozean.github.io/scorpion-page/.

papers.title: 2D coherent spectroscopy of topological insulators
papers.abstract: Multidimensional coherent spectroscopy probes the response of a system to a sequence of time-separated light pulses, and has attracted significant interest in recent years. In the frequency space, it generates multidimensional spectra, in which information about different degrees of freedom of the system is generically disentangled. In this work, we develop a quantum geometric formulation of multidimensional optical susceptibilities in insulating systems. Focusing on a two-pulse setup and working in the velocity gauge, we derive analytical expressions for second-order and third-order two-dimensional coherent spectra (2DCS). We focus on the third-order ABB response, which remains finite in centrosymmetric systems where the second-order susceptibility vanishes by inversion symmetry. Its paramagnetic contribution supports an echo signal that probes products of four interband Berry-connection matrix elements, which reduce in two-band systems to bilinear combinations of the quantum geometric tensor of the occupied band. Using continuum and square-lattice models of two-dimensional Chern insulators, we show how the echo resolves the momentum-space sign structure of these geometric quantities. For the $xxyx$ response of the models considered, the number of nodes in the echo signal is related to the band topology. Our results extend the quantum-geometric interpretation of multidimensional spectroscopy to higher-order responses, showing that third-order 2DCS provides access to geometric structures beyond those probed at lower orders.

papers.title: Non-reciprocal Rouse chain model
papers.abstract: We study the center-of-mass mean-squared displacement (MSD) of a free non-reciprocal Rouse chain. Three stochastic models are considered: an overdamped linear chain, an underdamped linear chain, and an underdamped nonlinear chain with finite natural bond length that fully takes into account the elastic interactions. For the overdamped model, an exact transient expression for the center-of-mass MSD is obtained from the associated Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process. We show that non-reciprocity enhances the effective diffusion with respect to the classic Rouse model, and that it separates the translational right and left zero modes, so the arithmetic center of mass is not, in general, the dynamically decoupled translational coordinate. It is found that the normalized left zero mode gives a closed expression for the effective diffusivity in terms of the non-reciprocal parameter and the number of beads ($N$) which still scales as $N^{-1}$. Interestingly, the same long-time diffusivity coefficient is found for both, the underdamped linear model and for the less studied finite-natural-length nonlinear model. It is concluded that inertia and finite bond length, modify the transient dynamics of the system, while non-reciprocity determines the long-time diffusion coefficient.

papers.title: Quantum synchronizable codes, polynomial and quasi-polynomial shifts
papers.abstract: Quantum synchronizable codes protect quantum information against Pauli errors and against misalignments of the block boundaries. Almost all known constructions use cyclic codes, because the channel shifts the transmitted block cyclically. We study what happens when the algebraic shift of the code differs from the physical one. When one uses a twisted padding, constacyclic codes synchronize at no cost, and they are the only polycyclic codes with this property for a linear padding. For the other polycyclic codes, we measure the cost of each misaligned position, and we show that the phase damage it causes can be corrected as erasures. Using annihilator duality, we extend the construction to quasi-polycyclic codes, in which the cost is confined to a single block. We prove that the usual quasi-cyclic families have a distance bound that does not grow with the length, and show that quasi-polycyclic codes over repeated-root trinomials overcome it, giving synchronizable codes with larger dimension and distance than the known synchronizable codes of the same length.
authors: Miguel de los Ríos de Antonio

papers.title: Bisect-Index-Choose: A Fast and Exact Algorithm for EV Charging under Minimum Charging Rates
papers.abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations are increasingly operated with an aggregate power limit below the sum of their port ratings, and require scheduling algorithms to divide the available power among the connected EVs. Charging standards permit a current that is either zero or at least a minimum rate, typically 6 A, which makes this allocation problem non-convex. Existing methods either solve a mixed-integer program with a commercial solver, which can be computationally expensive, adds software dependencies, and incurs licensing costs, or apply heuristics without optimality guarantees. This paper proposes Bisect-Index-Choose (BIC), a fast and solver-free scheduling algorithm that computes a globally optimal allocation among EVs under mild assumptions on their utilities. For $n$ EVs, BIC runs in $O(n \log n)$ time when all EVs share one maximum rate and in $O(n^2)$ time for two, times a logarithmic factor in the numerical precision. In tests with up to 1000 EVs, BIC attains global optimality and is up to three orders of magnitude faster than the solver. On real-world charging data, it needs less capacity and delivers more energy than existing heuristics. We implement BIC on a low-cost microcontroller and show that it solves instances with 1000 EVs in less than 90 ms.

papers.title: How Short Is Too Short? Length-Conditional Calibration and Abstention for Detecting AI-Generated Text
papers.abstract: Detectors of AI-generated text are usually tuned and tested on passages of several hundred tokens, yet many real cases are short. We study score-based detection as a function of passage length. We give a closed form for how the false-positive rate of a threshold set on long text changes as length falls, and a formula for the number of tokens a detector needs to reach a target true-positive rate. We calibrate thresholds within length bins with conformal p-values, and we add a bin-level rule that abstains when the detector cannot be informative at that length. On synthetic scores the formulas agree with simulation, and binned calibration holds the false-positive rate at its nominal value at every length. On three zero-shot detectors (log-likelihood, log-rank, Binoculars), three corpora and two open-weight generators, binned calibration gives a mean false-positive rate of 5.0% in every detector-length cell from 10 to 200 tokens, averaged over 300 random document-level resplits. A single threshold set at 200 tokens gives 29% for Binoculars at 10 tokens and about 1% for log-likelihood, as the closed form predicts. No detector reaches an 80% true-positive rate, and the best, Binoculars at 200 tokens, reaches 59%, so the rule abstains in every cell at that floor and releases only the 200-token bins at floors of 0.3 and 0.5.

papers.title: Sharp Constants and Maximizers for Weighted Moser--Trudinger Inequalities on the Heisenberg Group
papers.abstract: This article concerns Moser-Trudinger inequalities on the entire Heisenberg group, focusing on sharp constants, maximizers, and applications to subelliptic PDEs. We address several questions on the existence of maximizers in the singular case $0<β<Q$, where the singular weight yields compactness.
