papers.abstract: We introduce TrackTok, an efficient video tokenization framework that produces object-centric tokens, i.e., tokens that consistently encode the same semantic object across time, even as it moves, deforms, or undergoes partial occlusion. Conventional patch-based or existing holistic tokenizers produce token identities often tied to fixed image locations. In contrast, our approach learns temporally persistent object-centric representations that bind visual features across frames into stable semantic units. This enables substantially more compact, continuous latent video representations, reducing the number of tokens required for downstream generative modeling with state-of-the-art flow models, while preserving the semantic structure needed for high-quality synthesis. Our tokenizer offers a favorable quality-efficiency trade-off. TrackTok achieves comparable class-conditional generative FVD on UCF-101 dataset at 8 times fewer latent tokens and better latency, and outperforms existing 1D tokenization baselines on frame prediction task on Kinetics-600 across low token budgets. These results suggest that object-aligned and temporally persistent tokenization is a promising direction for scalable video generation, where reducing latent token counts is critical for efficient modeling. Our code for this work is available at https://github.com/phamleyennhi/tracktok.

papers.title: Recursive Semantic Divergence for LLM Agent Consistency
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents with tool use can behave inconsistently across independent runs from identical states. They may call different tools, produce contradictory outputs, or follow divergent strategies.This variability compounds over time and undermines deployment reliability. Existing evaluation metrics primarily measure task correctness via completion-based scores and do not capture consistency in agent behavior across executions. Separately, agent behavior is analyzed either at the token level using probability distributions or at the single-response level using semantic clustering, but neither captures how inconsistency propagates across future turns of a trajectory. We introduce Recursive Semantic Divergence (RSD), a trajectory-level consistency metric adapted from bisimulation metrics in reinforcement learning. RSD measures the expected cumulative semantic disagreement between two independent rollouts of the same agent from the same state, using natural language inference to detect logical inconsistency. It is defined recursively over future states and approximated by a neural network trained on independent rollouts. The learned metric estimates future divergence from the current state, providing a consistency score at each turn without requiring the full trajectory to complete. When used as a reward signal for fine-tuning, RSD reduces AUC coefficient of variation (CV) by up to 30.9% on tau2-bench and 50.5% on ToolSandbox. Across Qwen-2.5 and Qwen-3.5 models, RSD reduces AUC CV in seven out of eight model-benchmark settings, while improving the final task progress in all eight settings.

papers.title: Strongly Adaptive Online Learning with Time-Varying Movement Costs
papers.abstract: We study online convex optimization (OCO) with time-varying movement costs, where the learner incurs both a loss and a time-dependent penalty for changing its decisions. While previous work has established dynamic regret guarantees for this setting, obtaining strongly adaptive guarantees that hold simultaneously over arbitrary intervals remains an open challenge. We address this by developing a new algorithm which, for every interval $[a,b]\subseteq[T]$ and arbitrary comparator sequence, achieves a data-dependent regret bound of $ \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \sqrt{(D^2+DP_{[a,b]})\sum_{t \in [a,b]}(\|g_t\|^2+λ_t\|g_t\|)} \right) $, where $D$ is the diameter of the decision domain, $P_{[a,b]}$ is the path length of the comparator sequence over $[a,b]$, $g_t$ is the gradient of the loss, and $λ_t$ is the movement-cost coefficient at round~$t$. Key to our approach is a novel reduction to sleeping experts with movement costs, a previously unexplored variant that is of independent interest. As a result of our development, we further obtain strongly-adaptive dynamic regret guarantees under arbitrary delayed feedback with a refined dependence on interval-restricted cumulative delays. Our approach also naturally extends to OCO with time-varying memory, where we obtain strongly-adaptive guarantees which improve the best-known bounds.

papers.title: Bogoliubov Dynamics and Zitterbewegung in Optical Dirac Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a bosonic Bogoliubov description of Zitterbewegung in time-dependent optical-Dirac systems. Within the optical-Dirac framework, the anomalous pair-creation and pair-annihilation terms of a bosonic Bogoliubov Hamiltonian correspond to couplings between the positive- and negative-frequency sectors, whose coherence underlies the Zitterbewegung response. When the constitutive parameters vary in time, the resulting moving-frame connection generates dynamical interbranch coupling and positive--negative-frequency coherence. Under periodic modulation, this coupling becomes resonant near $Ω\simeq2ω_0$, leading to parametric amplification of the coherence and consequently to an enhanced Zitterbewegung motion.

papers.title: DriveMind: Mind-Evolving Belief Tracking for Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can perceive a traffic scene, reason about it, and propose a driving action within a single model. However, existing MLLM-based drivers reason from scratch at each frame and commit to a single explanation, discarding earlier hypotheses about the scene. When the scene is ambiguous, the agent locks in on the wrong interpretation and acts on it before evidence accumulates. In this paper, we propose DriveMind, an MLLM-based driving framework that keeps several hypotheses about the scene alive at the same time and updates their weights as new frames arrive. Inspired by particle filtering, DriveMind propagates each hypothesis through a VLM, scores it against the current observation, and resamples to maintain diversity. On Bench2Drive, adding belief tracking to the same driving pipeline improves the Driving Score (DS) from 68.50 to 81.37 and the Success Rate (SR) from 41.36% to 54.09%. The largest gains occur on ambiguous scenarios such as unsignalized intersections (+20.0 DS) and oncoming-traffic interactions (+20.5 DS). Beyond the overall metrics, DriveMind also improves fine-grained interactive driving abilities such as merging, emergency braking, and give-way.

papers.title: Swapping Compatible Words
papers.abstract: In 1981 Guibas and Odlyzko showed that the set $A$ of all words of a given length $n$ that avoid a given word $p$, and the set $B$ of all words of length $n$ that avoid a given word $q$, have the same cardinality if and only if $p$ and $q$ have the same self-border lengths. Carrigan et.~ al.~ ask in if there is a ``natural'' bijection between $A$ and $B$. This paper makes partial progress toward answering that question. We provide such a bijection by imposing additional conditions on $p$ and $q$, but we also obtain a stronger conclusion: there is a ``natural'' bijection $Φ$ from the set of all finite words to itself that swaps $p$ and $q$ in each word $Ω$, meaning that $Ω$ has a $p$ or $q$ at a given position iff $Φ(Ω)$ has, repectively, a $q$ or a $p$ at that same position. An algorithm is given for converting $Ω$ into $Φ(Ω)$.

papers.title: Machine-Readable Operator Manuals over the ISO 11783 Network for Offline, Multilingual LLM Assistance
papers.abstract: If agricultural machinery is to support intelligent, offline assistance, then the system must access technical documentation dynamically. In this paper, the Semantic Synchronization of operator manuals over ISO 11783-based CAN buses is analyzed, defined as the process that brings the local knowledge base of a tractor-side assistant into agreement with the operator manual of the connected implement. Data transfer performance was benchmarked using Markdown, JSON, and XML; various open-weight Large Language Models (LLMs) were also evaluated in cross-lingual query tasks. The automatic evaluation of the answers was validated against four human raters. A complete manual was transferred over a physical ISO 11783 network in 31 to 89 s, depending on format and transport settings, which is comparable to the object pool upload that operators already wait for at the first coupling of an implement. Markdown produced the smallest files, while the question-answering performance was comparable across the three formats for most models. With retrieval-augmented generation, locally run models answered most questions on the English manual correctly, with no advantage of the largest model over 7B and 8B models, but performed worse on the five other language editions. Keyword retrieval failed across languages, whereas semantic retrieval provided the cross-lingual capability. The exchange requires only a new parameter group that uses the existing request and transport mechanisms of ISO 11783, which makes it a candidate for standardization. The study is a proof of concept with inference on PC-grade hardware; deployment on embedded agricultural hardware remains future work.

papers.title: Precise Measurement of the Inclusive Cross Sections of Open-Charm Mesons at Energies from 3.80 to 4.95 GeV
papers.abstract: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies from $3.80$ to $4.95~\text{GeV}$, the inclusive production cross sections of open-charm mesons, $σ(e^{+}e^{-}\to D^{0}/D^{+}/D_{s}^{+}+X)$, are measured by tagging a $D^0$, $D^+$, or $D_s^+$ meson, where $X$ denotes any accompanying particles. Open-charm production dominates the total hadronic yield above threshold. Therefore these measurements provide a vital reference for understanding hadron production and for validating global $R$ value results. The results offer crucial inputs for investigating heavier charmonia and exotic states coupled to open-charm final states, while serving as a benchmark for comparison with the sum of measured exclusive channels. This comparison directly evaluates the completeness of current exclusive datasets and clarifies the underlying hadronization mechanisms in the open-charm region.

papers.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact orbifold with corners admits a triangulation compatible with all its corners: for every $k\ge1$, each connected component of the $k$-corners maps onto the image of a subcomplex, and every open simplex lies in the set of points of a single depth. Faces need not be embedded, and the local groups may permute boundary components. The proof turns the boundary hyperplanes of linear charts into mirrors by means of the squaring map, which, unlike the folding $y\mapsto|y|$, is compatible with smooth changes of charts, and then applies the triangulation theorem for orbit spaces of proper Lie groupoids.

papers.title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
papers.abstract: The study of three-vertex subgraph densities has developed along two complementary lines: exact finite realization in large graphs of a given order, and asymptotic approximate realization by sequences of graphs. We bridge these viewpoints for the edge density and the four induced three-vertex subgraph densities. By analyzing local modifications of finite samples from graphons, we show that, for any nonempty subset of these densities, every asymptotically feasible target vector lying a fixed positive distance from the boundary of the corresponding feasible region is realized exactly by a graph of every sufficiently large order, subject only to the natural arithmetic constraints. Thus, in the interior of these feasible regions, asymptotic feasibility implies exact finite realizability up to the unavoidable arithmetic obstructions.

papers.title: Beyond Tokens: NumAnchor for Address-Grounded Numeric Operand Representation in Assembly Language Models
papers.abstract: Assembly language models (ALMs) are becoming important for automated binary analysis, yet their token-level interfaces often obscure numeric-like operands. In two corpora, such operands account for 45.7% and 40.9% of operand occurrences and may denote branch targets, global data, stack slots, constants, or unresolved pointer-derived values. Existing normalization strategies often lose their identities and structural relationships. We present NumAnchor, an input-boundary adapter that represents recoverable numeric-like operands as typed, canonicalized program entities. NumAnchor encodes code, data, and stack context in compact structural side descriptors, preserving entity identity and locality without increasing the host sequence length. These descriptors are fused into input embeddings before the first Transformer layer, while the host architecture, pretraining objectives, and downstream protocols remain unchanged. Probing frozen instruction-level embeddings yields 98.7% hierarchical-location accuracy and AUROC scores of 0.932 and 0.907 for jump and call target alignment, respectively, showing that the encoded structural information remains recoverable. Across multiple ALM families, NumAnchor achieves relative improvements of up to 35.0% in Recall@1 and 31.7% in MRR on 10k-candidate function retrieval, and improves execution-aware type recovery by up to 5.2 F1 points. Ablations show complementary gains from code, data, and stack descriptors with modest overhead.

papers.title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
papers.abstract: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions whose bulk dual is not yet identified, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. We show that the $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and analytically compute their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.

papers.title: LG-Bench: A Graph-Structured Evaluation Benchmark for Life Sciences
papers.abstract: Traditional evaluation benchmarks reduce inherently interconnected scientific knowledge in life sciences into flat lists of questions, disregarding the underlying topological structure of the knowledge. We introduce LG-Bench, the first graph-structured benchmark for life sciences, featuring over 10,000 high-quality multiple-choice questions across medicine, biology, and chemistry. Our approach constructs a weighted evaluation graph using bidirectional matching and semantic similarity algorithms, where nodes represent questions and edge weights capture their semantic relationships. Leveraging this graph topology, we design two novel evaluation metrics. The Global Coherence Score (GCS) measures a model's consistency within semantically related neighborhoods, while Knowledge Balance Score (KBS) analyzes how model errors are distributed across the graph to reveal conceptual blind spots. LG-Bench facilitates fine-grained comparison of LLMs by surfacing differences in conceptual coherence and patterns of knowledge organization across models. Our framework shifts the evaluation paradigm from flat accuracy metrics to structure-aware analysis, offering a new lens for diagnosing and improving LLM performance in the life sciences domain.

papers.title: HP-PnP-Flow: Hybrid Time Scheduling and Projection for Plug-and-Play Image Restoration via Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Image restoration is a fundamental inverse problem that seeks to recover high-quality images from degraded observations. Plug-and-Play (PnP) methods provide a flexible framework for integrating pretrained denoisers into iterative reconstruction, whereas flow matching offers an efficient generative modeling approach based on continuous-time ODE dynamics. Very recently, Martin et al. (ICLR, 2025) developed a PnP-Flow method, which integrates the PnP framework with flow matching through a time-dependent denoiser constructed from a pretrained flow matching model. By incorporating a different time schedule and an additional pixel-space projection operator, this paper proposes a novel efficient PnP-Flow algorithm (HP-PnP-Flow) that enjoys rigorous convergence guarantees under mild assumptions, without imposing restrictive conditions on iterates required by the aforementioned work. Numerical experiments on CelebA and AFHQ-Cat demonstrate that the newly proposed HP-PnP-Flow algorithm significantly outperforms PnP-Flow on several restoration tasks such as denoising, deblurring, super-resolution, random inpainting, and box inpainting. Notably, our algorithm achieves comparable or better reconstruction quality with substantially fewer iterations, reducing the iteration count from $500$ to $100$ for deblurring and super-resolution on AFHQ-Cat.

papers.title: A learner-free swarm approximates the explore-exploit equilibrium allocation: A self-organized attractor in place of reinforcement-learning machinery
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) solves the explore-exploit problem by training a learner on reward; its multi-agent, resource-sharing form has an equilibrium allocation as its optimum -- the ideal-free distribution (IFD), the Nash equilibrium of a congestion game. We show a minimal swarm approximates it with no learner at all. We present a decentralized, learner-free method for this problem: agents explore by heavy-tailed (Levy) flights, recruit neighbours to a discovery through a degree-normalized threshold cascade, and disperse as a patch crowds. The method drives the collective to the shape of the equilibrium allocation (pooled spatial matching slope 1.14, R^2=0.61) with no training, no stored parameters, and no reward in its dynamics; it reaches this as a self-organized attractor and holds it, re-finding it when the resources move -- though it reaches the shape, not the exact equilibrium, and stays measurably exploitable (Nash-gap 1.46). Coupling recruitment to movement causes the allocation: removing it collapses the matching (slope 0.006). Against Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) learners (feedforward, centralized-critic, graph message-passing, and recurrent) trained in the same sensing-limited environment, the method at zero training is the only arm left unbiased w.r.t. the IFD gradient (slope ~1, CI containing 1, vs learners 0.69-0.97, all under-concentrating) and ties the best learner's harvest where resource is clustered, while the learner collects more where resource is scarce (0.33 vs 0.22) and holds a tighter per-capita intake. Learning buys precision and transfer across reward structures, not a better allocation shape. A companion paper develops the mechanism.

papers.title: Global Convergence in Deep Networks via the Second Law of Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: Existing convergence analyses of finite-width overparameterized deep neural networks under standard parameterization often rely on parameters remaining close to their initialization and typically neglect the role of noise, despite empirical evidence that stochasticity can improve optimization and generalization. To bridge this gap, we study $L_2$-regularized continuous-time Langevin dynamics (CLD) with isotropic noise, for training feedforward networks with smooth activations. We introduce a change-of-measure inequality, inspired by the second law of thermodynamics, that enables control of key properties of the training dynamics under the time-evolving parameter distribution. Leveraging a sharpened lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue of the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) at initialization, we show that injected noise helps preserve NTK stability with high probability without confining the weights to a small neighborhood of their initialization. As a result, we derive a non-asymptotic upper bound on the expected training loss. Our analysis yields explicit conditions on width and noise temperature that guarantee convergence to a finite loss floor. Finally, we experimentally show the network Jacobian can change from initialization, departing the commonly analyzed lazy regime.

papers.title: Multi-author style detection with stylistic embeddings
papers.abstract: We investigate the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in multi-author style change detection. Using off-the-shelf LLMs or supervised fine-tuning solely within the target domain fails to yield effective features; for this reason, we propose cross-domain transfer learning with LLM-based embeddings fine-tuned for authorship verification. We fine-tune Mistral-7B embedding model and compare it with DeBERTa, used in the state-of-the-art (SOTA) systems in PAN-25 multi-author writing style analysis challenge. Results show that DeBERTa and Mistral excel in different user-generated text scenarios. We exploit this diversity by combining both embeddings, leading to more effective style change detection.

papers.title: Beyond the Disc--Spheroid Dichotomy at $0.6 < z < 8.0$: Evidence for a Morphological Indeterminacy Regime from JWST
papers.abstract: Galaxy morphology is a fundamental tracer of galaxy assembly, but its characterization becomes increasingly uncertain in the early Universe. We investigate morphological classifications across different methodologies over the redshift range $0.6 < z < 8.0$, using JWST observations of 15,567 galaxies with 6,099 synthetic galaxies from IllustrisTNG. To quantify morphology without relying on visual labels or prescribed light profiles, we use an unsupervised-supervised hybrid machine-learning approach based on the non-parametric MEGG system, which combines the second moment of the light distribution, Entropy, Gini, and Gradient Pattern Analysis. We find that parametric and non-parametric classifications remain broadly consistent at $z < 2.5$, but diverge systematically at higher redshift. We identify this epoch as the Morphological Indeterminacy Regime (MIR), in which classical disc and spheroidal categories no longer provide a unique description of the galaxy population. The fraction of mixed-interpretation galaxies increases with redshift, reaching $F_{\rm MIR} \sim 0.55$ at $z > 2.5$. Cross-domain and projection-invariance tests show that the classifications are stable and insensitive to data set and viewing angle. In the interval $2.5 < z < 8.0$, MIR galaxies occupy an intermediate stellar-mass regime (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.7$), between low-mass discs (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.5$) and massive spheroids (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 10.1$), while irregular systems have stellar-mass distributions similar to those of MIR galaxies. We interpret these results as evidence that morphological indeterminacy is a characteristic feature of galaxy assembly in the early Universe, reflecting a population of dynamically young systems that have not yet settled into the classical Hubble sequence.

papers.title: Reason-guided Human Reward Modeling for Preference-based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies optimized for task rewards may produce behaviors that are efficient but misaligned with human expectations, safety preferences, or intent. This paper presents a reason-guided preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) framework that learns a human reward model from trajectory-level feedback. In addition to preference labels, the framework incorporates reason tags explaining why a behavior is preferred, enabling the learned reward to capture both human choices and their underlying rationale. Compared with preference-only reward learning, the reason-guided formulation provides additional supervision for learning human-aligned rewards and improves the interpretability of the resulting policy. The learned human reward is combined with the environment reward during policy optimization, allowing the agent to improve task performance while producing more interpretable, human- aligned, and preference-sensitive behavior

papers.title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning
papers.abstract: Isogai's case A, a pitch-plunge aerofoil whose elastic axis lies half a chord ahead of the leading edge, has a folded transonic flutter boundary in inviscid flow, with several flutter speeds at one Mach number. We map this boundary and its elastic-axis family with coupled Euler simulations, a Gaussian-process surrogate of the damping trained by batch active learning, and distribution-free split conformal prediction, which bounds the marginal error rate of stability calls. Three failure modes of damping labels are invisible in the residuals, and the half-degree mean incidence left by an impulsive start at $1^\circ$ freestream incidence raises the flutter speed at the dip by 2.8%, more than any numerical setting. With 80 simulations the learned case A boundary labels 63 of 64 independent runs correctly, and at most 1.8% of calibrated calls on held-out runs are wrong. Over Mach number, elastic axis and flutter speed index, 193 simulations show that, for the case A structure about the axis, the inviscid fold exists only for axes more than about 0.4 chord ahead of the leading edge, on two meshes. Chordwise energy budgets, closed three ways, explain both branches. On the lower branch the falling reduced frequency, at unchanged shock phase, raises the shock input and lowers the upstream damping similarly. On the upper branch the shock is pinned at the trailing edge; moving the axis aft brings the flutter-mode pivot towards the section, so the upstream damping falls faster than the residual shock input and the fold closes.

papers.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Decision Rules in an Agent-Based Agro-Ecological Model
papers.abstract: Agent-based models are well-suited for modelling agro-ecological systems for decision-making, yet turning their simulations into actionable insight requires identifying which decisions actually drive the behaviours. In such a context, sensitivity analysis stumbles upon a structural feature of many complex systems: the parameters are not a flat vector but a decision tree in which many parameters appear only when a higher-level choice activates them. Classical global sensitivity analysis presupposes independent inputs over a fixed Cartesian product and is ill-posed on such a branched space and biased by construction. We instead treat the structure of the decisions as a first-class modelling object. Using advanced surrogate modelling techniques, we encode the crop-management itinerary of the high-resolution agro-ecological modelling platform MAELIA as a hierarchical design space featuring both categorical and numerical variables. We propose a novel dedicated method to analyse this kind of hierarchical space, a random-forest-supervised HSIC-ANOVA, which ranks main effects and interactions natively on the tree while placing rarely and always active decisions on an equal footing. We show how, when applied to simulation outputs such as nitrogen leaching, soil organic carbon variation, and yield predictions, it can deliver an interpretable, decision-oriented reading.

papers.title: A quantitative form of the planar Falconer distance theorem
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a uniform lower bound for the length of a planar distance set under a bound on the concentration of mass. For each $0<η<1$, we obtain $b(η)>0$ such that every compact $F\subset\overline{B}(0,1)$ carrying a Borel probability $ν$ with $ν(B(z,r))\le2r^{1+η}$ for all $z\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $0<r\le1$ satisfies $|ΔF|\ge b(η)$. For a compact planar set $E$ of diameter $D>0$ carrying a probability with $μ(B(z,r))\le A(r/D)^{1+\varepsilon}$ for all centers and $0<r\le D$, where $A\ge1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, localization gives $|ΔE|\ge c_{\varepsilon,p}DA^{-p}$ for each fixed $p>1/\varepsilon$, with $c_{\varepsilon,p}>0$ depending only on $\varepsilon$ and $p$. In particular, every compact planar set of Hausdorff dimension greater than one has a distance set of positive length. The proof uses scale-dependent cutoffs to construct approximants to a fixed positive distance measure. The same approximants have summable total-variation errors and summable integrals of the squared modulus of their Fourier transforms over the corresponding dyadic bands. We develop the multiscale method of OpenAI's release on October 6, 2026 in the plane and prove the estimates with constants uniform over the normalized family. This paper is for expository purpose only and is not intended for publication.

papers.title: When the next byte's type is fixed: why entropy patching skips computed values under tight budgets
papers.abstract: The Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) runs a large model once per patch and starts patches where a small model's next-byte entropy is high. Under tight budgets this rule skips computed values, such as the number after "= " in math. On BLT-1B at inference we trace the miss to the cue before a value: when the preceding bytes fix the next byte's type, the patcher's entropy is capped near log2 10 bits, close to a 10% budget's threshold. Entropy then starts a patch at 0% of values after a dollar sign and 19% after "= "; writing "is " instead of "= " raises the 19% to 66%. Version 1's two-byte lookup table, motivated by LZ novelty, acts as a learned detector of cues that tend to precede new values in its fitting text: on the solutions rewritten as prose it covers every value after a dollar sign and none after a plain space, and its margin over entropy falls from +42.1 to -8.9 points, partly because prose gives entropy more starts per value. In BLT-style models trained from scratch (1M-50M parameters, 128-byte context, 3 seeds per rule) and scored by teacher-forced exact match on answer spans, the table beats entropy at 50M by 36.8 points on computed results and 29.6 on final answers, which mostly copy the last computed result. A hand-written marker rule is not distinguishable from the table at 1M and 12M; its 50M control was not run. At 1M and 12M the table ran on a T4 GPU in fp16 and the baselines on an A40 in bf16; at 50M all ran on the A40. End to end, no 1M-50M model solves more than 2 of 100 GSM8K problems. A label-free probe of BLT-1B's patcher finds prose values, mostly after a dollar sign, but costs final answers. In six domains, no rule we tested beat entropy on exact match of whole words and numbers in more than one domain. The positive findings concern tight budgets on cue-formatted text. This version corrects version 1; the work is closed, with no venue intended.

papers.title: A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
papers.abstract: We prove a weak $(1,1)$ estimate for the full Poisson Littlewood--Paley $g$-function on every complete Riemannian manifold without boundary, with an explicit universal constant approximately equal to $2.06970$. The estimate requires no curvature restriction, volume doubling, heat kernel bound, or stochastic completeness. The proof combines a precise Poisson maximal inequality with a good-set energy estimate derived from a convex entropy identity. The constant is sharp for the abstract combination of these two estimates; no optimality is claimed for the operator norm. Local elliptic regularity is used to justify the passage to arbitrary real $L^1$ data. As an application, we obtain weak $(1,1)$ estimates for certain spectral multipliers represented by Poisson time derivatives with coefficients in $L^2((0,\infty),dt/t)$.

papers.title: Orlik-Solomon algebras determine the Tutte polynomials of matroids of rank at most three
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a simple matroid of rank $r$ on the ground set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial, and let $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ denote its Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. We say that $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ determines $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ if, for every simple matroid $\mathcal{N}$, an isomorphism $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})\cong\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{N})$ of $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, without regard to the grading, implies $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)=T_{\mathcal{N}}(x,y)$. Falk conjectured that the Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of every simple matroid of rank three determines its Tutte polynomial. We prove that this holds for every simple matroid of rank at most three, thereby resolving Falk's conjecture.

papers.title: Hierarchical Building-Floo-Room Framework for Privacy-Preserving Autonomous Delivery in Large-Scale Buildings
papers.abstract: Autonomous delivery in large scale buildings requires coordinated planning across multiple spatial levels, including building, floor, and room, while ensuring scheduling efficiency. Existing methods often focus solely on algorithmic development, neglecting integration with physical robotic platforms, and rarely validate performance in real world scenarios. Many approaches also overlook hierarchical building structures and room level privacy constraints, limiting practical applicability. To address these challenges, this paper presents a hierarchical delivery framework based on a Building-Floor-Room abstraction, which decomposes the problem across multiple levels to significantly reduce optimization complexity. We formulate a building aware extension of the capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) that explicitly models inter building and inter floor connectivity, room level access constraints, and privacy sensitive areas, enabling globally feasible and privacy compliant task assignment and routing. Based on this hierarchical model, the framework can evaluate delivery efficiency across different building layouts and optimize depot placement for specific configurations. At the execution level, we introduce a novel hardware design for non interactive, privacy preserving delivery, supported by reachability aware distances and a closed loop mapping, localization, and navigation system, ensuring consistency between planned routes and physical navigation. The proposed framework is validated on a real multi sensor robotic platform, demonstrating reliable multi floor delivery with improved path rationality and overall efficiency.

papers.title: Square-difference factorization: ring structure, torsion splitting, and ideal classes
papers.abstract: We introduce and study commutative rings whose regular ideals, or all ideals, factor into square-difference factor absorbing ideals. We establish permanence under finite products, suitable localizations and quotients, and coefficient descent for monoid algebras. For an SP-domain, the regular factorization property is equivalent to the localization obtained by inverting $2$ being zero or Dedekind; equivalently, the maximal ideals avoiding $2$ are invertible and form a discrete subspace in the inverse topology. Over an arbitrary domain, we characterize unique functorial splitting of localization on all torsion modules by a condition excluding nonzero prime chains across the vanishing set of the localized element. Complementary localizations of one-dimensional Prüfer domains give a decomposition of invertible ideal groups and an exact Picard-group sequence. For an SP-domain whose Picard group has finite exponent $m$, every irreducible element has local valuation at most $m$. We also give regular-ideal criteria for arbitrary idealizations and a complete strong-factorization criterion over von Neumann regular bases. The zero ideal is treated separately throughout, and explicit examples show why unrestricted quotient and localization assertions fail.

papers.title: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails from Classical Soft Theorem for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
papers.abstract: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.

papers.title: Smoothness criterion for Fano orbifolds and bases of Lagrangian fibrations
papers.abstract: We establish a smoothness criterion for Fano varieties with quotient singularities. As an application, we show that if $X\to B$ is a Lagrangian fibration from a compact hyper-Kähler manifold and $B$ has quotient singularities, then $B$ is a projective space.

papers.title: Transverse impulse response of finite and infinite Rayleigh beams
papers.abstract: Here, we study an undamped Rayleigh beam subjected to a concentrated transverse impulse applied at a point far from the boundaries. For a simply supported finite beam struck at its midpoint, using the modal expansion of the impulse response, a short-time asymptotic series for the response of the struck point is derived. The infinite beam impulse response is obtained as a spectral integral in two ways. The spectral integral is evaluated exactly in terms of modified Bessel functions via Laplace transform calculations. The corresponding short- and long-time asymptotics of the exact integral are consistent with the power series developed earlier and the Euler-Bernoulli beam, respectively. Direct numerical evaluation of the integral with a pre-specified error bound and numerical contour integration is also presented for verification. An ad hoc approximation is given which matches the response well for all times. The relationship between finite and infinite beam responses is examined in some detail. There are three consequences of finite length. First, the coefficients in the power series expansion contain components that decay exponentially with increasing length of the beam. Second, a smooth deviation from the infinite beam response is observed, consistent with the greatest group velocity in the beam, wherein a small precursor is detected which is consistent with broader theory. Third, a slope discontinuity is observed, corresponding to the high-frequency limit of group velocity. The full time series plot from modal expansion satisfactorily shows both the arrival and passage of these high frequency components. This paper opens the door to impact studies that are envisaged in future work.

papers.title: Beyond Model Scaling: Rethinking Sequence Construction for Transformer-based Network Intrusion Detection
papers.abstract: Transformer-based network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) have shown strong potential for detecting multi-stage cyberattacks, yet most methods construct input sequences using fixed temporalization schemes rather than treating sequence construction as a systems design decision. In flow-based intrusion detection, timestamp-based windowing often fragments related attack activities while merging unrelated communications, reducing the behavioral context available to transformers. We present a unified pipeline abstraction that decomposes transformer-based NIDS into four design dimensions (traffic representation, temporalization, transformer backbone, and prediction aggregation) and propose session-coherent temporalization, which constructs sequences from communication sessions instead of fixed time windows. Experiments on three complementary intrusion detection datasets show that temporalization is the dominant factor governing transformer performance: session-coherent temporalization more than doubles Macro-F1 over timestamp-based windowing, enabling lightweight transformers to achieve up to 0.95 Macro-F1 at substantially higher inference throughput than pretrained models. We further vary the transformer size from 0.65M to 3.38M parameters and find that larger transformer models provide no measurable accuracy improvement despite substantially higher computational cost, while zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation shows only modest gains under domain shift. These results indicate that preserving communication-session semantics, rather than scaling transformer capacity, is the key to accurate and efficient transformer-based intrusion detection.

papers.title: RELAY: Selective Self-Distillation with Adaptive Hand-off for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning grades a response against many written criteria but collapses them into one reward, which discards the detail the rubric carries and gives no GRPO reward gradient when a group's responses tie. A frozen teacher that reads the rubric as privileged context provides token-level supervision, but we observe an early plateau in the gains over GRPO. RELAY uses advantages and rewards to select positive-advantage and low-scoring zero-advantage rollouts, and monitors the distillation loss to decide when to retire the teacher. Stage 1 combines selective distillation from a frozen teacher with GRPO; a plateau detector then removes the teacher, and Stage 2 continues with GRPO alone. Calibrated on one model-domain pair and reused unchanged in three others, the plateau detector fires between steps 122 and 171. RELAY scores highest in-domain among the compared methods in all four settings, ahead of GRPO on RaR-Medicine by 4.62 points with Qwen3-1.7B and 6.02 with Qwen3-4B. On Qwen3-1.7B/Medicine, removing the teacher from a shared checkpoint outperforms keeping, weakening or refreshing it. Distilling selected rollouts covering about half the response tokens also outperforms distilling all rollouts at a matched average coefficient.

papers.title: CWE-bench: Refocusing Agentic Security from Exploitation to Defense
papers.abstract: Cybersecurity evaluations of AI agents have focused largely on offense, yet a working exploit does not show that an agent can make software safe. An attacker needs to exploit only one vulnerability; a defender must find and fix all of them. We introduce CWE-bench, a benchmark of 250 repository audit-and-repair tasks spanning 185 CWE types and eight languages, grouped into ten weakness classes. We release 100 tasks publicly and keep 150 held out. Agents are given a repository to audit and a description of its threat model, but are not told the weakness, where it occurs, or how many vulnerable sites there are. Each patch must block the exploit while preserving original functionality, as checked by a deterministic programmatic verifier. Verifiers were curated with panels of agentic judges and reviewed by hand, so that they reject incomplete repairs without penalizing correct ones. The best agent reaches 67% pass@1 and 79% pass@4. We further conduct analyses showing that (i) agents with similar pass@1 differ widely in retry gains and cost, and (ii) no single agent is best across languages or weakness classes. As the offensive capabilities of agents improve, CWE-bench provides a broad and rigorous measure of whether their defensive capabilities keep pace.

papers.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
papers.abstract: We establish a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) that integrates three components: (i) a comprehensive, self-contained treatment of its particle-physics foundations and a broad range of model classes; (ii) a systematic, quantitative mapping from microscopic dark-sector physics to structure-formation simulation inputs through explicit expressions and numerical prescriptions; and (iii) the development, implementation, and validation of a broad suite of SIDM algorithms and a dedicated DM decay module in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. Under (i), we detail the particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints of a broad landscape of elementary and composite SIDM models, and present representative viable benchmark models. Under (ii), the mapping specifies cosmological initial conditions, internal-state masses and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. We then apply this mapping to a broad range of SIDM model classes. Under (iii), we implement and validate SIDM algorithms with constant and velocity-dependent cross sections, covering isotropic and anisotropic scattering, multi-state elastic and inelastic reactions, and dissipative processes, alongside a dedicated DM decay module in AREPO-2. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection, thermalization and decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. The results recover analytical predictions and published benchmarks and demonstrate agreement across numerical schemes. Our theory-to-simulation framework serves as a cross-disciplinary reference and a practical bridge between SIDM particle physics and simulations of nonlinear structure formation.

papers.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
papers.abstract: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P. A. Ogarok and A. M. Raigorodskii. In this paper we establish the order of the critical probability for growing r=r(n) and s=s(n): if min{C_r^s r^2, s r^3} = o(n), then the upper and lower bounds differ only by an absolute constant factor. The proof is elementary; only one of the two branches of the growth condition uses the complete nontrivial-intersection theorem of Ahlswede-Khachatrian.

papers.title: An Integrated Framework for Rule-Based Data Editing
papers.abstract: Statistical data editing in official statistics must restore consistency while limiting changes to observed data. Exact minimum-change correction can be computationally demanding. This paper develops a general framework for structured data whose dependencies admit a normalized acyclic routing representation. It connects routing metadata and explicitly specified semantic edits to logical admissibility, violation diagnosis, and correction. Under stated record semantics, the generated Horn theory characterizes admissibility without materializing its deductive closure. Canonical indices preserve the origin of each requirement and identify the variables that can affect a violation. With complete diagnostics and strictly positive weights, a nonnegative violation Hamiltonian vanishes exactly on admissible records within the specified domain. This characterization is independent of the correction procedure and provides both an objective for correction and a certificate: a verified zero-energy output is admissible and globally minimizes violation energy within its permitted candidate domain. Minimum modification cost is formulated separately, with sufficient conditions for an equivalent penalized objective and optimality certificates based on attained lower bounds. A household survey application illustrates the construction, the verification of admissible corrections, and minimum-cost certification for a subset of outputs. The framework supports traceable validation and correction in official statistics, while statistical accuracy of replacement values requires separate assessment.

papers.title: DTA-GT: Direction- and Topology-Aware Graph Transformer for Neural Network Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Architecture attribute predictors reduce the cost of neural architecture search by estimating accuracy or latency from a small set of evaluated candidates. Neural architectures are operation-labeled directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), where edge directions determine computational roles and execution dependencies. Existing graph Transformer predictors incorporate topological and directional information in different ways, but primarily focus on specific mechanisms rather than coordinated encoder-wide modeling of these semantics. We introduce encoder-wide directional consistency, a design principle that coordinates the modeling of directed computational semantics across node initialization, global spectral encoding, pairwise interaction, and feature updates. To implement this principle, we propose DTA-GT, a Direction- and Topology-Aware Graph Transformer that integrates direction- and topology-aware node initialization, magnetic Laplacian spectral encoding, direction-dual structural attention, and a Direction-Sensitive MoE-FFN. Across accuracy and latency prediction on NAS-Bench-101 and NAS-Bench-201, DTA-GT consistently outperforms representative RNN-, CNN-, GNN-, Transformer-, and hybrid predictors under limited-budget settings. Ablations and magnetic spectral controls support the contribution of the direction-aware stages and orientation-sensitive spectral information, while mechanistic diagnostics characterize module behavior. These results support encoder-wide directional consistency as an effective design principle for architecture DAG representation.

papers.title: Well-posedness for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation posed on a classical kinetic phase space. The nonlinear factor $f(1-f)$ appears both in the transport term and in the collision part of the Fokker-Planck operator, accounting for the exclusion principle of fermions. We prove the existence and uniqueness of global solutions without any smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. To construct solutions, we use a vanishing viscosity approximation by adding a Laplacian in the spatial variable. We derive uniform estimates for the regularized problem and obtain compactness in the space of functions of bounded variation $(BV),$ allowing us to pass to the limit as the spatial viscosity vanishes. Since the limiting equation is degenerate with a nonlinear transport, we formulate an appropriate notion of entropy solutions incorporating the kinetic structure of the equation. We prove uniqueness within this class and show that every vanishing-viscosity limit satisfies the entropy formulation. Our result provides a global well-posedness theory beyond the perturbative regime.

papers.title: Perfect discrimination of an orthogonal $2\otimes2$ basis may require collective separable measurements on two copies
papers.abstract: We consider an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2$ with three entangled states and one product state. This basis is not perfectly distinguishable by LOCC or even by separable measurements when a single copy of the unknown state is available. We show that with two copies no adaptive separable protocol, which measures the copies one at a time, distinguishes the basis perfectly. We then show that a collective separable measurement on the two copies does. Whether two copies suffice for LOCC remains open.

papers.title: Discontinuous actions of rational special linear groups on manifolds
papers.abstract: For every $n\geq 1$, we construct continuum-many pairwise non-conjugate actions of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{Q})$ by homeomorphisms on the $n$-sphere. None of these actions extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{R})$. Our construction refines a blow-up procedure of Bowden and Mann, allowing the stabiliser action inside each blown-up disc to be prescribed. We motivate studying these actions and record some related observations.

papers.title: Selection of Marginally Stable Patterns by Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: We study the effect of boundary conditions on the selection of wavenumbers in pattern-forming systems. Prior work established that, for a large class of boundary conditions, equilibria only within a narrow band of wavenumbers are compatible with the boundary. We demonstrate here that for a large class of initial conditions, solutions evolve towards an extremal member of this narrow band of equilibria. In fact, this extremal member is linearly stable, nonlinearly unstable, and the convergence is realized through a series of snapping events at the boundary. We observe this behavior in simulations of the Swift-Hohenberg equation when the pattern forming region is confined to a large spatial interval through a parameter quench. We prove the convergence in a phase-diffusion approximation using comparison principles and astutely chosen subsolutions that mimic the snapping behavior.

papers.title: Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
papers.abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Grünbaum in 2000, and successive work of Bokowski, Grünbaum, Schewe, Pilaud and Cuntz settled every case but $n=23$. We settle this last case by bounding the symmetry of such configurations and classifying the most symmetric ones exactly. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$ the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, explaining why symmetric constructions failed at $n=23$, and the same argument bounds the symmetry of $(n_5)$ configurations for primes $n\not\equiv1\pmod5$. Reducing the Klein four-group case to 4021 bilinear polynomial systems and solving all of them exactly with Gröbner bases, we show that exactly two $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound up to projective equivalence and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar; the first has integer coordinates and the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$ but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. The same classification recovers Cuntz's $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$. Among self-polar $(23_4)$ configurations with a single involution we find $50$ more, defined over number fields of degree at most $7$. Four of them deform in one-parameter families, and computing three of these exactly, one birational to the modular curve $X_1(11)$, we prove that there are infinitely many geometric $(23_4)$ configurations, among them infinitely many with rational coordinates that are self-polar and have no projective symmetry.

papers.title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes from the spectral edge of DSSYK and supersymmetric extensions
papers.abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same $q$-deformed volumes can also be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call ``irrelevant'' contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how $q$-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

papers.title: SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices
papers.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) jointly predict robot actions and future observations, but their video diffusion backbones are costly for edge deployment. We introduce SmolWAM, a compact latent WAM derived from the 2B-parameter Cosmos Policy using single-frame encoding, cached text features with preserved attention sinks, depth pruning, and token compaction. With 12 of 28 transformer blocks and 1,008 tokens, SmolWAM predicts actions and future latents in one rectified-flow step. After 3.6 A100 GPU-hours of training, it achieves 95.5% success over 400 LIBERO episodes at 57ms, 2.3TFLOP, and 2.4GiB per 16-action chunk on an A100: 11x lower latency and 3.2x lower memory than the five-step teacher. Its world head predicts scene motion; joint training improves success by 6.2 percentage points over an action-only ablation.

papers.title: NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval
papers.abstract: Memory retrieval aims to identify evidence from stored records to answer a query. Stored records with different factual details may share topics, entities, or events. Such shared contents would make records without the required evidence more likely to receive high similarity scores and outrank the correct evidence. In this paper, we use the information shared by these records to construct local references for query-memory matching. We propose NEighborhood-Aware Residuals (NEAR), a training-free framework that uses these references to construct residual representations that complement the original embeddings. Specifically, each memory derives a reference direction from its neighbors, and each query obtains its reference from a precomputed table. Using these references, NEAR constructs projection residuals for both queries and memories. These residuals are combined with the original embeddings for a single approximate nearest-neighbor search over a fixed memory index. Experiments on eight long-context retrieval benchmarks show consistent improvements across nine embedding models. Downstream evaluations show that NEAR improves question-answering performance.

papers.title: Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence
papers.abstract: Memory-augmented assistants retrieve evidence from stored conversations and documents to answer queries. Most embedding-based retrievers compare single-vector representations of queries and memories, even when relevance depends on a small part of the content. Such local evidence can be matched to queries using the contextual token representations already computed by the same embedding models. Our method uses sparse token matching to improve retrieval without additional training. Each query token retrieves a small set of matching tokens across candidate memories. The matching scores are aggregated for each memory and combined with whole-memory similarity to rank memories. An optional low-rank query adapter can be trained with supervision while keeping the encoder and stored memory representations fixed. Our method improves retrieval across eight benchmarks and multiple model families without additional training. Query adaptation further increases the gains to 13.3 and 14.3 percentage points in average Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on Qwen3-Embedding-4B. These retrieval gains translate into higher question-answering accuracy on long-term memory benchmarks.

papers.title: MLP-Initialized Reinforcement Learning for Exit Timing in SPX Short-Straddle Portfolios
papers.abstract: This paper studies exit timing for SPX short-straddle portfolios using a two-stage supervised and reinforcement-learning framework. Historical episodes first generate ex-post optimal hold/exit labels for training a multilayer perceptron (MLP) using only contemporaneously available state variables at deployment. The trained MLP then initializes reinforcement-learning actors that are fine-tuned with a risk-aware trading reward. Out-of-sample evaluation over 2024-2026 shows that the supervised MLP substantially outperforms passive holding and representative fixed-time and profit-and-loss-based exit rules. Across seven independent seeds, MLP-initialized Actor-Critic averages 37.54% cumulative return and a Sharpe ratio of 1.705, compared with 35.01% and 1.651 for the supervised MLP. Actor-Critic trained from scratch averages only 0.18% return. These findings show that oracle-guided supervised learning provides a stable foundation for reward-based policy fine-tuning in a sparse and path-dependent option-exit problem.

papers.title: Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
papers.abstract: We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N\geq4$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta--Iovita--Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard--Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao--Liu. When $p$ has a unique prime of $F$ above it, we remove this hypothesis and obtain unconditional properness, by establishing base-change compatibility for spaces of overconvergent Hilbert modular forms and analyzing the associated spectral variety over certain closed subspaces of the weight space.

papers.title: BayesJudge: Uncertainty-Aware Bayesian Meta-Evaluation of Human and LLM Judgments
papers.abstract: AI evaluation pipelines often produce conflicting judgments rather than clean labels. Yet existing methods largely collapse disagreement into a single hard label. As a result, item ambiguity, rater biases, and the position preferences of LLM judges are erased together: evaluation outcomes appear deterministic while concealing the underlying uncertainty, and may even systematically favor one response. This conflict is especially acute in pairwise LLM evaluation. We propose \textbf{BayesJudge}, an online Bayesian meta-evaluation layer for conflicting human-LLM judgment streams. BayesJudge treats the latent preference of each item as a latent variable and jointly models two sources of evaluator bias: rater-specific confusion matrices for human annotation bias, and an explicit order parameter for the position preference of LLM judges, thereby separating response quality from evaluator bias. We derive an exact online posterior recursion and adopt a scalable Rao-Blackwellized assumed-density sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) approximation for streaming inference. Consequently, each comparison yields not a single hard label but a posterior distribution over each response winning (as well as a tie or ambiguity state), together with posterior estimates of the bias parameters, making evaluation uncertainty explicit and quantifiable. On synthetic data, BayesJudge accurately recovers human annotation biases and LLM position biases online, and strictly outperforms variants that freeze either bias channel in held-out predictive log-likelihood. On the real-world SummEval dataset, BayesJudge detects systematic order effects in LLM judgments, distinguishes the behavioral signatures of experts and crowdworkers without rater metadata, and yields posterior uncertainty that reflects genuine human disagreement. Our code is available at https://github.com/Killerofthecard/BayesJudge.git

papers.title: Self-Supervised Keyframe Discovery for Horizon-Invariant Behavior Cloning
papers.abstract: Behavior cloning (BC) in non-Markovian environments is a challenging problem because policies have to reason over contextual information over long horizons. Existing policy architectures rely on recurrent or attention-based mechanisms to capture long-term dependencies. However, recurrent models suffer from hidden-state collapse and gradient instability under backpropagation through time while attention-based models are fundamentally limited by context length. To address these issues, we propose Keyframe Mnemonics, a novel self-supervised method that $\textit{discovers}$ a set of information-critical observations ($\textit{mnemonics}$) by learning an objective from randomly sampled past observations and using it as a reward for keyframe selection. We then train a BC policy that conditions on the discovered keyframes to model the action distribution. Under the simplicity bias assumption, our formulation provides context retention guarantees over an infinite horizon, while maintaining a small set of decision-relevant keyframes in the policy's working memory. We evaluate our method on synthetic memory domains, where mnemonic-conditioned BC policies achieve $100$% success rates (SR) and generalize to horizons orders of magnitude beyond training without performance degradation. Moreover, we evaluate on a memory-intensive robot manipulation benchmark, achieving a $13.9$% average absolute SR improvement over the strongest baseline across $23$ tasks. Finally, we demonstrate generalization with $80$% SR at $20\times$ longer time horizons on a real robot. Code and videos available at https://keyframe-mnemonics.github.io.

papers.title: Distilling Graph Geometry: Knowledge Gap from GNNs to MLPs
papers.abstract: GNN-to-MLP distillation aims to retain the predictive accuracy of a message-passing teacher while deploying a graph-free MLP at inference. Existing methods mainly transfer node-wise predictions or use confidence-based reweighting, but they do not specify where the student should preserve the teacher's graph-induced geometry. We show that this omission leads to two spectral failure modes in the student's representation space. On sparse graphs, the student suffers from spectral underfit, missing high-energy teacher directions induced by aggregation. On dense graphs, it suffers from spectral overfit, retaining spurious directions that the teacher has collapsed through aggregation. Motivated by an energy-weighted teacher-student alignment objective, we propose Graph Geometry-aware MLP (G^2MLP), a training-time distillation framework guided by Ollivier-Ricci curvature. Curvature acts as a local proxy for allocating supervision between prediction-level and representation-level alignment. The deployed model is a standard MLP with no graph access at inference. Across node-classification benchmarks, G^2MLP improves over graph-free distillation baselines in most settings, reduces the teacher-student rank gap in both regimes, and transfers to Graph Transformer teachers and link prediction.

papers.title: Pauli Decomposition by Character Theory: A Memory-Bounded Algorithm for Qubits and Qudits
papers.abstract: Pauli decomposition of an $n$-qubit operator is expensive if each of the $4^n$ Pauli strings is treated as an unstructured object. Labeling those strings by the configuration space $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ makes them displacement operators $X^{\otimes x}Z^{\otimes z}$ on the computational space: shifts by~$x$ and multiplications by characters $Z^{\otimes z}$ in the computational basis. That labeling organizes the operator into $2^n$ fibers of length $2^n$, one per shift~$x$, each collecting the computational-basis amplitudes that hop by~$x$. Expanding each fiber function in the character basis of $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^n$ --- a length-$2^n$ Walsh--Hadamard transform --- recovers the Pauli coefficients at total cost $O(n\cdot4^n)$. The same fiber / shift--character picture extends to $(\mathbb{Z}_p)^n$ (Heisenberg--Weyl qudits). \texttt{paulikit} is a memory-bounded realization for qubits: for matrix-sparse inputs, peak memory need not densify to a full $2^n\times2^n$ operator. Performance is checked on a stated low-end GNU/Linux platform for a coupled-oscillator sweep beyond a billion Pauli terms.

papers.title: Irreducibility of Verma modules for symmetrizable Kac-Moody superalgebras
papers.abstract: We establish a criterion for the irreducibility of Verma modules over symmetrizable Kac--Moody superalgebras. Our main tool is the Weyl-Kac denominator identity.

papers.title: Sub-Voxel Displacement and Ipsilateral Territory Decoupling for 3D Bilateral Coronary Artery Tree Reconstruction in Cardiac CT Angiography
papers.abstract: Reconstructing topologically complete, sub-voxel-accurate 3D bilateral coronary artery trees from cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) requires simultaneously recovering continuous centerline trajectories and separating dense left/right coronary territories without cross-ostial collisions. We present a five-stage tubular drift and ipsilateral territory decoupling framework (M1-M5). Stage M1 pairs a 398,843-parameter multi-scale 3D pyramid encoder with a four-head tubular field network predicting vesselness probability, signed tubular boundary distance, unit tangent vectors, and continuous 3D centripetal displacement vectors. Stage M2 introduces recall-preserving multi-task optimization with 7-group AdamW parameter decoupling, L2-SP backbone regularization, and per-step anchor shrinkage. Stage M3 calibrates cylindrical Valsalva-sinotubular-junction wall coordinates and native-resolution orifice contact expectations for robust left and right ostial rooting. Stage M4 constructs a scalar-potential-weighted minimum-cost arborescence followed by normal-plane cross-sectional pullback and centripetal trajectory pruning. Stage M5 enforces coverage-guarded ipsilateral-field-coupled bilateral collision reduction and subtree handover. Across a 14-case held-out development cohort (Dev-14, 17-arm forward incremental build and 9-arm leave-one-out ablation) and an independent 50-case out-of-sample evaluation cohort (OOS-50) benchmarked against seven external architectures (nnU-Net, 3D UX-Net, Swin-UNETR, MedNeXt, CS2-Net, clDice-UNet, and Point-UNet), M1-M5 reduces bilateral chamfer distance on Dev-14 from 3.4381 mm to 2.2759 mm and achieves 2.7671 mm on OOS-50 with 7.11% bilateral collision rate and 79.7% distal branch completeness.

papers.title: Path-Space Optimal Transport with Interactions: Kinetic Equations and Eikonal Structure
papers.abstract: We study a dynamical optimal transport problem on path-space with kinetic cost and nonlocal interaction. For a Gaussian interaction kernel, cyclical monotonicity and the regularity of the effective endpoint cost yield a conservative vector field associated with the initial momentum of the optimal trajectories. Separately, the Gaussian interaction potential $W_{π_0}$ satisfies a uniform gradient estimate and, under a quantitative condition on the interaction strength, is a classical and hence viscosity subsolution of an eikonal equation. We also derive the Euler--Lagrange dynamics directly from path-space optimality by means of endpoint-preserving perturbations of the optimal path measure. The associated phase-space marginals satisfy a measure-valued Liouville-type, or nonlocal kinetic, equation driven by the smooth Gaussian self-consistent force. Conversely, a superposition principle lifts suitable measure-valued solutions of the phase-space continuity equation to measures on phase-space trajectories. Thus path-space optimal transport provides a variational connection between endpoint geometry, eikonal behavior of the Gaussian interaction potential, and kinetic mean-field dynamics.

papers.title: Poisson-GENERIC Neural Operators: Exact Metriplectic Structure in Function Space via Casimir Entropies
papers.abstract: Existing thermodynamically consistent neural operators enforce GENERIC degeneracy by projecting the reversible operator, introducing state dependence without guaranteeing Jacobi. We instead use a compatible Lie--Poisson pencil $L=αD+λ(uD+Du)$ for nonlinear transport and constant Poisson multipliers otherwise. Augmenting the observed field $u$ with a latent entropy density $s$ makes $S=\int s$ a Casimir, so $L\,δS/δz=0$ without projection. The energy combines a fixed mechanical quadratic, a learned gauge-free potential, and a convex internal energy; the friction operator $M=AA^\top$ enforces $M\,δE/δz=0$ pointwise and supports diffusion and damping without a separate transport generator. Skewness, positivity, and both degeneracies hold for any parameters; the continuum pencil satisfies Jacobi, verified on the alias-free band; the closed-form heat and damped-wave friction operators are representable; physical energy is bounded under coercivity assumptions; and a discrete-gradient integrator preserves both laws in discrete time. On four PDEs in 1D and 2D with three backbones (FNO, Transolver, CNO), at equal optimizer steps the model wins 62/72 seed-level comparisons against unconstrained baselines, recovers the exact transport and wave symbols, matches heat and Burgers dissipation within 12\%, and dissipates nothing on advection; at equal wall-clock the unconstrained FNO is the more accurate ten-frame surrogate. What the structure gives at any budget is the energy balance: over a hundred frames, in and out of distribution, the model never raises the physical energy and conserves it where dissipation vanishes, whereas the unconstrained FNO loses a quarter of a conserved energy off distribution and projected GENERIC-FNO creates energy on most frames. Late-time under-damping on heat and explicit-integrator divergence on the wave are reported as limits.

papers.title: On pointwise convergence of singular integrals of Christ-Journé type
papers.abstract: The primary objective of this paper is to establish the pointwise almost everywhere convergence of the singular integrals of Christ-Journé type. To this end, we prove the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for the corresponding maximal operator defined as \[ T^*[a] f(x):= \sup_{r>0}\left|\int_{|x-y| > r} K(x-y) \int_0^1 a(tx + (1-t)y)\, dt f(y)\, dy\right|, \] where $K$ is a Calderón--Zygmund kernel and $a\in L^\infty$. This result resolves a problem posed by Seeger (Rev. Mat. Iberoam., 2014).

papers.title: The Right Wing of the SABR Smile with an Absorbing Boundary: Resolution of Conjectures of Henry-Labordère
papers.abstract: We determine the fixed-maturity right tail of the SABR model with $β\in(0,1)$ absorbed at zero, for every correlation $ρ$: the probability $P(k)$ that the forward ends above $f_0e^k$ satisfies $-k^{-2}\ln P(k)\to(1-β)^2/(2ν^2T(1-(ρ\wedge0)^2))$. The implied volatility therefore tends to $ν\sqrt{1-(ρ\wedge0)^2}/(1-β)$. Henry-Labordère's conjectured limit $ν/(1-β)$, which Hagan's leading-order formula also gives, holds for $ρ\ge0$ and fails for $ρ<0$, where survival keeps the noise orthogonal to volatility above a moving square-root barrier. The Gaussian estimate behind his second conjecture does not hold for $ρ<0$; the rate is instead given by the intrinsic distance within the survival domain.

papers.title: On wall-crossing invariant combinations of Welschinger numbers for rational surfaces with a conic bundle
papers.abstract: We refine the real enumerative invariants insensitive to changes in the real structure introduced in our previous paper on del Pezzo surfaces, and extend these refined invariants to arbitrary rational surfaces. The construction involves a choice of an auxiliary conic bundle together with a Pin-structure. We prove that the resulting invariants are independent of these auxiliary choices and establish recursive relations for their computation.

papers.title: Fixed-Capacity Causal Models with Parallel Recovery for GPU Lossless Compression
papers.abstract: GPU lossless compression requires both compact complete frames and fast checked recovery. We evaluate fixed-capacity causal byte-bank representations under a shared 512-row probability budget, select a single representation via a pre-payload complete-cost proxy charging both empirical cross-entropy and compressed model tables, and align two rANS states per 8\,KiB chunk with the causal byte banks. Independent byte banks decode concurrently, whereas intra-word conditional banks decode in two ordered phases. On ten structured imaging and electrophysiology inputs, split-bank execution lowers aggregate median encode-plus-recovery time by 13.10\% for 0.18\% additional frame bytes, and reduces complete encoding cost by 44.16\% relative to a matched native-CPU model control while supporting a standalone CUDA-free CPU receiver. In a twelve-configuration GPU comparison, Split GPX produces 5.75\% and 7.11\% smaller complete frames than Zigshuffle + nvCOMP Zstd at 35.14\% and 19.03\% lower paired cost for 64\,KiB and 8\,KiB requests. For multi-channel sample-interleaved waveforms, extending causal differencing with zero-oracle GPU stride screening (strided-residual) reduces holdout 12-lead PTB Diagnostic ECG frames by 49.89\% (from 71.47\% to 35.81\% of raw bytes, 37.20\% smaller than Zigshuffle + Zstd-1 and 46.67\% smaller than OpenZL-9) while preserving byte parity across all single-stream benchmarks.

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Order-Two Clifford Electric-Magnetic Duality
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic duality in the toric code has order two at the level of anyon types and acts as a Hadamard-type logical transformation on the encoded quantum information. Here, we ask whether it can likewise be realized microscopically as an order-two Clifford operation. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ toric code, we prove that any locality-preserving Clifford realization of electric-magnetic exchange cannot have order two. Our proof is fully general and requires neither translation symmetry with restricted families of system sizes nor a fixed pairing between vertex and plaquette stabilizers.
